author: Philip Saulescu
review_text: The food was great, the ingredients were very good but be careful with the spice levels. We tried the second spice level and it was a bit too spicy for us, even though we consider ourselves spicy eaters. I gave this place 4 stars not because of the food, but because of the waiting time. We stayed in line around 15-20 minutes to order, and then they told us that the food will be ready in 35 mins. We actually ate 1h after we ordered because they were late. Other than that this place is worth visiting for the great food.

author: Evana Mannan
review_text: MARK DOES NOT PLAY!!!! The spice levels are no joke 😭 I love spicy and always add lots of spice, but Mark is on another level. I tried the signature level 4 and I immediately got hiccups from how spicy it was. However, the flavor was absolutely delicious! I got the beef with spice level four and my husband got the wagyu with spice level three. If you get any level more than three then I suggest to get two or more eggs to balance it out. All in all a great experience and I recommend!

author: Christopher U
review_text:
Had to find time to try Phed Mark’s while in Bangkok since I’ve been watching Mark Wiens for years now and want to try his Pad Kra Pao.

We had our dinner coming back from our Safari World.  Luckily no lines so it took only 10 mins for our 10 orders.

Simple and small menu but it’s full/packed of deliciousness.  Eight veg/meat/seafood options that includes rice and fried duck egg.

Enjoyed our Sour Pork (Spicy/Recommended) & Beef (Non-spicy) Phad Kra Pao. Meats were full of umami flavors and love the perfectly fried duck egg.

Highly recommended!

author: onJuice Nguyen
review_text:
When you get there, you need to order first then wait outside for your number to be called. They let us know that it will be around 20 mins and this was around 12:30pm which wasn’t too bad.

So basically they only serve one type of dish, Pad Kra Pao. Which is just duck egg on top of rice and mince meat with chilli. I had the chicken with spicy level 3 (recommended) with 2 duck yolks. I like enjoy chilli and handle quite abit before it gets too spicy. I thought the level 3 was just beginning of the spicy level and wasn’t that hot that people are claiming it to be. But it might be the recommended option as the spice level doesn’t overpower the flavours. But if you love your spice, I recommend 4 or 5.

Overall, nothing special. Didn’t even end up finishing the dish. Flavours didn’t pop. Dish felt very dry and not that enjoyable to finish. Must be the hype.

author: Thomas
review_text:
Phed Mark is exactly the kind of place you want to discover in Bangkok: a small spot with big flavor. The Pad Krapao was intense, full of aroma, and properly spicy, exactly how it should be. The crispy fried egg with the creamy yolk on top was the perfect finishing touch.

The plate was completely empty at the end. No surprise, the dish was simply too good.

The place itself is small and straightforward, but that’s part of its charm. The awards on the wall make it obvious why this spot is so popular: they focus on the food, and the food delivers.

If you’re looking for real, no-nonsense Pad Krapao in Bangkok, this is the place to go.

Not Spicy, Not Eating ! :)

author: Daryl Lee
review_text:
So yummy! Tried the pork and the beef. Both were good, but I think the pork is better. The eggs were fried to perfection. We were saving our stomachs for more food later, but definitely order more than one egg if you have the space for it!

Overall, I will definitely be back! Easily something I would crave every now and then.

author: Samantha Pyq
review_text:
If you like fried eggs with runny yolk, you will love this! Get more eggs, you wont regret. More expensive but portion is bigger than usual Thai portion. I will say the price is reasonable.

Chicken was thinly sliced, lacked flavour, but was great after adding fish sauce.
Pork was fantastic, bits of fat adding flavour.
Beef was dry, get the pork instead.

Level 2 seating is much cooler, because level 1 main door is always open for the ordering queue.

author: Curtis Bull
review_text:
The best Pad Kra Pao I’ve had, ever.

The level 4 spicy was a decent level of spice, not unmanageable in the slightest, next time I’ll try 5. It’s not a gimmicky “blow your socks off spice” that some YouTuber owned restaurants do.

This place actually feels like they’re trying to serve you really amazing food without the frills of it being owned obviously by Mark Wiens.

It’s genuinely great food at good prices, and the portion sizes are huge!

All in all, this place deserves its 5/5 rating, truly. Can’t wait to go back

author: Amisha Ajay
review_text:
I’d heard so much about how good Mark Wiens’ restaurant was, and I can say it absolutely lived up to the hype!

I had the Thai basil chicken rice, spice level 3 (it goes up to 5), and it was so good. I’d 101% recommend it to anyone who loves spicy food 🔥 The flavour of the basil was hitting just right. I needed a Coke Zero to balance out that kick of spice haha, but you might not.

The place itself is small and there was a bit of a queue when I visited, but the service was quick and efficient. I’m definitely coming back here for more next time I’m in town.

author: Loraine R.
review_text:
Like Mark himself would say: ‘Wow!’
I ordered the chicken and beef, level 4 spicy and it was SPICY 🥵but really good! I preferred the chicken over the beef and they either forgot to bring half of the order or the beef took longer than the chicken to prepare, so had to ask where the rest of the order was. If you’re a party of multiple people, it would be nice to receive your order in 1 go.
Other than that, definitely recommend!

author: Zhengmei Pongpun
review_text:
Speaking as a Thai person, the basil stir-fry I had was just very ordinary nothing impressive and definitely not worth waiting an entire hour for. If I could turn back time, I wouldn’t have come to eat here; it felt like such a waste of my life. I decided to eat because the staff told me the wait would be only 40 minutes. At first, I wasn’t going to eat here, but then they said it would be about 35 minutes. In reality, though, I ended up waiting for an hour. That’s completely different from what they told me. And I couldn’t just leave because I had already paid, so I had to wait. You can see the time I paid on the bill and the time I got food on my phone

When I finally got my food and took the first bite, it was just… meh. Not amazing, not impressive, nothing memorable at all. So I guess this is going to be the first time in my last time here.

author: Tazio Lai
review_text:
Passed by many times and finally made it in today!

Located very near the BTS Ekkamai station this place generally has a big line during meal times, but we made it in off peak so no wait whatsoever!

Ordered the standard chicken version & of course with the fried duck eggs and it all came out quick, hot and delicious!

Food taste, quality and quantity for the price and location are an absolute deal and great meal fix in a jam!

They’ve got the merchandise game also locked down with stickers, caps, and even a football (soccer) displayed!

Definitely worth a visit , just make sure you’re not too hungry if you go during peak hours as the wait might get you due to popularity!

author: Adnan Chowdhury
review_text:
I was staying at an air bnb close by and passed this place once. It was busy with grab drivers so I could say it was popular. I ordered the chicken and beef jokes. I am not into spicy so I said no spicy. But after eating the food I felt it was too bland. So add ask for little spice. The food was very good. I liked the chicken more than the beef. Not a fan of duck egg though so I didn’t eat it.

Service is fast and you have to do take out.

author: ben (Boboramen)
review_text:
Q to order - after order wait outside for your table estimate 30min waiting (Thursday afternoon around 2pm)

Service was easy they will ask on your prefer spicy level
- 3 and above spicy
- 2 and below average spicy

For me spicy level 3 just nice, must order double duck egg original come with 1 add on 1 more. Those egg really amazed me with the crispy edge and creamy yoke

Recommended to try, for trying you can order 1 plate for sharing.

I notice also some customer order 1 plate each and only finish half or even less I suspect due to the heat.

Dear people, please do not waste food! maybe you don’t care about the price or it’s not expensive to you but wasting food is really not cool.

author: thaichrislife
review_text: Highly recommended with fried squid! If you can eat spicy a little bit, level 4 is a best choice. Overall the environment is rush and small with little bit seats, food is tasty.

author: Shantanu Mishra
review_text:
I got the vegetarian* spice level 5 - it wasn't nearly as spicy as I thought it would be but I did wish I had water because of the chillies. The dish itself wasn't spicy - it was the red chillies in it that were spicy.

I wouldn't say it's the most delicious food I've had in Thailand but definitely the spiciest, yet.

Got there at 1pm (Thursday) and was seated upstairs right after ordering. Got my food in about 10 minutes. Staff was really nice.

Happy to try it once, wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to have it again.

*Not sure if it's actually "vegetarian" since I think they use fish sauce in the food but I didn't ask because I didn't want to find out. Check before you order.

author: Torontoian_007
review_text:
Wanted to visit since we watched from YouTube in Canada 🇨🇦. Saved the address n here we are.
Medium spicy for Pad Kapong 😋.
Mark Wien's (Foody YouTube) restaurant and something to remember.
Self serv and pretty small place. We arrived there just b4 it's opened and we have a place to sit n enjoy the food.

author: Matthew Lee
review_text:
Came here on a weekend lunchtime.  Was almost close to noon and initially was worried I left late there would be a long queue for lunch but thankfully it wasn't crowded.
There was no queue outside so I managed to enter into the shop. To my surprise 5 minutes later there was already a long queue and the queue stretched outside. Some people even after ordering had to wait outside for a seat.
I admit I don't have a high threshold for spicy food, I wanted to order non spicy but decided to give very less spicy a try.
After ordering was very quick to get a seat and the food was also served quite fast. The people around me seemed to not really enjoy it because they said it was too spicy to finish the whole plate. Some ate only a quarter or half of it.
I was quite afraid but it wasn't that bad for me. I managed to clear the whole plate without much difficulty. Though I didn't order any drinks at first I had to get some water because once you get irritated by the spiciness it's kinda hard to continue as you will keep coughing so had to stop the irritation by drinking.
Manageable but also sweated a bit. Thought I was weak but seemed there were people who were weaker than me and wanted to try it.
Maybe will visit again next time and try the next level.
I recommend bringing cash as I see they don't accept cards.
Worth giving a try to judge for yourself.

author: 李志東
review_text:
This was my second visit to the restaurant to try their spicy minced pork rice, as my first experience was delightful—the dish was served piping hot, and the rice was equally warm. However, during this visit, I encountered some issues. After a 20-minute wait, which I understand is reasonable given the crowd, I was disappointed to find that both the rice and the minced pork were lukewarm. It seemed as though they had prepared too many plates at once, resulting in them cooling down before serving.

I believe there is room for improvement in the heating process. Additionally, I found the restaurant's layout to be quite cramped, and there was no clear queue management system in place. While I recognize this is a popular spot, effective management is essential to enhance the dining experience.

I sincerely hope that my next visit will result in a hot and satisfying meal, as the flavors are genuinely worth returning for.

author: Reeve
review_text:
This food was absolutely delicious!
The flavors were perfectly balanced, and the ingredients tasted incredibly fresh. Egg was perfectly cooked. Prepare for traffic within the area, extra patience while waiting your seat and food! Price little bit higher than the usual amount. But its worth it.

author: Joseph Mercurio
review_text: Saturday night, fabulous street vibe, the atmosphere was excellent, restaurant was packed with an endless queue that kept moving. Staff fantastic people efficient rushed off their feet busy busy yet still friendly and personable. We were so lucky had to wait maybe 10 min after we sat down the line was all the way around the restaurant. The crispy pork was outstanding light fluffy soft tender meat with a firm tasty crispy crust, near perfection. The fish soup was delicious hot pepper and very fishy, no bones in the flesh big tick. The greens had spicy sweet sauce which was extremely moorish. All in this was an excellent experience both the restaurant, the staff and the general area. Buzzing and vibrant. If you can you definitely should.

author: derek neo
review_text: This restaurant is a hotspot at the night market! Queue's worth it - moves fast despite being popular. They kept the outdoor tables clean, and staff were on top of things, serving efficiently amidst the crowd. Food's great - roast pork was crispy, big chunks!, tomyum noodle was flavorful (a tad salty for me, but ppl loved it). Good vibes all round! Would definitely go back for more!

author: phAna dr
review_text: It’s a restaurant in Buntadthong every time I walked passed it I wonder why it is always packed with tourists and I always thought that it was expensive. But this time I went in and tried it and the food was amazing compared to other restaurants nearby. The price was reasonable, the service was great, everyone was so friendly, the food came out very quick too. I can confidently say that this is the best restaurant in Bantadthong that I’ve tried.

author: Victor Ng
review_text:
This place is popular because of social media hype. Taste wise fail. It serves a wide variety of dishes but ends up being a jack of all trades, master of none.

Tom yum seafood noodles 🫲
Very oily and sour. Good Tom yum should have the right balance of sweet, sour and salty.

Instant fried noodles 🫲
Full of MSG.

Crab fried rice 👎
Tasteless and poor quality rice.

Suki 👎
Tasteless.

author: P S
review_text: I walk by this restaurant frequently, and as a Thai person, I always wonder why it's so crowded. So, I decided to give it a try. Their recommended dish was Tom Yum Noodles, which comes in one size—a big bowl that's enough for 2-3 people. It was quite delicious, as a good Tom Yum should be, and they added seafood and crispy pork, which were also very tasty. Overall, it was a delicious meal, though a bit hot since the restaurant only has outdoor seating.

author: Ong
review_text:
Only ordered the mama noodle and roast pork as thats what I came specifically for.

Verdict: J Os miles better. Here in Baan Kook Kai the noodles taste like I could make myself and the soup base is more sour while the other is like more tasty and flavourful. Here the roast pork is also drier and hard.

The servers work with a mind of their own...I can order additional drinks with 2 different server and both can miss and never came.

If you have never tried the other one, this will probably work ok. 没比较没伤害。

author: Jonas Ng
review_text: The food here is generally good and affordable! Feels like a good local fan fare and it’s delicious. Atmosphere may not be the best as it is outdoors with stool seating.

author: Eugene Khoo
review_text: Recommended by a friend to come here instead of the Michelin shop at nearby, not regretting the decision. The mama tomyam pack a punch and balance of spicy & sour, remember to tell the shop less spicy if you can't handle the heat. Watch out as the portion of the mama tomyam already have tons of ingredients such as roast pork, squid, pork minced meat, pork ball and yolk. You can sleep the fried chicken wing as it's just so-so, and it's cold when served. Overall, will revisit for the mama tomyam again! Go early as the crowds buildup by 5pm+.

author: Musa Çiçek
review_text: Tom yam was delicious and a bit hot for me. Fried rice with seafood was ok. prices are affordable. Service is fast .Line was about 10 min.

author: Suho L01
review_text:
Mostly tourists here. overall food’s great, No AC.
mama noodle is a bit tangy but still good, stir-fried veggie is super tasty, crispy pork is delicious, and the raw shrimp is fresh too! Recommend 😋

author: Hanh P
review_text:
Food here is exeptional good and low price.
Fresh shrimp.
Waiter waitress are quick. Very happy here.
Crispy pork also amazing must try pls.

author: Lis Horning
review_text:
This is a popular Thai restaurant, known for its signature seafood noodle dish. I came here to try it out, but honestly, the taste was quite average. The dish costs around 350 baht and is basically a mix of seafood and pork. It's more of a hype than actual value.

The place is quite hot and noisy, and although I didn’t have to wait today, it seems like there can be a wait during busy hours. The restaurant doesn’t offer Wi-Fi and only accepts cash—no card or mobile payment options—which makes it a bit inconvenient.

While the staff were polite and the menu has a decent variety, the overall experience didn’t feel worth a special trip. It’s okay for a one-time visit if you're nearby, but I wouldn’t come back regularly.

Ratings:

Food: 3.5/5 (variety is good, but flavor is average)

Service: 3.5/5 (limited payment options, no Wi-Fi)

Environment: 3/5 (hot and noisy)

Overall: Around 3/5

author: Wee Guan Kho
review_text:
This is a good alternative to the famous Jeh O.

The waiting time here is shorter and the food here can considered to be equally good.

Tom yum mama was flavourful but less spicy compared to the other famous stall.
The serving is huge with huge chunks of roasted pork, shrimp, squid, meatballs.

The salmon sashimi is well marinated and was in thick cuts too.

Would visit here again

author: huyền trần
review_text: Really must to try the shrimp spicy noodle 10/10 🤩🤩🤩 we have 7 members, total bill 1500bath => 220bath/per

author: Anique Lim
review_text: Alternatively shop for mama mee. Taste is good. Seafood also fresh. Both mama mee can’t compare as in their taste are different. Both for me is ok. This is the second choice. If you not enough time and not willing to wait can try this shop. Many other dishes can order too. Abit crowded during the dinner timing. But the staff will fast arrangement seat for you. Worth to eat as their tastes have their own style. Recommended.

author: Aron Loh
review_text: Tom yum noodles is great and nice. More towards the sour side. The seafood is fresh. The crispy pork is also delicious. The pork meat balls are tasty too. This restaurant is so much better than the "famous" michelin resturant who sell Tom yum noodles... you dont have to wait ridiculously long (e.g. 3-4hours). We were immediately seated, and there are many locals and tourists eating. I definitely will come back for this, if I'm craving for tom yum noodles. 😋

author: Kelv Low
review_text: Great Thai food with authentic flavors! The tom yum is rich and spicy, the crispy pork is perfectly crunchy, and every dish tastes fresh and well-seasoned. Portions are generous and the atmosphere is cozy. Definitely a place I’d come back to again. Highly recommended!

author: Sun Sassaeng
review_text:
As a local, I love this restaurant so much due to reasonable price, food portion and taste. I give all 5 stars.

This is One of my recommended restaurant.

Recommend crispy pork stir with garlic and chili

author: Eva Ruth
review_text: This place was busy and crowded around 10 pm. The tom yum mama noodles were delicious and flavourful. The crispy pork however was dry and quite chewy (like meat jerky) but flavour wise, it was good. The noodles can be shared between 2 - 3 hungry people or more if you order other dishes to share. It was worth the wait and visit as the noodles were satisfying. Despite eating at night, it can be quite warm due to the crowd and small spaces between people. A must try for dinner or supper if you’re nearby.

author: Leo Longo
review_text: I went there in a Sunday sunset and it was such a pleasant experience. I ordered this tasty and surprising Seafood and Pork Noodle that comes in this delicious sweet-sour-spicy sauce made with chilli, lemongrass, galangal, lime, coriander, kaffir lime leaves and some more. Prawns and squid were fresh and very well cooked. The pork, perfect. And the egg noodles, really tasty.

author: Happitel Apartment
review_text:
Som Som, a well-known Thai restaurant situated in the city center, carries the Chinese name "Song Song Restaurant." The venue features a vibrant orange color scheme, matching it's Thai name. The restaurant is specializing in a range of classic Thai dishes, stands out particularly for its crab and shrimp dishes.

The place tends to be quite busy, attracting mostly international tourists who come seeking an authentic experience. While the portion sizes are somewhat modest, possibly aligned with local Thai standard. The price is on the higher side. The dining environment is fairly standard, with limited space and closely arranged tables, creating a cozy but slightly cramped atmosphere.

In terms of flavor, the food delivers a solid and authentic Thai taste. As a foreigner, I can’t claim definitive expertise, but based on my experiences with various Thai restaurants, the quality here is quite commendable. Service, however, is average; while there appears to be an effort in staff training, some of the foreign employees seem not attractive enough perhaps due to cultural or communication gaps.

The drink menu is fairly standard as well, without any particularly standout options.
At this price point,one might find more genuinely traditional Thai meals elsewhere in Bangkok. That said, considering its central location and the convenience of paid parking available nearby at the stadium one, Som Som remains a decent choice.

A special mention goes to the glass noodle shrimp pot, a delightful dish with excellent flavor and appealing presentation. Keep up the good work!

author: YippieYaYa
review_text:
If you’re looking for a place that serves fresh seafood with bold flavors, Som Som Seafood is a must-visit! The highlight for me was their curry crab—rich, aromatic, and perfectly spiced. The crab was fresh and meaty, and the curry sauce had just the right balance of heat and creaminess, making it irresistible with steamed rice or mantou.

The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, and the staff were attentive and friendly. Prices are reasonable for the quality you get.

Highly recommended for seafood lovers—don’t miss the curry crab!

author: Kevin Khor
review_text: The glass noodles crab is so good, a must try. The prawn is well grill and juicy, and the curry crab meat is good too. The service is good with a lot of smile on face, love it. Seating is a bit packed but manageable.

author: mini kimtae
review_text:
For the first dish, which is fried fish with chili and salt, the fish was cut into nicely sized pieces, but the frying wasn’t very impressive — it wasn’t quite crispy. The seasoning was fairly okay, but overall it still wasn’t memorable.

As for the second dish, which is their signature glass noodles, I could only choose the crab-meat version this time because the whole-crab option was sold out. The seasoning leaned noticeably sweet, which personally wasn’t to my liking.

Regarding the price, it was fairly reasonable — not cheap, but not overly expensive either. Overall, the ingredients were of very good quality, but the seasoning and execution still weren’t outstanding enough.

author: Colin Leow
review_text:
One of the first places we went to once we arrived. While accustoming to the weather, getting accustomed to local delicacies is a must.

The wait time was relatively short, given the amount of people in line. They had a proper que system so you could gauge how long the wait it.

The crab and prawn dishes are amazing. Having ready peeled crab is a dream for most while the river prawn was extremely fresh and succulent.

Highly recommend this place.

author: Brian C.J. Chang
review_text: Crab Meat Curry and Crab Roe Glass Noodle are the standout dishes. The Creamy Scallops are just average. Overall, it’s definitely worth a visit.

author: Eric Cheng
review_text: Visited the new indoor air conditioned branch just opposite the old main store, the environment looks much comfort than the main store. Ordered few dishes including the famous fried crab meat with curry powder, crab meat fried rice, fried squid in salted egg yolk and tom yum. The portions for seafood is quite at value as there are lots of crab meat. The salted egg yolk is in nice smell and flavor and matched with the squid. Fried rice is not bad and it is good to eat with the curry sauce of the fried crab meat. The ton yum is strong in flavor but not very spicy or sour. Overall the meal is at great value.

author: Ong
review_text:
It's been a long time since I visited a nice Thai Zichar style restaurant.

The food here are amazing and the standout has got to be the curry crab and prawn woonsen. The glass noodle are  super tasty and must try. Every dish are easily a 7/10 up.

author: BC C
review_text: We waited about 45 minutes for a table for two, so be prepared for a crowd. The place was packed mostly with Chinese tourists, which already says something about its popularity. Once seated, we ordered the big prawns, scallops, and curry crab meat. Every dish was flavorful and cooked well — the curry crab meat especially stood out. Overall, the food was delicious and worth the wait, though the queue can test your patience.

author: wei chong lim
review_text: Best place for a seafood lover! This restaurant is so famous that they own 2 shops in the same alley. The new shop was much bigger and nicer compared to old restaurant. All the seafoods served was fresh and in good quality. The curry crab is suitable for those who can’t take spicy, haha. It was rich and creamy with slight spicy. River prawn has 2 sizes with different prices. It was not overly grilled which can bring out the best flavour and texture of the prawn. Crab meat fried rice was another dish that I like. Foods were presentable and served fast. Service from staffs was good as well.

author: Hai Yan Yu
review_text: we reached(12:10pm) before the shop open to skip the queue. we have already decided what to order while waiting for the store to open. so we are the first table to be served. Many dishes have different size to choose from. curry crab is the best. unfortunately that day live crab has not available yet when we place order. so we changed to river Prawn Vermicelli Casserole, not bad also.

author: DANNY LIN
review_text: We went to the new store across from the original restaurant. The new place is indoor with AC so a better environment to enjoy the meal. But IMO the food was just average. Mostly tourist crowd.

author: SUEB Songprasert
review_text:
Service was warm and attentive. The staff really know their menu and give great recommendations.

The atmosphere is HUNGRY but still cozy — perfect for a casual dinner or celebration with friends.

author: Skye Cai
review_text:
Great yellow curry crab meat.
Not too oily. the crab meat is jumbo and fresh. The meat is sweet doesn’t have strong taste. Goes very well with the curry.
The red chilli cloves on top is a little spicy.
Friendly staff that will great everyone.
Queue is massy but once get the queue number it’s quite fast.
CASH ONLY!

author: Emily Ky
review_text:
Sevice is good and staff well trained.
However food serving not hot enough and getting cold in 15 minutes. River prawn not the fresh catch indeed it’s frozen. Overall,foods just average with not in economic range. A lot of China Tourist and most probably they saw some tourist videos.

author: Wayne Wayne
review_text: Very popular seafood restaurant in Chulalongkorn Street. The staff are very efficient, the waiting time for table is around 10mins. For the dish that I ordered which is glass noodles with prawn, crabmeat with curry, seafood Tom yum gong and vegetables. Taste good and very authentic Thai food. The total bill is THB 1250 plus drinks.

author: SF SIT
review_text: the food here was super good!!! the seafood was so fresh and flavourful, hope to come again sometime in the near future the next time i’m in bangkok. also pretty affordable for the size of the seafood.

author: RA Rivera
review_text: Foods are sumptous and fresh! I love the seafoods that they served us. They gave us a generous serving of our meals. Service is okay, a typical asian restaurant but its really the taste of the food that made a mark for me. Pricing is not cheap but definitely not expensive.

author: Ying Xin
review_text: Had a great dining experience at Som Som Seafood! The seafood was incredibly fresh, and you can really taste the difference. Everything was cooked perfectly – flavorful, not overdone, and served hot. Definitely a hidden gem for seafood lovers. Will come back again! ❤️

author: Eunice Ang
review_text: To be fair, food is good. I like the honesty of the staff, they informed the price of the crab and prawn before we ordered. Love the grilled prawn, cuttlefish,  clams and also the vegetables. The vermicelli crab...not so nice, a bit sweet. Overall is good and reasonably priced.

author: Eevonn Ng
review_text: Famous for their toasted milk bun will filling, must try when you’re here. Butter sugar seem average would recommend other flavour! Nutella is good! Full of filling

author: Louis Lin
review_text:
Came here for my lil sweet treat after dining at Chula 50 and on my way back to Siam Centre 🤭

It was recommended to me multiple times from my For You Page as a popular/ viral charcoal toast place, and I was so so glad that there wasn’t a line when I arrived (it was also bordering on drizzling/raining and before the huge dinner rush time).

The staff was incredibly kind and helped me decide on the flavors (cue me: indecisive and overwhelmed by the options available 😂), and their interior was nice and clean as well (I was able to use their washroom while I was waiting).

Now, onto the toast itself. Listen, I’m a HUGE sweet tooth, like, I can devour a full chocolate cake to myself if I really want to in one sitting (neither here nor there don’t judge me 🫣🥴), but holy. Moly. The condensed milk flavor one I almost couldn’t finish because of how sweet it was. That’s just a personal preference though, as the other two I got (Ovaltine Crunchy/ Thai Milk Tea) were fantastic.

I love they you can see them grill the bread right in front of you and how fluffy they are when you bite into them. My favorite was definitely the Ovaltine Crunchy one with the nutty flavor combing with the slightly charcoal taste to create an amazing infusion of texture and taste in your mouth 👄 The best way to describe it is literally eating a pillowy Ferrero Rocher 🤤

I want to come back to try other flavors!

author: Marcus Ang
review_text:
bread was toasted over charcoal, crispy and fluffy. pandan custard is like singapore's 'kaya', but its way more coconutty and less sweet.

'special' as theres nothing of this sort around the area, come for consistency, not for 'wow'

author: мιѕѕувєlα2828
review_text:
Another popular spot along Banthat Thong Road that consistently draws a long queue—this place is well-loved for its toasted buns with a variety of fillings.

We tried the Thai milk tea and pandan custard versions, and they definitely exceeded our expectations. The buns were perfectly toasted—crispy on the outside while staying soft and fluffy inside. The chilled custard filling, which had an ice cream–like texture, complemented the warm bun beautifully.

At just 50 THB for two buns, it’s an affordable and satisfying sweet treat worth queuing for!

author: Anique Lim
review_text: Nice buttery buns comes with different filling. Of course my favourites will be Thai Tea and Matcha. When we order then produce. Fresh buns and seating area just next to the shop. Air conditioning and provide free drinking water. Must try is you in the area. You won’t regret.

author: Yeoh Ts
review_text: They offer a variety of flavors, all made fresh to order. I tried the pandan flavour it was delicious! The bread has a slightly crispy outer layer, is fragrant and soft, with just the right amount of sweetness not too heavy at all. The place has seating, air conditioning, and even free drinking water.

author: Wojciech Kałużny
review_text:
Ok! I have to admit. That was best dessert I ate in whole thailand.

Its soft, kind of cripsy and sauce inside its just sooooo tasty!

You must try it when you will be in Bangkok!

author: Victor Ng
review_text:
Even though I ordered to eat at the shop the bread was served in a closed plastic box. Bread was soggy and mushy - as though it came from the microwave.

Thai tea had no sugar.

author: Keith
review_text:
Nestled on the bustling Banthat Thong Road, Pungdet is a charming café that has garnered a loyal following for its meticulously prepared charcoal-toasted bread. Banthat Thong Road itself has a rich history—originally known as "Phra That Thong" and once a hub for car repair shops, it has since transformed into one of Bangkok's premier culinary destinations. Today, the street is lined with a vibrant array of eateries, attracting food enthusiasts from near and far.

At Pungdet, the focus is clear: delivering perfectly toasted bread with fillings that delight both the sweet and savory palate. Each piece is toasted to order over a charcoal flame, a process that takes just enough time to create a crisp, golden exterior while warming the fillings within. The result? A fragrant and irresistibly soft bite that lingers on the palate.

The Offerings
With an impressive selection of 22 fillings, diners are spoiled for choice. Among the highlights are:

Ham and Cheese – A timeless pairing of melted cheese and smoky ham.
Butter Sugar – A sweet classic with buttery richness and a delicate sprinkle of sugar.
Hokkaido Milk – Smooth, creamy, and delicately sweet, inspired by Japan's famed dairy.
Tuna – A savory favorite for seafood lovers.
Smoked Salmon – A luxurious option with bold, smoky notes.
Prices are refreshingly affordable, ranging from 20 THB for a simple butter sugar toast to 60 THB for premium fillings like smoked salmon.

A Culinary Experience
During my visit, I opted for the Hokkaido Milk and Thai Tea fillings. The bread, served fresh from the grill, boasted a wonderfully crisp crust and a pillowy-soft interior. The Hokkaido Milk filling was divine—creamy, light, and delicately sweet, a perfect complement to the toasted bread. The Thai Tea filling, though flavorful, leaned on the sweeter side and might be an acquired taste for some.

For those seeking a savory indulgence, the Ham and Cheese filling appears to be a crowd favorite, and it’s certainly on my list for my next visit.

Ambiance
The café features a cozy, air-conditioned space next door, complete with tables and chairs for diners who prefer to savor their toast on-site. Fresh water and tissues are thoughtfully provided, making for a comfortable dining experience. While the buns are delightful at any time, they’re best enjoyed fresh off the grill when the textures and aromas are at their peak.

Verdict
Pungdet is a must-visit for anyone exploring Banthat Thong Road. Its combination of expertly toasted bread, a wide variety of fillings, and unbeatable value makes it a standout destination in Bangkok's thriving food scene. Whether you're looking for a quick snack or a leisurely treat, Pungdet delivers with charm and consistency.

author: Sai
review_text:
Consider as street food.
Sell barbecued bread with various filling. The owner tried to put in all his favourite food as the bread filling, that's how the idea come to mind.
You can sit beside the shop with air conditional. But the area is bad with air ventilation where the smell of burned charcoal in the room.
Table is not clean after guest left.
The price is acceptable and worth to try.

author: Nickyta Cahaya Putri
review_text:
Pungdet offer more than 20 fillings you can choose, and we end up getting the thai tea custard and ovaltine crunch. the bun has crisp crust and pillowy texture, combined with smooth and not overly sweet custard that blends well in our mouth.

overall, this is the best option to go instead of the famous Yaowarat bread. less queue, same ambience, same price, plus you can dine in next to the shop!

author: JJ Jen
review_text: Can try if you are around here, need to wait for 5-8 mins. Nothing overly fantastic. They are generous with the fillings.

author: Ong Ting Yong
review_text:
I tried Pungdet’s Bread with Nutella, and it was a simple yet indulgent treat! The bread itself was incredibly soft and fluffy, with a light texture that made every bite enjoyable. It had the perfect balance of chewiness and airiness, making it an ideal base for the rich filling.

The Nutella filling was generous and oozed out beautifully with every bite, giving that signature chocolate-hazelnut flavor that we all love. It was smooth, creamy, and not overly sweet, complementing the softness of the bread perfectly. The slight warmth of the bread made the Nutella even more melty and satisfying.

While it’s a straightforward snack, the quality of the bread and the richness of the filling set it apart. It’s the perfect comfort food—simple, nostalgic, and delicious. Whether you’re grabbing a quick bite or satisfying a sweet craving, Pungdet’s Bread with Nutella is definitely worth trying. Highly recommended for chocolate lovers!

author: SK C
review_text: I feel nothing special, just a normal bread filled with cream/jam

author: MX
review_text: Best buns EVER. So crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside. Pandan custard was fragrant without being overly sweet. I wish I had more stomach space to try every single flavour on the menu. Very good

author: Benya
review_text:
DECENT

The crunchy Ovaltine spread was divine but the toasted bread was so-so - it could use more toasting, making it more crispy on the outside. The menu toasted bread dip was awesome though - the texture was just right.

author: Jowen Goh
review_text: I came around 5:30pm and luckily there wasn’t a very long queue. The buns are toasted with butter and then filled with whatever fillings we choose. I ordered their Pandan and thai milk tea, both were divine. Fillings were generous and the servers were also very friendly.

author: Kayla Lujan
review_text: Quick spot for a sweet treat. We got Nutella and PN&J both were good! Messy but they have a small AC area next door (most people dont see it) so there was seating to snack on these!

author: William Ten
review_text:
The bun is quite nice but not surprised
Price is reasonable
The environment is good, they have a small aircon room for sitting beside the store

author: Andesita Ryanesia
review_text:
so so soo good! much better than the famous thai Yawarat bread!
the size of the bread is perfect, not too big not too small. I buy 4, and got the free one for butter and sugar bread!
Its always full of people, but their service is top! No need to wait for long cos they have enough staff to make your bread ready, and professional having queue number so its fair for everyone. If youre in Banthatong area, this is a must try one!

author: Pang Thunyalak
review_text: The milk is delicious, but the place gets quite crowded, so the wait can be long. I recommend booking a queue through the QueQ app beforehand. Orders are placed and picked up at the counter. The shop isn’t very spacious but has a great location. The salted egg yolk toast is also amazing and reasonably priced!

author: inky Lalita
review_text: We went there around 5:30 PM on a Thursday, so there was no queue. Their tea was quite good in terms of both taste and aroma. I recommend ordering the Lava Toast with salted egg and Hokkaido ice cream—it’s definitely worth trying!

author: Thee Theerapat
review_text:
The flavored milk is the best! All flavor! Other desserts like bingsu is also worth mentioning with reasonable price. However, the other signature; toast on a stick with dipping options is not as good as others.

Not to mention that all the good time with this restaurant exchanged with extremely long queues, and ultimately long if you chose to seat-in.

author: H L
review_text: If you are into bread and milk, this place is a must try. However the queue is always very long, so it is good if you can get the Q number first then walk around or eat other things while waiting. Alternatively, you can buy the milk to-go and enjoy it elsewhere.

author: Yun Yi Thiam
review_text:
Nothing fantastic. Ordered takeaway as the queue was too long (mostly tourists) but still ended up waiting 35 min for our toast.

The toast itself was crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and paired well with the pandan sauce. The milk was alright, I personally liked the original flavour. My friend had the milk slushy and unfortunately vomited afterwards, which was disappointing.

Overall, food was decent, the long wait and our experience with the milk slushy means I wouldn’t queue for this again.

author: Amy Jessica
review_text: The bread was so good. I love the White Melt Milk and Signature flavors. They're not too sweet and have a fresh milk . I really love it, and I've bought it twice. If you want to buy a drink, the wait isn't too long, but if you're buying bread, it takes more time.

author: Mac Vichien
review_text: Let me start with smoother, richer and delicately flavored. A second time visiting this place and it's still enjoyable. Beautiful baked quality bread and mouthwatering dip. Salted egg York is still a champ. Thai tea and passionfruit are delightful too. This place is quite busy. I've waited nearly 30 mins. Plan yourself if you want to go there. However, my focus is on the quality that makes it worthy to be waited for.

author: KN IWN
review_text:
There are around 70+ queues ahead of us but we got seats within less than 30 mins which we consider it’s quite fast. You can just walk around to get some other snack while waiting but make sure you arrive the shop before they call/announce your number/queue.

The bread and dipping are very good but the milk is normal. We were 7 people but we got a small table at the corner but we had no problem as we will finish quite fast.

author: Daud
review_text: It’s probably the most popular place in here, very crowded all the time. The kind of food are bread dipping with Kaya, milk and some dessert. Their milk isn’t my favorite. It is overhyped and overwhelming people because customers have to wait outside for their takeout order, in the corner of the road.

author: Sammy
review_text:
This place is very crowded. The queue is very long, which takes like an hours during the evening till night.

There are variety of menus and options for dipping. I really like salted egg dipping.
I tried the milk, its not special for me, its ok.

Overall is yummy for sweet tooth!

author: Kawin Leenutaphong
review_text:
The queue is super long especially during the weekend, better use the QueQ to check in before coming. The wait time is most likely not worth it and I came here twice a months….

The brioche is quite good compared to the same kind of popular bread joint in BKK, the milk is popular but also average… anyway give it a try it is a good place with reasonable price

author: Jasmine Tan
review_text: Very crowded, but queue moves fast. After ordering, can wait outside if no space inside. Bread is nice but dip (hokkaido milk) was tasteless. Can just get the bread without dip. The bottled milk (Taiwanese milk tea flavour) was very sweet but quite fragrant.

author: Andrea D'Souza
review_text:
This place was near our hotel and had a crowd of locals every single night so we decided to see what the hype was all about.
Got the toasted bread and the milk after reading the reviews and personally didn't like either.
The toast was dry, couldn't taste much of the flavour. The milk wasn't that great and tasted a bit too sweet for my liking.
I'd suggest skipping it. It's just a fad and in my honest opinion not worth such a high price point.
P.S: the staff were really sweet. 5/5 for being helpful and very patient with the language barrier.

author: Jonathan
review_text: Went during the Halloween period, street super crowded. Queue to eat inside is very long, takeaway can be done much faster at the counter, waited around 15 minutes. Got 9 sticks of bread, sauces were ok, the yellow salted egg one was a little too savoury. The bottled milk from the fridge is very sweet

author: Ittiwat Sa-nguanwong
review_text:
From Phuket to BKK, the most crowded milk and toast restaurant.

Their line filled up before they are open on 16:00 but no matter early you be here on 16:00 you have to que up in the app called "QueQ" which can find on both play store and app store.

Their milk serves in double walled tumbler with no ice that will make the milk more concentrated without ice melting. The milk itself is average taste and smell

For bread they have 3 kinds of breads, the most famous is Shokupan with the choices of toast or steam. They serve with many kinds of dippings. You can follow their best seller if it is your first time here.

For me the Shokupan is too light and hollow which makes my after bite feeling gone so fast may be it is because they serve in tiny pieces.

Overall they are serving quality food with good services.

LET'S TRY!!!!

author: Canbettt
review_text: Normal toast with Thai sauce dip. Very crowded and queue up more than 2 hours. You need to download Queq app to queue up this restaurant. If you can wait and have nothing to do at night, you can try this place. If u're not, other type of toasts at other restaurant is quite the same. I think just popular among juveniles. Nothing's special, but the price is worth and fair.

author: Eddie Lim
review_text:
Long queue.
Milk is just normal. Any fresh milk or meiji milk is better.
Bread was OK but the dipping sauce is just sweet and colouring with no taste of custard or brown

author: Berlinda Goh
review_text:
A popular dessert shop with a cute boy logo. Managed to get a table without much waiting in the evening but it was full house.
Ordered the toast skewers with 3 dipping sauces - bread was light in texture, sauces were given generously and not overly sweet.
Drinks - had the Thai Tea Milk and Strawberry Milk, too sweet!

author: Madeleine Tan
review_text: We visited on a weekday before 5 PM and were seated immediately. Despite the early hour, the place was already bustling and by 6 PM, a queue had formed outside so arriving early is a good idea. We ordered the toast with three dips. The salted egg dip stood out with its strong, savory, and creamy flavor. The pandan dip was fragrant and had just the right level of sweetness. The Hokkaido milk dip while slightly sweet, didn't have as bold a flavor as the others. The staff frequently topped up the milk at the fridge and my personal favorite was the chocolate milk which had the most intense flavor.

author: Emeline Koh
review_text:
I choose to take away because there is no seats at the place and need to wait for a long time.   Tried the milk and find that it’s not nice as it’s sweet and taste weird for fresh milk.  For the bread , I don’t like it because it’s toasted and a bit too dry.  Guess I still prefer the street steam bread with kaya.

This is not worth the price and the wait.  The queue is because of the crowd from social media.  It will die down soon for the trend then.

author: Philip Saulescu
review_text: Long queue but the food was amazing. The tom yum was very rich in flavors and had amazing toppings. The broth was very thick and perfect for someone who likes the tom yum with more coconut milk. Dumplings tasted amazing as well and the prices were really good.

author: Coriandermixxx
review_text:
The place is super hype and people will queue for hours! There are two options for queuing:

Use the QueQ app (recommended for faster process)

Or come directly to the restaurant.

We used the app and only waited about 10 minutes in front of the restaurant.

What we ordered:

1. Roasted Pork 🐖 – 4/5 Good, but tastes similar to what you find at the night market.

2. Mama Noodle 🍜 (Roasted Pork & Seafood) – 4/5 This is the specialty here. Toppings are generous (prawn, squid). Noodles are too thin for my taste. If you can eat spicy, go for it! Otherwise, the sourness dominates.

3. Salmon Salad 🐟🥗– 4/5 Good, but again similar to night market quality.

💡 Tip: For roasted pork and salmon, the night market is better value – same quality, cheaper price, and bigger portion.

author: Aung Aung Oo (Ezra)
review_text:
The food is great and the portions are huge (one bowl easily feeds two!). Service is fast once you’re seated, but honestly, waiting through hundreds of tables is a "do it once" kind of experience. Next time, I’d probably just hit a regular street food spot. 🤷🏻‍♂️

Pro Tip: Use the QueQ app to queue up early so you can wander around while you wait.

Overall: 7/10 — worth trying once for the hype!

author: Thanthar Shwe
review_text:
Spicy Salmon Salad - very fresh and flavorful. So spicy though. Would recommend.

Signature Mama Noodle - We’ve got the one with mixed toppings. Crispy pork, crabs, pork balls, shrimp, squid etc. topping were all fresh but the noodle and the soup is just your typical instant spicy mama noodles. I really don’t understand the hype at all.

Dumplings - good and juicy. Don’t know what they were made of.

The waiting - we went on a Wednesday. we did the queue through QueQ app. We had to wait about 2 hours. Took the queue around 7 and we got seated around 8:30 pm. We just went and ate around the Banthatong street while we wait, so it wasn’t so bad. The queue was still long until the time we left the area at 10:30.

The total bill - 1400 THB.

The menu - there were so many items on the menu but Mama Noodle, salmon salad and crispy pork seem to be the most popular. The menu’s all in Thai. No English menu available.

If anyone sees this review in time, the shop is gonna close from 27 Nov to 2 Dec 2025.

author: stevanie yuliana
review_text:
Located in a busy dining hub, this restaurant is a favorite among tourists. I suggest visiting when you are hungry because the dishes are meant for sharing.

At first, I was a bit confused by the long line. You have to download an app to get a queue number and wait for your turn to be called. The service is very fast, but I suggest improving the restrooms because so many people visit this place.

Overall, the food tastes great, and it even has a Michelin star. It is located near Central World, an area full of other great restaurants.

author: Nikireview
review_text:
My number one place to visit whenever I’m in Bangkok.

This is my favorite Tom Yum ever! The taste is rich, a bit spicy, and the combination of seafood, egg, and all the condiments inside is just amazing. We also tried their fried sausage , and it was incredible.

The only downside is the long wait, we had to queue for a solid 2-3 hours. The good thing is, there are plenty of trendy cafes and restaurants nearby to check out while you wait.

I definitely recommend everyone to visit at least once if you’re in Bangkok.

author: Hank Peng
review_text: Seriously, I don't get it. Mama noodles are okay, but definitely not worth waiting an hour and 40 minutes for. They make you download the QueQ app to get a number, and then you wait to be called. And if you're not there when they call your number, you gotta start all over. One dish worth mentioning is the spicy salmon salad. It's good～

author: Frédéric Hachnel
review_text: Get a line number on QueQ app before. We waited 2 hoyrs 30mn and it was worth all the wait. Salmon salad and tom yum mama were amazing. Just go and give 5 stars rhey deserve way more than 4.1 avg. Only negative point was they ran out of crispy pork and shrimps but it didn t matter much at the end

author: Frederick Sun (Freddie)
review_text: You will download the App to get a number and wait for the table. It took me about 90 mins to get the table. I started joining the App while leaving the hotel. Still waited 40 mins at the restaurant. The mama noddle mixed was delicious as their signature. The crispy pork was also super good. Especially dipping in mama noddle’s soup. The squid with yellow curry was so so, not recommended. Did not order the raw salmon which is also their signature.

author: 马焕昭
review_text:
Last night, I made a special trip to the Chulalongkorn University Night Market and finally got to try the legendary Jeb O Chula Banthatthong! Even though we waited in line for almost an hour, the first bite made it all worth it.

We ordered the signature "Mama Noodles." The steaming copper pot was packed with ingredients—large, fresh prawns, tender minced pork, a runny egg, and refreshing straw mushrooms. The most amazing part was the soup: the Tom Yum base was perfectly sour and spicy, with the richness of coconut milk balancing the heat just right. Every spoonful was incredibly addictive. I especially have to praise the spiciness level—it had a strong kick but didn't upset the stomach, making you crave more with each bite.

Even though the place was packed, the service was surprisingly fast. Highly recommended for anyone who loves spicy food. This is absolutely a must-try, god-tier supper spot in Bangkok!

author: Junior Franco
review_text: This popular Michelin awarded spot is charming and the service is friendly. However, the food doesn't quite live up to the hype. The flavors often taste muted and one-note, lacking the fresh, vibrant punch of authentic Thai cuisine. Some dishes ingredients don't always taste garden-fresh. It's a decent meal, but for the reputation, you'd expect more exciting taste and better quality. It's good for a casual fix, but not the culinary destination it's made out to be.

author: kunal gandhi
review_text:
The food at Jeh O Chula is absolutely worth the wait—and wait you will. Even if you arrive early, there’s already a line, and it usually takes over an hour to get a table. The service is fast and tables turn quickly, but the queue still moves slowly.

Now, the menu is huge, but let’s be honest—you’re here for one thing: the Tom Yum Noodles. Go straight to that section. There are six versions: two with pork, two with seafood, and two with crab. While you wait, order a few starters; there are plenty of great options to warm up your appetite.

Be careful with the spice level—it can get seriously hot. If you’re not big on spicy food, choose the mild option.

Will I come back to Jeh O Chula? Absolutely. It may feel touristy, and many locals skip the line because they don’t have the patience, but everyone agrees the food is outstanding. Oh one last thing, they only accept cash so do carry enough money with you.

Till next time.

author: i . am . kenny
review_text: Tried their (in)famous tom yam seafood Mama. I would say it tastes and looks good. Order a veggie as a side and i was stuffed. I came early around 4 when there is still space, but crowd started to stream in and queue formed when i left. I guess this place is really popular. Staff were sometimes non-attentive likely because i sat at a corner where no one can really see me. Best to come in group to enjoy more of their food. Overall great experience. Will patronize again.

author: yc
review_text:
Please use the QueQ app to book your place else expect to wait for a very long time. We came on a Wednesday evening and had 89 people ahead of us.
Ordered the Tom Yum Mama (everything except the crab meat) and crispy pork.
The noodles was very good as it soaked up the Tom yum nicely. Every bite was divine. The ingredients tbh was not anything special. Meatball were slightly dry but if you dip in the Tom yum it’s ok. Squid was slightly tough to chew. The crispy pork was ok not fantastic.
I would definitely return for the noodles as it was superb.

author: Remika
review_text:
Great experience but please book before on queQ so you don’t have to wait! the noodles are so yummy and they have so many options.

Staff are friendly and helpfully. service is also quick. try everything! for 5 people we paid 1600 baht

author: Kate Rosita
review_text: A very popular restaurant. Although it serves instant noodles, the ingredients are great. It deserves the Michelin name and tastes great. Be sure to use the app to queue in advance to avoid meal times. They sell whole coconuts, so you can ask the staff.

author: Crystal
review_text: Queued 2 hours for our turn (thank god for the online queue system). Didn't have much expectation but the taste and experience was really mediocre for all the Michelin stickers and hype around this shop. Tom yum taste was not rich and creamy. However, broth was flavourful from the pork and seafood. Ordered the deep fried tofu and fried kale which definitely tasted better than the main dish.

author: KE XIN CHUA
review_text: The mama noodles are on the sweeter side, and the food overall is fairly average. The taste really depends on personal preference, and nothing particularly gave me a “wow” feeling. Remember to download the QueQ app to get a queue number for your table.

author: Andrew Rodriguez
review_text: Jeh O Chula is crazy busy but totally worth the wait. The Mama Tom Yum noodles are rich, spicy, and loaded with toppings—I couldn’t stop eating. The crispy pork belly and salmon sashimi were also fantastic. It’s chaotic, crowded, and fun—exactly the kind of Bangkok food experience I was hoping for.

author: Melody Liang
review_text:
The pros:
The food is 100% DELICIOUS. I got the spicy salmon salad and the pork tom yum mama noodles and they are both so good 😩😩if you love sour flavours this is the place for you
I would say that the spicy salmon salad is VERY spicy (at least for me) so either bring water or buy a cold drink
The tom yum on the other hand has that classic flavour but isn’t spicy, and hey, there’s free wifi!
Portion size is great as well
The cons:
I came on a Monday night at around 6:45pm, there were I think 92 in front of me and I waited a total of 2 hours (I was told it’d be 90 minutes)
They put me (a single person) on a table that could easily fit four people if not five people, I think this is the reason for the long queue and low table turnover rate — should consider putting guests together!
Service is also subpar — staff looks like they’d rather be anywhere else
I also had to go to another table to get tissue since there wasn’t any on mine

author: Chetha Thirathinarut
review_text:
Enjoy a variety of creative fusion-style som tam dishes (I tried the mangosteen & strawberry version!)
along with authentic Northeastern Thai (Isaan) favorites that are packed with bold, spicy flavors.
Every dish was absolutely delicious! 😋

author: Mulyadi Syariffudin
review_text: Had a superb meal at Kampang ISAN. First time ever trying Ants Larva but it doesn’t have any taste really but the omelette was superbly fried. The grilled Pork Neck was done to perfection!

author: MP
review_text: Food is really good, portions abundant but service could be better. We had a few dishes which were really tasty and more than enough.

author: J “Joey” Jouk
review_text:
I’ve been to Kampang ISAN Casual Dining (คำแพง) many times now, and each visit continues to impress me. It’s rare to find a place that maintains such a high level of consistency, but Kampang nails it — every single time. The food is truly authentic Isan, bursting with bold, spicy flavors and made with fresh, high-quality ingredients.

Some of my favorites include the som tum (papaya salad), grilled chicken, and larb — all perfectly seasoned and packed with that signature northeastern kick. The sticky rice is always warm and soft, and their dipping sauces are addictive. Even the simple dishes are elevated with care and attention to detail.

The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, making it great for anything from a quick lunch to a relaxed dinner with friends. The staff are always kind, attentive, and efficient, which adds to the overall great experience. You feel genuinely taken care of from the moment you arrive.

And I can’t leave out the iced tea — it’s honestly one of the best I’ve ever had. Perfectly sweet, cold, and refreshing — it balances out the heat of the food beautifully.

Kampang is a gem for anyone who loves Isan cuisine. Highly recommended and worth coming back to again and again!

author: Siwahdol Chaimano
review_text: This place is Esaan (northeastern Thai) food. Personally, it is a bit too sweet and salty. I thought it was good but after few spoon taken, I had to take a break for the saltiness. The pork is very good and the soup was alright. The. Staff are nice, and the location was good. We got free tea just to add Line of the restaurant. The price was quite expensive compared to other Somtom (papaya salad) especially for the one that has noodles in it. Overall it was good to try.

author: Andrew S
review_text: We ordered two salads: mangosteen salad and schrimp salad. Both salads have very interesting combinations, and both are tasty. Some vegetables I would never eat raw, but here they are in the salads. The small fried fish were too much in both salads. The steak was a bit chewy but I like it that way.

author: Thanatpong Rujirawan
review_text:
Despite a 30-minute wait for a table, this Thai papaya salad restaurant proved to be worth the patience. The compact, bustling space creates an intimate atmosphere, though it can feel somewhat crowded during peak hours.

The standout dish was undoubtedly their grilled chicken – beautifully marinated and grilled to perfection, it's an absolute must-try for any visitor. Their salads showcase authentic Thai flavors with well-balanced seasoning that stays true to traditional preparations. The portion sizes justify the pricing, offering good value for the quality received.

The service had some hiccups, with a noticeable 20-minute gap between our initial dishes and the final two orders, which appeared to have been overlooked. However, the staff handled the situation professionally, offering sincere apologies and expediting the remaining dishes.

Overall, while the restaurant may have room for improvement in service efficiency and space management, the exceptional food quality, particularly the grilled chicken, makes it a worthwhile dining destination.

author: Kitprasert Srisamran
review_text: Really enjoyed the food, the chill vibe, and how fast everything came out. It wasn’t crowded, and they had some good promos too. Great place to hang out after work.

author: Kim Chii
review_text: I had tried similar salads at other places and really enjoyed it, so I gave this place a shot — but honestly, it was a huge letdown. The soup was absolutely terrible, with a strong, unpleasant smell that made it almost inedible. The salad was just plain and forgettable. The salad was okay at best, but nothing worth coming back for. The only good thing was the service — staff were polite and attentive. the atmosphere is lovely also. Unfortunately, the food was bad enough that I won’t be returnin

author: Wasita Jirakajohnchai
review_text:
▪️ Taste so the food quite simple and salty
▪️ The price too high if compared with the ordinary market price.
▪️ The shop so narrow and feel uncomfortable to sit.

Ps. Suggest to get the sit without get the line come early around 3:30-4:00 pm

author: Sandee Tour
review_text: Fusion and modernized eastern Thai food. The salad dishes were very tasty, fresh ingredients, nice French and aromatic. However the protein dishes such as the beef was over cooked, tough and under flavor. This was also the same thing with the grilled pork neck, which was way thinly cut and not that aromatic.  We dine during lunch time and no wait even for large group

author: Mmhewy S
review_text: This is an Isan restaurant decorated in a casual dining style. Those who like spicy food will probably like it, but I personally don't eat fermented fish, and each menu focuses on that. Fortunately, there are some interesting dishes on the menu. We ordered the Somtam Thai with Chan noodles and salted eggs, which didn't have any fermented fish. The taste was really good, sour, sweet, salty, and had a variety of flavors. However, the price was a bit higher, but compared to the ingredients and location, it's understandable.

author: Hangry Joobert
review_text:
The flavors are bold, fiery, and everything people have been raving about. They offer more than 100 dishes covering everything from somtum, yum, soups, deep-fried, stir-fried, grilled, and laab—literally every style you could crave.

The vibe is super relaxed with air conditioning, making it great whether you’re dining with family, friends, or a big group. The flavors lean toward authentic Isan—spicy, punchy, and definitely not toned down. We tried quite a few dishes today and loved every single one.

Highlights from our table:
🥩 Grilled beef brisket with jaew dipping sauce
🦀 Somtum with blue crab
🐜 Red ant egg omelet
🥓 Fried rice with pork cracklings
🌶️ Glass noodle somtum with minced pork
🍲 Spicy soup with pork cartilage

author: Pang Thunyalak
review_text: The food here is delicious, especially the mushroom curry and mangosteen salad—they’re a must-try! On weekday evenings, there’s hardly any wait, and the prices are reasonable. The service is excellent, and the food is served quickly. I can’t wait to try other dishes next time. Highly recommend this place!

author: Austin
review_text:
Came at 5pm on weekdays and some tables were available but we recommend you better call for reservations since it’s always crowded.

The meat was a bit chewy, tastes not bad though. Grilled chicken was really delicious, but the meat stuck to the bone making them hard to eat. Vanilla jasmine lemon tea was not our favorite.

The price was quite high. The table next to us tried to call the staffs for 3 times before they noticed.

author: Cheryl Lee
review_text:
This looks really good, almost full house in fact, hop over to get the authentic thai food here!! Come with friends and be satisfied!!
Love the vibes here!!

author: Anupong Wongkulluck
review_text:
Popular restaurant on Social Network. We arrived at 12.15 and got our hand on the first serve at 12.45 and it was a simple sticky rice without any main dishes. 10 minutes later we got mangosteen slad which was very salty and overpriced. Grilled chicken was okay but still overpriced as well. Lastly, papaya salad tasted weird and was not worth a try.

Summary: overpriced and too long waiting

author: Witchayut Chokwongjaroen
review_text:
Food was a bit overpriced but the taste was good. I got the ‘คั่วตับ‘ steak which is hard to find at other restaurants and the taste was good just the texture was a bit chewy like informed.
The Jaew Hon noodle was also good tasted quite strong and intense we ordered less spicy but still quite spicy

author: wan ling
review_text: Came during dinner. It was pretty busy. However, the service staff was friendly and attentive to the guest needs . Food wise,  ordered fried chicken wing , salmon papaya salad add on corn, and sticky rice . Best sticky rice i ever have in bangkok . It's tender and goes well with the dishes ordered. The restaurant to go to when in Ban tha tong.

author: Kanokrak
review_text: Food came out really quick. Good portions and nicely balanced flavour too. We ordered less spicy which is already spicy enough, make sure you don’t go for normal spicy if you’re foreigner..

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: leotrails
review_text:
A good Thai mookrata buffet spot located on Banthat Thong Road.

The atmosphere is great—perfect for cooking, chatting, and hanging out with friends. The fried chicken wings and enoki mushrooms are nicely crunchy and really satisfying.

For the BBQ, the sliced pork neck and pork loin are good quality and flavorful.

Beef and pork can be cooked separately, which is helpful for Muslim diners.

Would definitely come back again to dine with friends!👍

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Rhonda S
review_text:
🔥 Mookata Heaven at 71 Mookata (Banthat Thong Branch)! 🔥
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Hands down one of the best Mookata experiences in Bangkok!

🥩 Quality Ingredients:
The meat was incredibly fresh, especially the marbled pork and chicken slices. The seafood platter was packed with scallops, prawns, squid, and more—all super fresh and clean.

🍲 Flavorful Broth & Grill:
Their golden grill pan heats up quickly and evenly. The broth was rich and comforting, perfect for boiling veggies and noodles. Grilling meat on the dome gave it that authentic smokey-charred edge.

🥗 Sides & Highlights:
We loved the generous veggie platter and their signature raw shrimp salad with spicy lime chili sauce—zesty, refreshing, and packed a punch! 🌶️🦐

🪑 Comfortable Setting:
Spacious, clean interior with modern decor and good ventilation. Tables were arranged neatly and staff was attentive and polite.

💰 Value for Money:
Portions were generous, and the quality surpassed the price. A great spot for group dinners or satisfying mookata cravings.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: D G S
review_text:
The most fabulous hot pot experience we’ve ever had! We enjoyed both the soup and the grill — everything was just amazing. We couldn’t even finish all the food we ordered, there was so much! The value for money was incredible.
Totally worth it.
Just wow!

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Panar Taw
review_text: Food is ok but I feel like the price is a bit high compared to the quality, the beef on the set is too chewy, but the picanha beef is nice

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Cheryl Lee
review_text: Aircon mookata, looks good and nice, many locals here instead of tourists, recommended to try, must come to this food street, it’s a amazing place with lots of variety!!

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Apple Mae Dionaldo
review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at 71 Mookata, and it was an experience I won’t forget. The restaurant specializes in mookata, a Thai-style BBQ where you grill your own meat and vegetables on a hot plate, creating a fun and interactive dining experience. The food grill set offered a wide variety of options, from juicy cuts of beef and pork to fresh seafood and a selection of vegetables. Everything was well-marinated, which really enhanced the flavors as it cooked. I especially enjoyed the dipping sauces that complemented the grilled items perfectly.

The location of 71 Mookata is very convenient, situated in a vibrant area with plenty of parking nearby. The atmosphere inside was casual and inviting, with a warm, cozy vibe that made it a great spot for both casual meals and gatherings with friends or family.

One of the standout aspects of my visit was the staff. They were incredibly friendly and attentive, always ready to assist with any questions we had and ensuring our grill was at the right temperature throughout the meal. Their service was both efficient and personable, which added to the overall enjoyment of the experience.

The food, location, and service all combined to make my visit to 71 Mookata a memorable one. Whether you're new to mookata or a seasoned fan, I highly recommend giving this place a try – it’s the perfect spot for a delicious, interactive meal with great company.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: N (Princess)
review_text:
Known of this mookata place from few Thai food blogger but didn't have the chance to try it. We were craving for mookata, was contemplating between this or everyday mookata, silom branch as the google reviews are not really promising.
Long story short, we decided to come and not regret with our decision.

Meats and vegetables are fresh and soup is 👍🏻 (didn't feel thirsty after meal). In here, we prefer pork and chicken over beef.

Service is great even though there are language barrier. At least they will try to understand and fulfilled the customers' needs as best as they could👍🏻.

Interior is simple, clean and with aircon which is needed for Bangkok weather now.
This place is definitely under rated whereby it was full even on wet Sunday evening.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: welton seah
review_text: Delicious mookata sets with good quality and variety in cooling air-conditioning

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: S. M.
review_text: Slow service. Greasy plates and spoon. Taste was so-so, not the best Moo Kata that I've had. I was seated at a table located on the second floor; and my seat was right under the the air conditioner which was dripping with aircon water almost the entire time I was eating.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Nuch Suppanuch
review_text: Ok quality, reasonable price. Definitely a lot of MSGs in dipping sauce, but it’s expected. A bit long wait during dinner hour (~30 mins)

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Koonma Souriya
review_text: Service was great! Food was delicious! Very reasonable pricing! Staff were polite and fast service! Variety of ice cream!

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: LALIJING JJ
review_text: Original Thai hot pot , yummy and good services , staff are always welcome and take care of customers. Near MRT station.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Ni Nguyễn
review_text: It was good but not that’s good! MBK have a better Moo Krata (Better price and also better atmosphere)

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: OANH PHAM
review_text: I passed by this restaurent on my way to the Michellin Guide JeOh Chula. Why nobody talking about this mookata dish as a Thai food must try? The food is good, fresh and delicious. Though it’s quite noisy because of people talking and music but the service is 5/5. The staff stopped me from order another drink cuz I can get it refill lol. Btw, if you want to try Thai traditional dishes and want to try hot pot and drilled meat as the same time, give this a try.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Sharon
review_text:
We walked from MBK.
The place is good.
Staff try to understand us even we don't speak Thai. They are very kind and always help us what we need.
The food is also good. The source is spicy, but we can eat without it. Meats and vegetables are fresh too.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Pho Big Bowl
review_text: On my trip to Thailand I walked by this restaurant that seemed busy with many people inside eating. I decided to go in and give it a try and it was delicious. The dipping sauce was the highlight. I really enjoyed all the bbq here as well as the generous portions. The staff was very attentive and helpful. I would highly recommend to any one looking for a yummy spot to eat!

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Watachiwa Aungaung
review_text: I went there for dinner with friends the staff were so nice and the food was delicious.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Pattaratorn Karnchanapaisal
review_text: Best thai-style grills in town. Reasonable price and good taste. The queue might be long during meal time, but should try at least once.

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: HL
review_text: First time eating mookata. Got the $729 set just enough for 2 pax. Wish there were more type of sauces

restaurant: 71 mookata - สาขาบรรทัดทอง
author: Thant Cin
review_text: The meat, sauce and soup, everything’s so delicious. Service is also good and fast.

author: Chris Low
review_text:
Have been to Banthat Thong a number of times and finally have a chance to try this restaurant.

Omelet rice with shrimp taste really good. However, the eggs seems undercook to my liking. It was too watery. But overall tastes great! I will remind myself to inform the staff to cook it slightly longer on my next visit!

Shrimp noodles are really delicious!

Definitely coming back for more!

author: Kenny Yau
review_text: Great food and atmosphere. We ordered four dishes and none disappointed. Everything arrived promptly, packed with smoky wok hei, and tasted fantastic. Highlights included the pork and basil omelette, shrimp noodles, stir-fried chicken with rice, and the crispy pork neck. The only downside was that they were out of crab and salmon that day. Otherwise, I’d absolutely return - especially to try the crab omelette, since the eggs were incredibly creamy.

author: Abby Goldschmidt
review_text: The food here was awesome!! Our only complaints were that they were sold out of crab by 8 pm and that the amount of pork in the pork salad was too little. We loved it so much!!! Just wanted more pork but so worth it. We waited in line for 45 minutes which was a lot for a Monday night BUT we ate before which I highly recommend. I want to come back just to try the crab omelet because we got the shrimp one instead and it was amazing as well.

author: Sandra Shinn
review_text: Came here on Sat around lunchtime and was fortunate to find no queue. We ordered three dishes for two people, and the portion sizes were generous. Everything tasted excellent, and the service was quick. However, the fried rice wasn’t very hot, and I couldn’t tell if it had been pre-fried. Regardless, it still tasted great. Overall, a pleasant dining experience!

author: Adrick Loh
review_text: A highly rated restaurant (branch) along the famous Banthat Thong road. Nicely decorated but space is tight and noise level is high. Food wise is above average and price wise is alright for tourists. Just note that the large river prawn prices are high here. Service here is commended. Overall a good place for a meal.

author: i . am . kenny
review_text: Possibly the best Thai Omelette Rice in Bangkok. Eggy omelette is cream, watery and tasty, adding thick crab meat and prawns, this is simply amazing. They do not scrimp on the meat and every plate is valued for money. Beware..the waiting time and queue can be very long due to the limited space but you will feel satisfied after the meal. The seafood omelette can be slightly pricy but these are the recommended ones that you should try. Another thing to point out is the pork neck is soft, easy to bite and very good. Try if you have the stomach to eat them all. Do note that the toilet is on the 2nd floor just in case you need to go there.

author: BMWGal
review_text: Expected the creamy prawns to be the best dish but it wasn’t. The egg was creamy, the prawns were crunchy, I felt thirsty after the meal. The red curry soup was too spicy till it tasted like extra spicy chicken rice chill sauce. It felt more like a sauce than a soup. The staffs was not able to help us add any water nor provide and solution. We left without taking the soup. It’s was disappointing and wonder how did they get 4.9 in reviews.

author: Cheryl Lee
review_text: Food is on the spicy level here so u need to ask them to reduce the spice level if u can’t take too spicy! Their food is well flavored and cooked with lots of spice! Not a huge variety but worth waiting and eating while you are near this area. Staffs are efficient and food is served quickly despite a queue! Prices are reasonable too! Just that the place is not too big so be prepared to wait for awhile!

author: Marcel Chatenet
