review_text: First time there to catch with a friend. The food is very good, the only drawback is the noise. But eh!! Enjoy the food, and speak loader!! Good place to enjoy good food, having good mood experiencing Thai typical life.

author: Jovan Yeo
review_text:
Ordered 2 prawn based dishes and we were blown away.

The prawns in the fried noodles were fresh and succulent. Each mouthful of the noodles had the Thai garlic perfectly infused.

The egg in the omu fried rice was a tad watery but still pairs well with the rice and diced prawns.

As for the pork dish, the meat was tender but the sauce was too tangy and spicy to be consumed on its own.

Overall a thumbs up for the both of us, will be back for sure!

author: Nikireview
review_text:
This is hands down one of the best meals we had during our trip.

Our favorite dish was the fried noodles with fried pork. We were so lucky, we arrived at 6:15 PM and only waited around 15 minutes before getting a seat.

I will definitely come back to this place and recommend it to friends who are planning to visit Thailand.

The location is also very convenient, as it is close to many other famous food spots in the area.

author: Bugwagen
review_text:
Food was excellent, especially their prawn creamy rice.  We wanted the creamy crab but it was out of stock that day.  Hope to try it next time.

The large prawn dish was out of the menu, delicious but expensive.  Service was good.  We arrived just before noon and managed to get a table.  The place soon filled up cause it is not very big.  Few tables.

author: Komang Lestari
review_text:
Had a pleasant dining experience at Here Duan. I ordered the spicy deep fried pork neck salad and stir fried-rice seafood, the taste was well-seasoned and flavorful. The portion size was worth the price.
The place is comfortable, making it a nice spot for family meals.
Overall, a enjoyable experience, and I’d definitely consider coming back to try other dishes.

author: Kyle Olney
review_text:
Delicious Thai street food / brunch spot. Went back multiple times on our trip to Bangkok it was so good. The egg + rice base is definitely the way to go.

Gets *SUPER* busy at peak hours so go on a shoulder time if you want AC or be ready to sweat outside on the sidewalk.

author: S ZS
review_text: Came on Tuesday 8.40pm, waited about 15mins to be seated. Very disappointed cause only when we were seated, only were we informed that crab is out of stock. Rice dishes were served fairly quickly but it was barely warm, almost cold. Tasty.. But can't comprehend when is it not served freshly cooked kinda hot? Egg, rice and pork neck not even warm. No options available just to order omelette, it is only served with rice. Prawns were plump and fresh on the dish with basil garlic. Prawns were cut into small pieces in the other omelette rice. I don't think I'll return. Not worth the travel time unless your near by. Free herbal drink for every five star google review.

author: Christine Aaron
review_text: Came for the crab omelette and left FULLY satisfied. This place is absolutely amazing. I did not have to wait at all. Also the butterfly pea tea and chrysanthemum teas were so tasty and good for recovery after massage. Highly recommend stopping here when you’re in Bangkok.

author: Steve Tham
review_text: Place is cozy and nicest decorated for Christmas. Chose the spicy crab omelette and it was tasty. The fried pork neck was a surprise as it was chewy and fragrant. Unfortunately it was served lukewarm which could be improved.

author: Lee Zhao
review_text: The egg is wonderfully creamy and rich, living up to the hype for a premium street-food experience. The shrimp are large and generous, and while you noted they are firm, that confirms their freshness and quality, though a bit more tenderness would be a great touch. At around 390 THB, it’s a high price point, but the excellent taste and the trendy, clean atmosphere

author: Sweet Home
review_text: The food is very good, the reason I put one star because the table have a post said if you give 5 stars you will have one free drink. I really don’t like that. It is not fair to the restaurant around it. It should earn its star by offering good food. It earns 7000+ good reviews, I don’t know how many of them is because of the free drink.

author: Kenny Yap
review_text: Perfect date spot. Food was good but I wouldn’t say mindblowing. Didn’t have to reserve and manage to get seated immediately on a Wednesday evening. Favorite for me was the pork collar, followed by the crab, the egg, then the vermicelli. The salmon was a let down for me, the quality felt like it was frozen and recently thawed only so it was quite hard. I didn’t enjoy the sauce either it felt very bland.

author: Erica Quah
review_text:
if you're rethinking whether you should be queuing for so long, i say just queue, it's worth it but go on an empty stomach because you should feast here! also the queue wasnt as long as i thought considering there were 20 groups in front of us (this was at 3pm)
jumbo crab curry is a must buy, the portion of crab is bigger than other places i went to and the sauce was pretty good (i'm a big crab curry lover and this was the best i tried so far)
the tom yum soup was so good too, it was spicy enough and flavourful, kind of like a clear-my-sinuses spicy rather than a i-just-drank-fire spicy which was really nice!
the stir fry glass noodle with crab meat was also 10/10 ❤️

there's also a nice matcha place nearby (good cha matcha) if you need something to do while waiting

p.s. note their new year opening times

author: Ce Ce (Cece)
review_text:
The taste are good and I love the crab meat fried rice.

And the Tomyam shrimp 🦐 and the garlic mantis prawns surprisingly it was equally good 😊

With this quality and the portion they serve consider fair.

Recommended been there early to avoid the long Q. The restaurant only have limited seat.

If you want to skip the Q they also have Grab food delivery service 🚚

author: Quoc Dung Phan
review_text: Chula 50 Kitchen is a great spot for tasty food at reasonable prices. The dishes are flavorful and well worth the cost, especially considering its convenient location near Chulalongkorn University and the Banthat Thong food street. The place is quite popular, so it can get very crowded during peak hours, and you may need to queue. The space is small, which makes it a bit hot and noisy, but overall it’s a solid choice for a quick and satisfying meal

author: Gatsuka L
review_text:
No wait on a weekday morning just after 8am so we could choose our table. Prices are very affordable and the fried fish in bean sauce was fresh & tasty. Rice with fried pork and vegetable was good as wok's breath (wok hei) was present in the vegetables & good marinade in the pork.
But the crab meat on the curry and scrambled egg with rice was not as substantial as pics by others. There was also hardly curry taste. Soup with bamboo pith was chockful of bamboo pith, sliced shitake mushrooms and button mushrooms but it clearly tasted of artificial seasoning. Drinks tasted alright.
Maybe will visit again if I'm in the vicinity and need a quick bite as the rice dishes come out fast but will not queue for it.

author: O TW
review_text:
Another random spot we found that turned out to be quite famous in the area—probably among tourists too. We went for lunch and there was a long queue, but it moved fast. We waited around 20 minutes, though be prepared to stand under the hot sun.
The curry crab meat omelette is a must-try—creamy but not undercooked, and the curry fragrance isn’t overpowering. The tomyam is spicy in a good way. Overall, it’s worth it and not pricey.

author: Giang Tran
review_text:
I tried the crab omelette rice and was impressed by how plentiful and fresh the crab was. But the real star was the pork Pad Kaprao—it was super spicy, but the flavors were so incredible it essentially took me to heaven.
The place is usually quite crowded, but I got lucky and got a table within 10 minutes. It’s not the most convenient location to get to, but for food this good, I’d come back anytime. A must-visit if you're a fan of authentic, bold flavors!

author: Rbw dinata
review_text:
So many option of interesting crab-based menu, so I picked rice with a combination of creamy omelette with crab and stir-fried crab curry, on one plate.
Tastewise, indeed their cream and curry just like two pole crashed in your mouth. Each of it gave a specific taste and sensation, so soft yet tasty, full of flavor.
The crab meat itself is generous, fresh and no fishy aroma at all. All is perfect to me.
And for all this satisfaction the price is no more than THB 100. Hands down!
Despite of horrible crowded customer, they apply a good and orderly queu system, so no extreme long wait even on lunch hour.
Highly recommended.

author: Elyse
review_text:
Small space only and full of tourists when peak dining hours. Good value for the money, but you have to queue patiently for a while. There are coffee shops nearby in case you wanna buy drinks and wait up.

Dine-in order process: Get menu from a staff to write down your order>>Hand over your order to a staff and get your queue number badge>>Waiting. You will see an electrical board on wall showing the latest queue number for dine-in.

author: HL Yap
review_text:
The Google review you read are real and genuine. All their food are so great! We have a take away ordered through Grab and the serving are professional and generous. The take away is nicely packed.

Jumbo crab curry and Jumbo crab glass noodle is must try items from menu

author: c c
review_text:
This restourant is famous within Chinese tourists which makes it difficult to wait for a table. After 15 minutes waiting, you will find out waiting is not the hardest part to bear. Table for two at the end of the corridor is too narrow and cramped.
Speaking of the dishes, we ordered curry crab with rice and deep fried prawn mantis. The flavour of crab is heavy sweet which make me dizzy. And the mantis is as common as any restourant can offer.
Remember price is the only reason you come to this restourant and dont expect too much. Every coin matters.

author: Lynley Niu
review_text:
Delicious and worth it! 🦀
Crab meat comes ready to eat, no shells. The curry powder flavor is rich, creamy, and so tasty. Perfect with rice. Great value and a must try! 💯

author: Stefano Gentile
review_text:
Found this small restaurant - not really a hidden gem - on Google Maps, apparently quite popular, since I’m staying in a nearby Airbnb, and definitely it deserves all its praise.
I did not have to wait in line (went Friday around 9h45), the restaurant was practically empty.
I ordered the mix (N.8?) curry scrambled eggs and normal scrambled eggs with rice, as well as Thai milk tea. Prices are very reasonable too!
In short, it was delicious, very recommended if you stay in the area.

author: Harvey
review_text:
Coconut juice was refreshing. Seafood tom yum was spicy, creamy and rich. Crab omelette and crab fried rice was pretty average.
Be prepared to wait in a long queue as this is a popular tourist spot and vloggers often come to try out the cuisine.

author: Jowe Chu
review_text:
A little underwhelming. Please dun be mistaken, the food is alright but the ingredients are really not top notch. From online review I had the expectations of chunky crab but all the small portions turned out to be sprinkling of crab meat.

Ordered a small crab with bee hoon, small crab with egg and the creamy tom yum seafood soup.

Pretty tasty but dun expect restaurant standards.

author: peter liew
review_text:
Reach the restaurant about 1830, there is queue but you don't have to wait very long.
You placed your order first and you will be given a queue number. You paid after you finish your meal.
The price is very reasonable and you get big chunky crab meat. The food is tasty.
Do take note that the last order is at 7pm. You can continue your meal and they will only closed when all guests have finished.
I highly recommend giving a try.

author: Chon Picha
review_text: The food is really delicious. Each dish comes in a big portion. There are a lot of people lining up. It's close to Chulalongkorn University. If you're visiting Bangkok, you definitely should try it!!

author: newchicgal
review_text:
14 Jun 2025, Saturday, 2.20pm to 2.55 pm waiting time. Long Queue.
After being seated, another period of waiting. I think I will only get my food after 1 hour from the time I get a number. Come on weekdays!
I am ordering Fish Maw Soup with Crab Meat 120 baht, Jumbo Fried Rice with Crab Meat 380 baht and water 10 baht.
Food is only 3 stars today. Fish Maw Soup with Crab Meat is too salty and has less ingredients than yesterday. Jumbo Fried Rice with Crab Meat is very wet today, not nice, like it is being cooked by an apprentice. I will not visit again after the inconsistent food quality on both visits. 3 stars for today's food.

13 Jun 2025, Friday, 9.30am
There's menu and order form in English & Thai. I ordered the Fish Maw Soup with Crab Meat 120 baht. It is slightly sour, very nice, not too salty. I also ordered the Crab in Curry and Omelet 380 baht. Unfortunately, I only ate the crab, the curry isn't to my liking, I left it untouched. I later ordered the Jumbo Fried Rice with Crab Meat Fried Rice 380 baht, asking for less rice but they don't understand English so I still get a big plate that's double the size of usual small Thai serving. The Crab Meat Fried Rice is sooooo much better than the curry dish! Skip the curry crab that's hard and messy to eat. Just this fried rice dish is enough. Thai tea 35 baht is nice but too sweet unless you wait for all ice to melt. Overall, it's a great meal, worth 5 stars. Cash only.

author: Travel Coffee Andy
review_text:
This local Thai food restaurant, nestled just a stone’s throw away from Samyan Mitrtown, offers a delightful dining experience despite its modest amenities. While there’s no air conditioning, the shared bathroom within the complex, and limited seating, the food is simply fantastic. They boast a wide array of freshly prepared dishes featuring a delightful combination of crab meat, shrimp, pork, chicken, and an assortment of vegetables.

The staff, though limited in their English proficiency, are incredibly helpful and attentive. However, it’s essential to note that they only accept cash or QR codes, so ensure you have sufficient cash for your visit.

author: KA YA
review_text: It's been a while since I last visited, but it's still as delicious as ever. It was a weekday, so I was able to get in easily before lunchtime. I think you can only get such delicious Kupatpong curry at this price here.

author: Leanne Kwek
review_text:
We went there around 3pm so there is not much queue, we order and got seated in around 10minutes. i order a rice w/ minced pork basil but it does not taste any spicy at all, just pure salty. My friend order a rice w/creamy omelette & crab, dont know why but the omelette has a very fishy smell.
And we order a stir fried crab curry to share, it taste just normal. Not worth it if need to queue.

author: bo seo
review_text: Today, my mother and I had lunch at Thong Smith, Siam Paragon. If you're looking for premium boat noodles with pork, beef and shredded chicken that are delicious, rich, and well-balanced, I highly recommend this place. The price is a bit on the high side, but I feel it's worth it. The service is also excellent, polite, and attentive. I visited between 1:00 and 2:00 PM, and there were already tables available, so I didn't have to wait in line for long. My order arrived fairly quickly, neither too slow nor too fast. The taste was as good as ever. I frequently eat at Thong Smith, at the branch near my house, and I've always enjoyed their food and service. I hope the brand maintains this same high-quality food and service.

author: I
review_text:
I've tried Boat noodles on several occasions in Thailand and whilst I found it ok, I didn't really enjoy it all that much.  Intrigued by the long queues, I tried another Thong Smith branch (CentralWorld) and loved it.  This review is for my most recent visit 2 weeks ago in Siam Paragon.

We went here for dinner at 6pm and there was a sizeable queue.  They have a number system where you get a ticket, and your number will be displayed on a monitor (and they will call it out) when your turn is up.  We probably had a 20 minute wait so it wasn't too bad.

We ordered the following:
Beef Boat Noodle with Ox Tongue, Beef Ball, Sliced Beef, Braised Shank and tendon.  This was excellent, with the soup having a deep, rich taste.  The assorted toppings were plentiful and there was also plenty of chopped vegetables in the dish.  This dish is the reason to come here and it did not disappoint.

Chicken Noodles with clear soup.  My son chose this dish and found it very tasty.  The soup was clean and refreshing, which was perfect as he was feeling a bit under the weather at the time.  Nothing like Chicken Soup to make you feel better!

Pork Boat Noodle without soup - Braised pork, pork ball, sliced pork.  My wife chose this dish as she is not a fan of the blood contained in the soup.  The dish was good, with the noodles being nice and chewy, and toppings being tasty.

One thing to note is that we also ordered a little plate of Crispy pork fat, which are these wonderful bits of crunchy lard that add incredible flavourful taste to every bite you have.  Highly recommended.

This restaurant chain is a favourite of mine and I will make it a point to return on any subsequent visits to Thailand.

author: Michelle
review_text:
I came here for my birthday breakfast and arrived right when they opened, so there was no line at all.

I ordered the beef boat noodles with egg noodles and spicy soup (menu with end number of 3). Honestly, I was surprised by how much meat they gave, very generous. The broth was rich and flavorful, and the spice level was just right. It’s spicy but not the kind that hurts your stomach later. I also ordered the Teddy Palm Juice, which was really good. The sweetness was perfectly balanced.

The service was great too. I didn’t catch the waitress’s name, I think her name tag said either “Ye” or “Yo.” When my noodles arrived, she noticed I hadn’t started eating yet and checked to see if everything had been served. I told her I was still waiting for my drink, and she quickly followed up with the kitchen. A few minutes later, my drink arrived.

Overall, great food, great service, and a nice atmosphere. Definitely worth the price!

author: Eddie Khoo
review_text:
🥢 Thong Smith Siamese Boat Noodles – A Premium Twist on a Thai Classic

Thong Smith offers an upscale take on traditional Thai boat noodles, known for their rich, flavorful broth and high-quality ingredients. Located in prime Bangkok malls like Siam Paragon, CentralWorld, and EmQuartier, it’s a go-to spot for locals and tourists looking to enjoy comfort food in a clean, air-conditioned setting.

✅ What’s Great
• Deep, savory broth: Thick and full-bodied, especially the beef broth—intensely aromatic with hints of spices.
• Premium meats: Choose from Wagyu beef, marbled pork, tenderloin, or Kurobuta. Meat is usually tender and well-cooked.
• Customisable noodles: Various noodle types (rice, egg, vermicelli) and soup bases (beef or pork).
• Crispy pork rinds & garlic toppings: Add satisfying crunch and aroma.
• Sides like fried wontons and grilled pork neck also shine.

⚠️ What to Note
• Price is higher than typical street stalls (expect around 150–300 baht per bowl).
• Small portions – more suited for tasting or sharing, not for big appetites.
• Some find the broth too salty, especially in the beef version.

💬 Verdict
If you’re after a clean, modern setting with gourmet-quality Thai boat noodles, Thong Smith is worth a visit. While it may not have the rustic charm of a boat-side stall, it makes up for it with quality ingredients, great presentation, and reliable service.

author: Mischa Ngan
review_text: Always feeling stress that the soup will soak up by the noodle as not much soup is given and the magical soup is the soul of this noodle. Yet, it still tastes so good that i always come back. Great ingredients. Amazing service, the waitresses are so considering, with great attitude. The iced milk tea less sugar is amazing too!

author: Average Guy
review_text:
Good, will come again if I’m in the area. But I don’t think I will make a special trip just to have this.
One thing is for sure, the beef tendons were very very soft. Loved them. But I thought the beef balls were just normal.

author: Aileen Chin
review_text: Thong Smith is a chain of restaurants that’s easy to find in many shopping malls. Prices are reasonable, and you can mix and match your bowl with pork or beef, different noodle types, and your preferred level of spiciness. Available in both dry or soup versions, the boat noodles are simple, traditional and tasty — great for a quick and satisfying meal.

author: Air Tree Water
review_text:
They offer traditional Thai-style noodles, including beef, pork, and chicken. I highly recommend the beef version. Although a bowl of noodles costs over 200 THB, which seems a bit expensive—about twice the price of regular affordable noodles—you’ll find that the ingredients are truly excellent. Both the noodles and the meat have a smooth texture, and the noodles have just the right level of chewiness.

In terms of portion size, an average adult might need 1.5 to 2 bowls to feel full, even when paired with side dishes and condiments.

For dessert, I highly recommend the green noodle-like dessert in the photo—it’s incredibly delicious.

Because their on-site queue and ordering process isn’t very smooth and has significant room for improvement, I didn’t give full marks for staff service. However, the food and location are absolutely impeccable.

author: Mauro Martin
review_text: Thong Smith at Siam Paragon offers an elevated take on classic Thai boat noodles. The broth is the clear standout-deep, aromatic, and intensely savory, simmered to a rich concentration without feeling heavy. You can choose from pork, beef, or mixed toppings, all tender, well-portioned, and noticeably high in quality. The noodles have a satisfying bite, while the seasoning is well-balanced with herbs and chili-bold yet refined. The freshness of the bean sprouts and leafy greens adds a crisp, clean contrast, balancing the richness of the broth and perfectly completing the dish. Portions are smaller than traditional street-style bowls, but this allows you to enjoy multiple variations or pair them with side dishes and light Thai desserts. Service is efficient despite the crowd, and the atmosphere is polished yet comfortable-ideal for both a quick lunch and a relaxed mall dinner. Overall: A premium, well-executed interpretation of a Thai classic with consistent quality and depth of flavor-a must-visit for boat noodle lovers in Bangkok.

author: Ray Liu
review_text: Thong Smith serves one of the best boat noodles in Bangkok, upgraded with premium ingredients and rich, flavorful broth. The pork boat noodles are a highlight—deeply satisfying with tender meat, crispy toppings, and just the right spice. Cozy seating with a great view inside Siam Paragon makes it perfect for a casual yet elevated local dining experience. Their grilled meatballs and crispy wonton sides are also worth trying. Fast service, clean space, and fair prices. A must-visit for noodle lovers exploring central Bangkok.

author: june netikosol
review_text: The best boat noodle ever!!! Rich flavor. They give a lot of meat verses noodle portion

author: Kasemsan Predaboon
review_text: Amazing Thai noodles served with high quality ingredients. Strongly recommend to order beef tongue. Very soft as if it could melt in your mouth!

author: A T
review_text:
ทอสมิทธ์ is undeniably a gem among the many noodle shops in Bangkok. Known for its widespread popularity, this place consistently delivers exceptional food that reflects the chef's meticulous attention to detail, right down to the carefully crafted condiments that accompany each dish. As a Thai person, I can confidently say this is how a boat noodle shop should be.

I highly recommend trying the beef ball with spicy sauce—it's truly delightful. While the overall experience is wonderful, I'd love to see the noodles served a bit hotter and with more soup. The pricing reflects a more upper-class noodle experience, but I find it well worth it for the quality and authenticity offered.

Overall, ทองสมิทธ์ captures the essence of Thai boat noodles with finesse and flair.

author: Danny Ng
review_text: This is one of my checklist whenever I visit Bangkok, hence it was no exception when I was here on the 3rd September 2025. Never failed me and love the umami from the beef broth, choice of Angus Beef and other cuts too. Highly recommend anyone should try not because the influencer said so, this is really authentic beef broth and not super expensive.

author: Janez Y
review_text: Nice, rich broth for Thai boat noodle soup. The beef is fresh and tender, and the chili adds a perfect spicy kick. Only downside is the constant queue and slightly pricey noodles. Still worth trying if you’re craving bold flavors.

author: Connie Chan
review_text: The boat noodles come with various options, beef, pork or chicken. We went with the beef with original noodles. We chose spice level 2 which was super spicy. Spice level 1 would have been sufficient. The wagyu beef was tender, but even the “normal” beef was good. The side dishes were great. We had fried wanton, spicy dumpling and beef balls. We repeat the orders as they were so good!!

author: Ed Wong
review_text: Hands down our favorite boat noodles spot in Bangkok! The only thing we wished for is if the soup that comes with the noodles can be a little more generous!

author: Ronrapee Leelawong
review_text:
The boat noodles are good - taste good and authentic, beef quality is perfect (no need to pay extra for the wagyu, the ordinary one is good enough.) Bigger portion than the typical boat noodles, so beware of over-ordering them. Grilled beef balls and dee fried wontons are also good. Kanhom-tuay is also great - not too sweet and creamy.

The service is quite slow, and the queue is super looooonnnggg.

Be aware that the price is excrutiating!!! Around 4 times over the normal boat noodles.

author: constantly penat
review_text:
combination of their flavourful broth and the tender wagyu is top-notch, worth the hype and the slightly higher price

service was great, no queue at all as we went 4pm on a weekday

author: Vanessa A.
review_text: We ordered pork noodle soup, Thai boat noodles (beef), dry pork noodles, and pork balls and they did not disappoint! The broth was super thick and flavorful and the springy noodles and toppings complemented the broth well. Portion-wise, a bowl is enough for one person, or even two people if you don't eat much.

author: bo seo
review_text: Today, my mother and I were strolling around Siam Paragon and wanted to find something to eat. We wanted Thai food, and we thought of Nara Thai Cuisine cuz it's a really good Thai restaurant. The staff were welcoming, polite, and very courteous to us, their customers. The interior and dining tables were excellent, making for a comfortable meal without feeling like the meal was over. However, the food might take a little while to prepare. But that's okay, because the food came out one dish at a time, so I could eat continuously without getting too full. The food has a rich, authentic Thai flavor, but not overly spicy. The seasoning is balanced, making it suitable for both Thais and foreigners. And of course, if I crave delicious Thai food again, my family and I will definitely think of Nara Thai Cuisine.

author: Bernie H
review_text: Very nice traditional thai restaurant. The service is very good and thoughtfull. Good decoration, and they have plenty seating, so basically no wait even so we have reservation for our lunchtime. They also have many other location, so its easily accessible for people wanting to taste the good thai cuisine.

author: Tuy Chanmonypech
review_text:
The experience can be described as opulent, given the cost and the elegant decor.

The cost of the food could be considered somewhat greater. Their menu features a variety of Thai cuisine.

The service was decent, although the food can take a while to arrive, and it tends to be busy regularly.

The food was acceptable, but I really enjoy their stir-fried crab with yellow curry, papaya salad, and deep-fried seabass. The serving size is quite small. Their mango sticky rice is likely the standout dessert on the menu.

All in all, this spot is a great choice for top-notch Thai cuisine.

author: Frederique De Sousa
review_text:
Nice restaurant located in Siam Paragon.

They have calm indoor seating.

Food were really tasty and delicious. They have as well a vegetarian menu. Price is on the higher side however good quality and portion.

Staff is very professional and kind

author: Haley Phan
review_text: The menu looks great, with proper presentation and manners. The service is quick and polite. The Pad Thai and papaya salad are delicious. I especially love the Thai iced milk tea and the coconut cake. I’ll definitely come back to try other dishes.

author: Alan Goh
review_text: Had the best meal in Bangkok at Nara Siam Paragon. Wonderful high quality food, superb service and nice restaurant ambience. The coconut cake dessert was out of this world. They only had 10 servings per day.

author: Tze Keong Choo
review_text: Had dinner here on Thursday evening before 6pm, assigned seats on Level 2. Service from Top was top-notch, helped us with carrying our bags up and attentive to our needs. Food was great and highlights were the beef in fish sauce and satay!

author: Ardi Tjitra
review_text:
I ordered a few dishes for a family of 7.

I can't give 5 ⭐ because I found the food is a bit oily especially the fried rice. Taste is okay, nothing stand out to be honest.

Price is at a higher level. Spent about THB6K for the food shown.

author: Ticha Pescod
review_text: We dined here twice during our stay in Bangkok and both times were a great experience. Firstly we found it by chance hidden away in the north west corner of Siam paragon floor M. The staff were friendly and attentive and the menu had photos and English descriptions so it was easy to find what you wanted. There are some impressively visual dishes and the coconut dessert is a unique and tasty option. The second time we booked a table and took a friend as there were lots of options. Well worth a visit if you want an extra special experience.

author: Sharmaine T
review_text: Great service and lovely ambience. The food was served well and on time. However, overall the dishes were a tad salty. The sticky rice with the fried chicken wing was dry and slightly undercooked, and the whole crab in the vermicelli dish wasn’t very fresh. The yellow curry crab also had noticeably less meat compared to our previous visit. We’d still like to give the CentralWorld outlet a try next time.

author: Leonis Minoris
review_text: I had a wonderful dining experience at Nara Thai. The staff were warm, attentive, and made us feel very welcome throughout the meal. The food was absolutely delicious – full of authentic Thai flavors, beautifully presented, and cooked to perfection. The restaurant’s environment was also lovely, with a cozy yet elegant atmosphere that made the meal even more enjoyable. Overall, it was an excellent experience, and I’ll definitely be coming back again.

author: Jufie
review_text: Whenever I visit Bangkok I always make it a point to eat at one of the Nara locations. I’ve been to this location a few times and I’ve always been impressed with the food. My personal favourite is the yellow curry with crab. Overall would highly recommend to anyone who wants to try upscaled, elevated Thai cuisine.

author: Htoo Shwe Yee Win Elleri
review_text: Absolutely loved this Thai cuisine restaurant! The food was very delicious, authentic, and full of rich flavors. The atmosphere was warm, lively, and welcoming, perfect for casual dining.

author: Jason Mendoza
review_text: Amazing Thai food, the quality is exceptional with so much flavour. The ambience is also very classy with great luxurious touches. The staff were also very attentive and knowledgeable.

author: Karissa Alberto
review_text: Their pad thai was so good. The highlight though was the fried chicken. It’s tender and flavourful just by itself. The salted egg calamari was also so good. Would recommend

author: antonius
review_text: The food, the staffs, and the place are all amazing! Various options of thai food are also available, especially if you’re not into spicy food.  They were also giving crackers as a complimentary while waiting for the food to come. Very recommended. 👍🏻

author: Saowanee Paweenwich
review_text: Nara Restaurant, the original and traditional Thai foods are very delicious. The staff are nice and well-trained. The atmosphere is great. Reasonable price with good quality.

author: Zhi Ting
review_text: Awesome location with great warm services. The people there tend to our need greatly and changes our disposal bowl of food scrap very promptly. All food we ordered was on point albeit too much for two. Great meal to start our bkk trip!

author: Lance L
review_text:
Good food, consistent quality.
Dishes are well-balanced, not overly sweet, and portions are decent.
Service is professional and efficient, especially considering it’s inside Siam Paragon.
A reliable choice for Thai cuisine in a mall setting.

author: Yi Ling Lai
review_text: Whenever I visit Bangkok, Nara Thai is a must have. The yellow curry soft shell crab and creamy tom yummy goong are my go to. Great service, great food, always happy to be back

author: Jayesh Nema
review_text:
After You Dessert Café at CentralWorld is an absolute paradise for anyone with a sweet tooth. The moment you step in, the aroma of freshly baked treats and the sight of their iconic desserts instantly tempts you into ordering more than you planned. Their Shibuya Honey Toast, Kakigori, and seasonal specials are nothing short of awesome and delicious—beautifully presented, consistently rich in flavour, and worth every calorie. This is the kind of place where every bite feels like a warm hug, and it’s easy to see why it’s a favourite among locals and tourists alike.

That said, be prepared for a bit of patience. Service tends to be slow, especially during peak hours, and the café often struggles with managing the heavy footfall it attracts. The staff can come across as rude or indifferent, which can feel a bit disappointing considering the high expectations the brand sets. Long queues and slightly chaotic crowd handling are fairly common.

Still, despite these drawbacks, the desserts remain the hero—so good that they almost make up for everything else. If you’re willing to overlook the service and the rush, the taste and quality of the treats make a visit totally worthwhile. After You at CentralWorld is definitely a must-stop for dessert lovers—just go in with patience, and you’ll walk out smiling (and full). 🍰✨

author: Sandra Tam
review_text: I definitely get the hype over this! The Thai milk tea shaved ice was really refreshing and true to its name as there was sticky rice hidden within the shaved ice, alongside generous servings of cubed mango. Their Shibuya toast continues to impress even though it has been around for a long time. I came with my partner so was particularly appreciative of the fact that they had mini sizes of their desserts available which allow us to try multiple items without wastage.

author: Chanya Anu
review_text: I ordered the cheddar cheese toast and it was absolutely delicious! The butter was rich and perfectly balanced, giving the toast a wonderful flavor. I also enjoyed the ice cream and whipped cream — both were fresh and creamy, making the whole experience even better. The atmosphere at After You Central World is cozy, and the staff are friendly and attentive. The wait was a bit long, but the food was worth it and easy to forgive. Definitely a place I’d recommend for anyone looking for a sweet treat or a relaxing break in the city.

author: Ali Alyammahi
review_text:
If you’re in Bangkok and love desserts, this place is a must visit. The menu offers both local and Korean inspired favorites like kakigori. The atmosphere is clean, perfect for cooling off after a long day of shopping. You can find branches in all the main malls in central bangkok.

Mango Sticky Rice Bingsu 8.7/10 ❤‍🔥
Original Milk Bun 8.5/10 ❤‍🔥
Nutella Bun 8.5/10 ❤‍🔥
Strawberry Bingsu 6/10
Honey Toast 7/10

author: Thiha Lu Lin
review_text: One of the top dessert cafes in Thailand. But taking some time to get a table. Maybe this branch is the busiest one in Bangkok. The food is quite pricey. You can have some free cold green tea here.

author: Loh Kwai Yin
review_text:
Pretty tasty food and drink. Interesting concept/ presentation for some of the dessert.
It was a bit rush the counter as the cashier expected us to be familiar with the items on the menu, and therefore able to place order very quickly.
The atmosphere would certainly be elevated if the servers served with a smile.

author: Susan Chai
review_text: Finally got to have it again after so long — I’ve missed it so much! 🥹💛 Tried their baby-size Hojicha this time — it’s just too cute! Even though it was crowded, it didn’t feel rushed at all; the staff managed everything so well 👍🏼Plus, they offer complimentary tea for customers — love the thoughtful touch! Definitely recommend 💫

author: Winniebear
review_text:
Wouldn’t come back here for dessert, but that’s only my preference. Ice shaven is bingsu quality but lacked flavor. Rating this a 3 since I only tried one.
Serving time took long also, 15 minutes but they did communicate this while ordering.

author: Ei Phyu Sin
review_text: The durian sticky rice bun is the best of all! Inside, there’s a soft, chewy sticky rice paste, and the bun itself is incredibly fluffy. The cream on top is rich, smooth, and full of that signature durian flavor — absolutely delicious!

author: Kanoon Siri
review_text: Personally, for the mango sticky rice bingsu, the coconut sauce was too salty that day. 🥹 (I’ve tried this menu at other branches and it wasn't salty there

author: Moshi J.
review_text:
“Sweet Treats Worth the Hype”

The After You café at CentralWorld’s 2nd floor (across from the Apple Store) may be smaller, but it has a major advantage—no queue! Meanwhile, the larger 7th-floor branch often has a wait, but both locations serve the same iconic desserts. I tried the baby-sized mix-flavor Kagikori and their famous Honey Toast, and both were excellent. The Honey Toast, while served with a honey-syrup blend, still nailed the perfect balance of sweetness. They even provide complimentary cold tea, a nice touch to cleanse the palate. The decor is cozy, and the staff is attentive. Note: it’s cashless, so have your card or app ready. Although prices lean on the higher side, the quality justifies it. Expect a short wait for your order even if there’s no line. Great spot for dessert without the usual hassle.

author: Fauzia D. Andani
review_text:
This place in the corner near of BTS train and serves really delicious food and has some of the best pastries we’ve had in Bangkok – fresh, flavorful, and clearly made with care.

Ofc we try milk bun, which was super refreshing and definitely worth a try.

The space itself is a bit tight and can feel a little hectic, especially during busy hours, so seating might feel slightly cramped.

That said, the quality of the food and pastries makes it a place we’d absolutely recommend!

author: Skidamarink a Dink a Dink
review_text:
Food is unique and delicious
Service is good, although theres almost always a waiting time
Atmosphere - good, almost similar in all locations, some spacious and some not
Price - a bit costly compared to local prices

+ they provide 2 kinds of free tea water
+ milk bread is also good

author: Rah
review_text:
Super pricey dessert but worth a try since it’s viral.
Kakigori is a mango sticky rice in bingsu style
Milk bun portion is hugeeee there’s 6 pieces inside but they packed it in takeaway boxes :)
Service is good too

author: Su Myat Kyi Sin
review_text: It worths the hype and the flavor the texture are amazing. Even the simple ice cream was so good that the taste was so smooth. The durian rice bun was the highlight of the show as well. It was around 200-300 baht around for one item.  But definitely you can share and try because of big portions.

author: GG K
review_text:
Finally tried this highly raved about dessert cafe in Bangkok and I did think it was not bad, but not worth a queue.

We got the mango sticky rice kakigori and the salted egg yolk cold buns. The flavours of both were pretty good, but were still a bit too sweet for me. I enjoyed how finely the ice was shaved for the kakigori, and the chunks of mango and sticky rice inside it, which helped in making the overall dessert less icy. I do think it could be improved by changing out the cream they drizzled on top and provided on the side into unsweetened coconut cream. The buns were pretty nice as well, though again the salted egg yolk filling was a tad too sweet. Additionally, it would be good if the portion could be smaller as 6 rather big buns per pack is quite a lot.

Overall, not a bad place for dessert, but definitely not worth the long queue that is nearly forever present at this place. We came at around 6pm and still had to wait for a while before getting a seat, so do try to avoid peak hours or the wait might take quite a while.

author: Lim Lim
review_text: The Shibuya toast takes quite a while to be served, but it’s worth the wait—the taste is as great as always. However, the price is slightly on the higher side.

author: arjun adinata
review_text: After a thousand of miles from my place, finally can taste a most popular dessert place in Bangkok. Well known with their milk bund fluffy bread, I prefer to give another things to try. Surprisingly good, their dessert is beyond my expectations. I was skeptical because they are too viral and hype at the moment. But I was totally wrong, their taste is amazing. They also provide free drink which is great after a heavy sugar load hahahaha. Can’t wait to back to this place soon 😋

author: Agus Santoso
review_text:
Finally got to try the original milk bun that used to be super popular in Thailand! Honestly, it tastes so different from the ones sold in Indonesia. It’s really soft and delicious, but I couldn’t eat too much—it gets a bit heavy.

As for the drinks, I think the prices are a bit on the expensive side

author: Hieu Trong
review_text:
After you is one of the most famous dessert shop in Thailand, its really good, reasonable price too.

The bingsu and toast or some more drinks are quality, its taste unique in each one. The size is not too big so everyone can try numerous plate at one time.

author: Coriandermixxx
review_text:
We decided to have our very first lunch in Bangkok at Inter Restaurant. Getting there was simple — just stop at Siam BTS and take a short walk.
Even though it was a Monday, there was already a line of people waiting to be seated. Upon arrival, don’t forget to mention your name and the number of guests to the waitress. We waited about 10–15 minutes before being seated.

The menu was straightforward, though many pages were worn out — some pictures and dish names were faded or erased.

We ordered: Spring roll, Crab omelette, Creamy tom yum, Thai tea. and Two white rice bowls (for 2 pax)

Final Verdict :
1. 🥟Spring Roll & 🧋 Thai Tea – 3/5 Not particularly special, but a nice appetizer to start the meal.

2. 🦀Crab Omelette – 4/5 Generous portion! Served on hot stones which kept it warm. Crispy outside, soft inside — very satisfying.

3. 🍲Creamy Tom Yum – 5/5 Perfectly creamy and spicy, yet light enough to make me crave more rice. Absolutely delicious!

Our first lunch in Bangkok was truly lovely thanks to Inter Restaurant. I was initially skeptical about the name, but in the end, it was worth it. The price wise is very cheap for lunch at a decent restaurant 💕💕

author: Jason Oh
review_text:
Still the best value & delicious Thai food restaurant in Bangkok for a long time.
We always visit Inter, good location after visiting Siam Paragon shopping centre to look at all the high end vehicles on display in retail shops on top floor.
Walk across to Siam Square to check out local arts & crafts stalls, enjoy lunch or dinner at Inter, then walk to MBK shopping centre to check out  “CHATUCHAK weekend market” style sellers in an air conditioned shopping centre for you to negotiate lowest prices 7 days a week.

author: Max N
review_text:
Visited on a Sunday afternoon around lunch time and the place was crowded with a short line of 5-6 parties lining up outside.

As we were a couple, we didn't have to wait too long (10-15 min). We were pleasantly surprised that the prices were very wallet friendly, as we were expecting it to be wildly expensive for a well-established restaurant like this one.

We got a Tom yum soup, som tum, basil pork, pad see ew and Thai ice milk tea (not pictured) Unfortunately I didn't not take a photo of the menu, and I can't recall how much we spent on this meal. It was definitely affordable for a meal of this proportion.

The service was quick and my ice milk tea arrived shortly. I found the tea taste to be strong, combined with the milky condensed milk  and evaporated milk. However it was a tad too sweet for liking.

The somtum was delicious, with the right amount of spice and tang to whet your appetite. The crunchy texture of the veg provided an excellent contrast to the pad see ew I had. The rice noodles were stir fried with a proper wok,  smoky and savoury. The Tom yum soup was creamy, sour and spicy. There were plenty of fresh ingredients such as mushrooms and seafood.

My partner had the basil pork rice and said it was an okay plate. But would have preferred more basil and for it to be less wet (his personal preference).

Overall we had a good meal at Inter Restaurant, would recommend for anyone who's nearby and looking a good lunch spot that has a wide menu of Thai food.

author: Bárbara Gregório
review_text:
The place is ok
Just accept cash
The flavour was really good but unfortunately I paid for less than 100g of chicken.
I received cashew nuts with chicken instead the opposite.
I tried to explain to staff but no one helped or not even offered a discount, anything.
Probably it is standard.

author: Tuong Vi
review_text: A friend recommended this place to me, and it did not disappoint. The food is reasonably priced, although the portions are a bit small — but the flavors totally make up for it. Every dish was well-seasoned and delicious. The staff were friendly and attentive. It gets quite busy at lunchtime, and they open at 11 AM. Conveniently located within walking distance of nearby shopping areas, so it’s definitely worth a try.

author: Tom S
review_text: Nostalgic family diner kinda restaurant, always with a queue of locals. Prices decent for the area. Catfish curry is outstanding. Laab was well seasoned. Papaya salad was great and funky with fermented fish/squid. Cheap iced tea. Two can be filled for 450 bht including 4 plates + rice + drinks.

author: Shibu Mattummal
review_text:
Local Delicacy!

Love their food. Tasty, healthy and reasonably priced. There is a lot in the menu to choose from.

It's located in Siam Square walk street. Easy and convenient to get in. But expect a long queue to get the seat during peak hours. The friendly staff will help you.

author: Joseph Zhi Wei Heah
review_text:
Overall it's a fuss free quick service restaurant. Food is not bad. There's a queue about 3pm. Food came fast. Prices are affordable for the masses.

Fried wide noodles w beef - beef was overcooked and chewy. Noodles seasoning was a little bland.

Minced pork basil - a little salty, can't taste the basil.

Tom yum soup chicken - flavorful and chicken meat was tender. Recommend.

Som tum - tasty. Recommend.

Phad Thai - taste average.

author: Chanaporn Yamjinda
review_text: I ordered fried rice with egg. It tasted very delicious and had the aroma of a wok, which reminded me of my childhood. It only cost 68 baht, a price that is hard to find in the Siam area.

author: Yugeizhumi
review_text: Inter Restaurant is a true gem for authentic Thai cuisine! Everything we ordered was delicious and full of flavor. The deep-fried tofu was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside, while the fried chicken wings were golden, crunchy, and well-seasoned. The portions were generous, and the price was reasonable for the quality. The restaurant has a casual and nostalgic charm, making it a great spot for a comforting meal.

author: M *
review_text:
This restaurant in Siam has been around for quite some time. They offer a variety of single-dish options and some ala carte menus for sharing. The food is tasty and flavorful. The noodles we ordered were okay, with a decent portion size, but the prawns were few only. The taste was adequate.

This place is a good option for a quick meal, especially since it’s near school and Siam. However, it can get crowded sometimes. The prices are reasonable.

author: Tom Maier
review_text: Very friendly stuff, authentic restaurant and very delicious food! We had pad krapao, pineapple fried rice and wing bean salad! Totally recommend!

author: Sann Wai Linn
review_text: A REALLY NICE RESTAURANT with a various cuisine. Its very affordable price to eat even in the busy area. Have 2 floor to dine in. Tried pineapple fried rice, Tom yum goong and duck meal, which taste are very great. MUST TRY in that area to have a dine in experience. In the ground floor you can see the busy kitchen operating with your own eyes beside the busy road filled with students. Cost only 485 baht for 3 people eating.

author: Thu Ho
review_text: Best Thai restaurant ever, and super cheap. The queue is long though. They wrote our names down and we had to wait for nearly an hour for a table but there were plenty of stores to look around while waiting.

author: Happy Bird
review_text: Great local food at very reasonable prices. Be prepared to wait in line though, even during off peak hours. We waited in line for 40 mins from 330pm to finally getting to our table at 410pm on a Monday afternoon. And be sure to constantly remind them that you've been there waiting for your seat as they have a disturbing habit of forgetting your place in the line. Our entire meal for 2 cost us less than 500baht. It's clear why this restaurant has been so popular and continues to be as popular as ever after all these years. Will definitely be back again next trip.

author: Albion Onskiedoki
review_text: Budget friendly. Fall down is the serving quite small just what you paid for, but the service was fast and friendly. Attaching the menu for you guys to check out. 🤗

author: John James Vargas
review_text: One of my favorite restaurants in Bangkok during our trip, we went here almost everyday. The line could get pretty long, but it goes by pretty fast. They make one of the best fried rice i’ve tasted in Bangkok, affordable price too!

author: sigit sigit
review_text:
I have been coming here everytime going to bangkok. They serve good quality thai dishes, quick, cheap, and tasty. They are not the best restaurant but everything they serve are good nevertheless.

The curries are amazing, esp the duck red curry. Chinese sausage fried rice was delish, smoky and umami.

Tom yum was also very delicious. Similar to other michelin restaurants i have been but half the price.

They used to have grilled pork salad but sad it was taken down. It was the best dish from them.

Anyhow, the place is legend, and the food is delicious with affordable price. Portion is small so perfect to order a few dishes to try.

author: T C
review_text:
U must come and try this place.

Restaurant has been opended for long lomg time.however they still.managed to.maintain food taste and quality till now

And still very very reasonable prices.

You hardly find quick.Thai dishes with these prices in Siamsquare anymore

author: Yayun Wang
review_text: The food has a high cost-performance ratio and tastes great. The service is fast, and there are plenty of seats. Located in the bustling Siam Square, it's very convenient and a great spot for group gatherings!

author: fille cainglet
review_text:
Don’t be fooled with the high ratings! They ask customers to rate before even trying the food so you can get free appetizer. I told them i’ll try it first. The food was okay but the tom yum soup we thought it was big for 2000bhat but it was just a small serving size good for 1 person.

Overall, I saw a lot of tourists try this shop because of the high rating but I see it as a tourist trap! Nothing special with the place

Plus the bathroom is in the 4th floor! Waited so long for my turn just to learn it was a staff inside probable making tiktok videos!

author: Totally Becks
review_text: The restaurant is a traditional Thai Chinese place that focuses on hot pot porridge.  The boiled rice black crab with roe soup is excellent.  The restaurant is very comfortable with interesting deco.  They also play nice music in the background that somehow isn’t noisy.  We can still have a lovely conversation while enjoying the meal.

author: Jaylene Low
review_text: Good location at Siam Square, very easy to find. Tried their crab meat curry and a vege, both were delicious. Tourist price but food worth it. Ambience is ok overall but will be better if the music at second floor can be lowered.

author: Cheryl Chua
review_text: Came down to try their Spicy Pork and Seafood hotpot, and it's amazing for people who like very spicy food! Tom yum taste is not the typical MSG powder type of flavour! Love it. I must give a special shout out to this chicken wing that looks dry but its so tender and flavourful. Very suitable for people who likes stronger flavoured food, 10/10 for me 👍

author: LY Jun
review_text: My 3rd time here! Love the spicy pork & seafood hotpot + mama noodle! It’s a must to order here! & the grill pork jowl is tasty, soft & nice thickness!

author: Austin
review_text: The restaurant was quite full on Friday night. There was no one at the front at the time we arrived so we had to wait around 5 minute. Overall, food was tasty but the price was relatively high. We really liked tomyum and crab meat and highly recommended them. Vibe was also really good.

author: PP K.
review_text:
The food was a mixed bag; some dishes were good while others were not. The portion sizes were quite small. Interestingly, we were asked to give a five-star review in exchange for a free dish (my friend did that, not me! 😂).

The clam dish was disappointing because it wasn't fresh, and some of the clams were closed. We were offered another dish instead: chicken with cashew nuts. It was very sweet and had only three pieces of chicken!

Overall, I wasn't particularly impressed. It's not terrible, but it didn't wow me either.

author: Deborah Loh
review_text: Amazing place! Food is affordable and staff is super friendly 😊 Food is mouth watering .. slurpy! Just outside of Siam square by the street.. a cute little restaurant! You need to visit 😍

author: Ang Low
review_text:
I stumbled upon this shop while walking to MBK.
The ambiance is beautiful, and the food is normal.
Prices are a bit on the high side, but with the lovely setting and good service, it’s worth a visit.

author: Gillian Bertram
review_text: A disappointing dinner after the end of a shopping day. Kept things simple and  ordered the shrimp Pad Thai, morning glory and clams with chili. Hardly any noodles in the pad Thai and after finally finding them they were very thin gluey noodles clumped together  they saturated in too much sauce with way too much fried pork skin all over it. The clams were not fresh, smelt fishy and were overcooked or reheated from frozen , stringy, and basically not worth eating. Such a shame! Waitress also a bit clueless. Nice decor inside. Again, such a shame as reviews looked good at 4.9!

author: Duke Poolpangnga
review_text: A stylish spot in Siam Square serving a wide variety of Thai dishes with great presentation. The tom yum noodles and steamed egg stood out both in taste and looks. You can ask for milder seasoning without sacrificing flavor, which is a plus for those who prefer less heat. The atmosphere is modern and inviting, with attention to detail in both décor and utensils. Staff are helpful and attentive, adding to the overall positive experience. A great place to enjoy flavorful Thai food in a well-designed setting.

author: Doreen Tan
review_text:
Everything was wonderful, tasty, a lot of seafood, and seafood was fresh too!
We highly recommend the boiled rice - we had the sea bass one. So good!

We also had the tomyum, crab omelette, shrimp crackers and deep fried baby soft shell crab. The drinks were wonderful too - Nam prick jaew soda, the mango sticky rice smoothie, calamansi sour plum soda too.

author: teng teng hor
review_text: Simply walked in to this restaurant as I was around Siam Square area. The mama hotpot is 👍🏼 as well as the crispy pork belly. Price is a lil high but worth the price 😋

author: A C
review_text:
I was deceived by the raving reviews, so I’m updating this to help others avoid the same experience. While the service was good, the staff repeatedly asked if I had reviewed the restaurant, as they were offering a free dish fried salmon head, which turned out to be overly oily and starchy.

I specifically searched for “authentic Thai food” and ended up here, only to realize it’s more of a Chinese-Thai fusion, which wasn’t what I was looking for. I ordered individual dishes with rice separately, and to my surprise, the portions were quite small, especially considering the high price range. Even the rice was served in a small plate, not a full bowl.

After spending 300-400 baht per person, I walked out feeling unsatisfied, knowing I could have gotten better quality food elsewhere. Unless you're just looking for an air-conditioned place to eat, I wouldn’t recommend this restaurant.

author: Mian Wu
review_text: One of the best meal we had in Bangkok! Would highly recommend the mango sticky rice smoothy, sausage, stir fried veggies! Love them all!!

author: Apinya Chamchoi
review_text: Came here with my parents for dinner and we love all the menu we ordered. The portions are perfect and the staffs are amazingly sweet. Best part of today’s dinning is the แจ่วโซดา drink! Highly recommended

author: flo joylene
review_text: Absolutely loved my meal at Korata Bangkok. the spicy pork ribs were fall-off-the-bone tender with just the right heat that lingers pleasantly, and the crab omelet was rich, fluffy, and generously filled with sweet crab meat. The friendly, attentive service made the experience even better. Comforting yet exciting flavors with a warm welcome, a must-try in the city!

author: Phumiphat Supanya
review_text: I love stir fried crispy pork. 🐽 Nice atmosphere and good service from smiley manager. ✨

author: Tommy Koh
review_text:
Food is decent

Service wise not so much? Couldn’t find anyone for 30-40% of the time , wanted to add dishes and drinks but I couldn’t find anyone

Wait time was super long if you’re hungry don’t come by here

author: Veronica Lim
review_text:
Very nice ambience, delicious food.
We ordered :
✔️Spicy Food and Pork Noodle Hotpot
The soup is very rich of flavour, and it’s not too spicy
✔️Grilled Pork Jowl
The meat is very juicy with a bit crispy layer outside, it’s so good even without the dipping sauce
✔️Stewed Pork and Egg with five spices
Just like taiwanese braised pork, it’s nice as well
Overall i’ll give it ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Chen May Yie
review_text:
Food was amazing especially crab meat in yellow curry sauce and salted egg yolk squid too. Service was attentive as we were seated the moment we walked in. Bout 4.5 dishes for 2000 THB it’s worth the money spent. Would recommend it to other visitors first time to Bangkok to dine here.

Pad kra pow could do a better job though, it was chewy and less fragrant. Creamy tom yum soup pairs with it well.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: JJ Tan
review_text:
A Fantastic Lunch at Kub Kao' Kub Pla (CentralWorld)

I had a wonderful dining experience here recently. The atmosphere was great, and the food hit the mark. Here is a breakdown of what I ordered:

The Standout: Crab Fried Rice 🦀
This was easily the highlight of the meal. The taste was excellent and the portion of crab meat was very generous. One thing I really appreciated was the quality of the prep—about 90% of the crab was free of fins/shells, making it very easy to enjoy.

Note: The serving size is a bit small, so keep that in mind if you're extra hungry!

Stir-fried Pumpkin with Salted Egg and Crab Meat 🎃
As a big fan of pumpkin, I enjoyed this dish. The salted egg flavor was good without being overwhelming. However, compared to the fried rice, the amount of crab meat here was not as generous. It was still a solid dish, but the rice definitely won the "crab ratio" contest.

Tom Yum Goong 🥣
This was served piping hot, exactly how it should be. It provided a perfect "vibe shift" for my palate, offering a sharp, spicy contrast to the richer stir-fried dishes.

The Finish: Longan Ice Tea 🥤
To wrap everything up, I had the Longan Ice Tea. It was refreshing, sweet, and the perfect way to end a fantastic meal.

Overall Experience: Fantastic. If you're looking for high-quality Thai comfort food in CentralWorld, this is a reliable and tasty choice.

Tip: If you love crab, definitely prioritize the Crab Fried Rice!

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: TN Lam
review_text: Got the queue number from the host, but she didn’t acknowledge or greet me. However, once I was seated with my local friends, the service was great. Most of the dishes were good, especially the crab curry noodle. This place never fails and usually is the place to go if you want some good Thai food.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Bernard Huang
review_text:
Absolutely impressed with Kub Kao Kub Pla! From the moment you enter, the cozy ambiance and friendly staff make you feel instantly welcomed. The menu is full of authentic Thai dishes, and every plate we tried was bursting with flavor. The Tom Yum had the perfect balance of sour and spicy, with a rich broth and generous portions of seafood. The Pad Thai was cooked perfectly chewy noodles, fresh ingredients, and an amazing smoky aroma.

I also loved how the staff paid attention to details, recommending the best dishes and adjusting the spice level to our preference. Service was quick, portions were generous, and the presentation of each dish was beautiful. You can truly taste the authenticity and the passion in their cooking.

Prices are reasonable for the quality you get. Whether you’re craving comfort Thai food or looking for a place to enjoy a good meal with family or friends, Kub Kao Kub Pla is a must visit. Can’t wait to come back and try more dishes!

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Kevin Tankas
review_text:
A must visit restaurant if you are visiting Bangkok / Centralworld, although a bit pricey, i think. But it is worth it, the price and the taste is just superb and worth. I can taste thailand in every dish if i may say.

We ordered spicy sea bass and golden needle mushroom (360 thb), stir fried pork with shrimp paste (225 thb) and 2 steam rice.

Definitely best buy, even visited couple times during our times in bangkok :)

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: derek neo
review_text: Good and popular thai food but not cheap.  Be prepared for a long queue.   The pandang chicken was really good, the chicken was wrapped in pandang leaves and was perfectly charred.  Service can be improved... they were sold busy and they forgot to smile.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: bo seo
review_text: When I think of and crave Thai food, the first restaurant I go to is Kub Khao' Kub Pla. The flavors and balance of the dishes are absolutely perfect. And I'm a huge fan of the food brand line owned by Khun Pla. Because almost every restaurant she owns has delicious food, and my absolute favorite for Thai food is Kub Kao' Kub Pla. And at the Central World branch, the food was served quickly and the service was excellent.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Andrew Howard
review_text: Popular local Thai food, but as an Aussie it was surprisingly more like Australian Thai food.  The pad Thai was served with Banana Blossums - a really nice touch as they are impossible to source in Australia, but the dish was normal and the prawns were at least a day old  The Tamrind fish was served on a Tamirind sauce base, but not cooked with it - so effectively just fried fish with sauce.  The deep fried crab with Tofu ball was nicely cooked and served on a bed of crispy light noodles.  A good entre choice, but it came out after the other dishes.  The highlight was the almond prawn cakes.  These were juicy and nicely balance.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Joanna Tags
review_text: We tried the crab omelette, wagyu pad kra pao, yellow curry with vermicelli, and pad thai. Everything was so delicious! It was such a nice dinner on our first night in Bangkok. They accidentally billed us twice for my drink, but when we went back a few minutes later, the staff were very accommodating and quickly gave us a refund. Great food and great service, highly recommend!

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: marie benjamin
review_text:
The food is tasty but salty. Over all portions and presentation is very good.
The sauce with the grilled beef was great.
Variety of drinks is good.
Tom yam creamy soup was too salty recommended to have with rice.
Bill for two persons was THB1540

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: WanderWithWit
review_text:
🌟 Comfort Thai Food with Hits and Misses – A Realistic Take on Kub Kao’ Kub Pla (CentralWorld)

We stopped by Kub Kao’ Kub Pla at CentralWorld for lunch, and while the experience had a few bumps, it still offered some memorable highlights.

The star of the meal was definitely the Southern Thai Crab Curry with Butterfly Pea Vermicelli. The crab meat was tender and fresh, and the southern-style curry packed a rich, spicy punch. Pouring the curry over the vibrant butterfly pea vermicelli gave each bite a delightful blend of heat and floral aroma — beautifully balanced and visually striking.

We also had the Stir-Fried Chinese Kai Lan with Crispy Pork, a classic dish we usually enjoy. The pork was nicely crisped, but we found the overall flavour a bit flat. It lacked the salty umami kick from the salted fish paste — the chef had added too little, which was disappointing given how much it could have elevated the dish.

Lastly, we had the Deep-Fried Seabass with Fish Sauce, although it arrived late due to a forgotten order by the waitress. While the fish itself was fresh and well-cooked, it was heavily salted, which made it overly intense. It came with a separate side of shredded green mango, red onions, and fish sauce — very tangy and sharp, almost overwhelming. We wished we had gone with the grilled or steamed version instead.

Service felt rushed due to the crowd, and though the staff were polite, we were slightly let down by the missed order and the lack of any gesture to smooth over the delay — even something small like a complimentary dessert or ice cream would’ve gone a long way.

⸻

✨ Overall: A lively, stylish spot with good food and beautiful presentation, but our experience didn’t feel as polished as expected. Still, that crab curry vermicelli? Worth returning for.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Ly
review_text: Eating at kub kao kub pla never disappoints! The tom yum was super fresh, perfectly spicy, and full of flavor-definitely my favorite dish 😋 the salted egg shirmp and squid were also really tasty. The place is comfy, though the service was a bit slow, still worth coming back!

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Ibtihal Alrasheed
review_text: The food was good overall. I ordered several different dishes and they were all tasty. The photos are available in the post. The only thing I didn’t like was the service, which could be improved.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Dedra Luna
review_text: The food is ok (not memorable), the service is really nice, staff is very attentive and they work hard and fast always with a smile. The place is nice, convenient, and comfortable. But overall, too expensive for what is is

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Caroline Cheong
review_text: Popped by for dinner on a Saturday and there was a queue. Took a number and we got seated in about 20mins. Food came really quick and every dish was outstanding and full of flavour. The stir-fried bitter gourd dish was surprisingly good.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Anna M
review_text:
I tried the fluffy egg white cloud omelette with some local vegetables inside. It was crunchy on the outside and flavourful and soft inside.

The fried crunchy pork sausage chips were excellent, super yummy and flavourful and super crunchy! I also had the coconut drink which was delicious.

The place wasn’t very clean.

The service was pretty good.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: xuan li
review_text: Tom Yum Kung soup is really too ordinary. There are only shrimp and the two foods in the first picture that in the Tom Yum Kung soup .Then the taste is very clear and watery. It is not the same as in the picture. The seafood fried noodles have no taste. It is pitiful that there are few seafood in it. There are only three shrimps and two small squids. There are also shrimp heads in it. There are more than half of themushrooms and the white potato-like thing in the seafood fried noodles. There is not much seafood. It is not cheap in terms of price, but the dishes are really ordinary. Two dishes and one drink is more than 800 baht. It is very expensive. And the waiter's attitude is relatively good, with a sense of service.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Brenda Yeo
review_text: The food was so delicious. Ingredients were generous, and the portions were just right for the four of us. The staff who took our order was very courteous and made appropriate recommendations so we don’t over order. Thank you for a great meal!

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Jasie
review_text:
Ordered a few dishes and verdict:

1st place: Their Thai Milk tea. Surprisingly good.

2nd place: Tom Yum Goong. Taste was unique. They have coconut meat in the soup. Which is quite nice.

3rd place: not in the pictures. But it’s fried Taro.

The rest, just normal.

restaurant: Kub Kao' Kub Pla Central World
author: Michael Fernandez
review_text: Kub Kao’ Kub Pla is a must try for all Thai cuisine fans. We passed this restaurant several times and every day we saw a long queue of people seated outside the restaurant. So the best time to come is around 11am when they just open so that you will be seated rather than wait for a table. Dishes ordered for lunch were : Deep Fried Baby Shrimps with Betel Leaves (Starter), Spicy Papaya Salad with Salted Egg, Stir Fried Melinjo Leaves with Eggs and Crab Meat Omelette. The Deep Fried Baby Shrimp is very flavourful, crispy bite sized shrimp morsels, fried to perfection and seasoned with herbs and spices. The inside is tender and succulent and it comes with a sweet and spicy peanut and cucumber sauce. The Papaya Sauce is a dish here that is not comparable to the Thai Papaya Salads in Singapore or Malaysia. This is the authentic Thai style where the papaya and ingredients are fresh and every bite is crunchy and refreshing. The tiny shrimps are tasty and crispy that you can eat the shells too. The salted egg gives it a nice ‘lift’.  We enjoyed the simple yet flavourful Melinjo leaves stir fried with garlic. The slightly bitter taste blended well with the savoury eggs. The best dish on the table was the Crab Meat Omelette. Fluffy and tender filled with lumps of succulent crab meat. The sweetness of the crab meat complemented the wrapped fluffy yet crispy egg omelette. Never in my life have I eaten so much crab meat at one sitting ! The crab meat omelette was served with a sweet and sour sauce that enhances its taste. For dessert we had their Taro Pearls in sweet coconut milk which was served warm and had yam pearls, yam cubes and slices of coconut .   The fresh mango & sticky rice, a truly Thai classic did not fail to please our taste buds. We will return to try the other offerings in their menu.

author: Rokib Zimi
review_text:
Crispy and delicious at Bonchon’s Chicken Fry, Bangkok!
Absolutely loved our experience here! The Korean fried chicken is incredibly crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside — the flavors are bold and addictive. The sauces are spot on, especially the soy garlic and spicy glaze.

The restaurant has a lively atmosphere and the staff were friendly and quick with service, even during busy times. Great place to enjoy flavorful fried chicken with friends or family. Highly recommend stopping by if you’re in Bangkok and craving something tasty! 🍗🔥🇰🇷

author: Owen Lim
review_text:
This was a life-changing experience.

Never ever in my 18+ years of life have I tasted quality of chicken as high as Bonchon Central World provided. The batter was crispy and just right, not too much and not overly-fried. NOT GREASY EITHER!

It's also very pocket friendly. 589 Baht for 4 amazing drumsticks, 10 mouth-watering wings, 2 SUPERB sides and a generational chicken experience.

Their Kimchi Coleslaw might be the greatest thing I ate alongside fried chicken, and I don't even like coleslaw. That's just how good it is!

10/10 would go here; cancel all your dinner plans and head here instead.

author: SK Katair
review_text: Bonchon at CentralWorld has tasty Korean fried chicken with a variety of flavors to choose from. The food is fresh, crispy, and flavorful. The restaurant is clean with a comfortable atmosphere, and the staff are nice and friendly. Always a good choice when I’m craving Korean fried chicken.

author: Chris P
review_text: This place feels like it should be fast food - not a sit-down experience. The chicken comes breaded and the flavors are good, but you might as well just order breading with sauce and skip the whole chicken thing. My fiancé got some kid of seafood bowl that she loved, but it reminded me of something from Pirates of the Caribbean

author: Natsu Gaara
review_text:
Chicken was well made. Wanted to order some special set menus, but it was only for members. When asked if we could be members we were met with silence.

Waitress English was not that great.

Food was quite ok. 1L Coke came with a lot of ice, so tasted mostly water.

Kitchen was quite efficient. Pricing was OK.

They don't accept cash!

author: Moshi J.
review_text:
Bonchon – The Crispy Korean Chicken Fix You Need 🍗🔥

When it comes to Korean fried chicken, Bonchon is the OG spot that never disappoints. With crispy skin, juicy meat, and that signature soy garlic glaze, it’s a must-visit for anyone craving legit KFC (Korean Fried Chicken, of course 😉). The restaurant is spacious, not too noisy, and service is attentive. Prices? Reasonable for the quality, but good luck stopping at just one order.

What’s Worth Ordering?

✅ Soy Garlic Wings – The Gold Standard
• Crispy, flavorful, and perfectly glazed—these are non-negotiable.
• Pro tip: Skip the breast, go for wings or drumsticks.

✅ Kimchi Soup – Spicy & Soul-Warming
• Bold, tangy, and packed with kimchi goodness.
• Pro tip: Hydrate after—this one can leave you thirsty!

✅ Kimchi Noodle Soup – Smooth & Satisfying
• Soft, tender Korean noodles in a spicy, umami-packed broth.
• Pro tip: Eat it while it’s hot—don’t let the noodles get soggy!

What’s Good About This Place?

✅ Best Korean Fried Chicken in Town – Perfect crunch, perfect flavor.
✅ Variety of Korean Comfort Food – Tteokbokki, bibimbap, ramen, you name it.
✅ Spacious Seating & Chill Ambience – Not too loud, great for casual dining.
✅ Attentive Staff – Quick service, friendly attitude.
✅ Late Ordering Hours – Order until 11 PM, stay until midnight.

Anything to Improve?

❌ Kimchi Soup Can Be Dehydrating – Drink up!
❌ Chicken Breast Can Be Dry – Stick to wings or drumsticks.
❌ Can Get Crowded During Peak Hours – Come early to avoid long waits.

Final Verdict – The Go-To Spot for Korean Chicken Lovers 🔥

Bonchon is the undefeated champion of crispy Korean fried chicken. Whether you’re here for the legendary soy garlic wings, the spicy kimchi soup, or just a chill meal with friends, this place delivers every time.

📢 Pro Tip: If you’re new here, start with the soy garlic wings. Then, if you’re feeling brave, level up with the spicy ones. 🌶️🔥

author: Hippo Poy
review_text: The service was trouble no body take Oder have to ask for Order. restaurant not rush hour on that time. the food come late have to ask for recheck the other

author: Km Y
review_text: If you are craving crispy chicken wings this should be your go to spot. They also have other items on their menu but their chicken is the best seller. Service was slow in this location but that’s expected since it’s inside a busy mall. Water is not free, you have to purchase bottled water. Price is very affordable and will fill you up.

author: Maryna Y.
review_text: A day ago, we just had been at the same restaurant in another province, and chicken there was more delicious than here, at Central World's branch. It was really surprising for us that the same chain of restaurants had different tastes and standards.

author: Pete Xouris
review_text: Great place for fried chicken and fried fish. Korean delicacies too can be found in the menu. A bit pricey though but deserves it.

author: Anthony
review_text: You ask if a dish is spicy or not. Waitress says no but... It is spicy. I didn't touch my meal. 300thb for nothing. Thanks.

author: Natasya Valerie
review_text:
Located at 6th floor, the waitress can speak english so i don't have difficulty to order. The waiting time is about 15-20 minutes

I ordered signature fried chicken with yangnyeom sauce, tasted good

author: icy iii
review_text:
The server’s attitude was really bad, and they might have even insulted foreigners by calling them stupid. When I was checking out, I used GF Fried Chicken promotional voucher. It was a gift from a friend—two vouchers worth 2,000 baht in total—but I wasn’t very familiar with the promotion’s terms.
My dine-in total was over 1,100 baht. I wanted to buy more fried chicken to reach 2,000 baht. However, the staff told me that only one voucher could be used per order. When she informed me of that, I immediately said I didn’t want to add anything else and took out cash to pay.

So, it took me around 5 minutes to complete the payment. After everything was settled, I seemed to hear the cashier say the word “โง่ (ngô) ”to another staff

author: dhanywicaksono handoyo
review_text:
Just like another fried chicken, nothing special, I was expecting to much with the sauce both of soy garlic or hot korean.
