The most terrible is the service, most waitress are passive, they throw their face to outside so they have reason to not seeing us, maybe they are lazy to get order from cuatomers.

One specific waitress, I dont know what is her problem is, but I think she is rude, dont have good attitude. I think because she doesnt speak english fluently, doesnt want to explain clearly to foreigners about the menu, just want have quick task and then finish it.

👎👎👎👎👎

author: Kate B
review_text: Hate chicken legs! I order wings and they try to explain me 100 times that it's wings! Come on! You make me really sad and I have to pay for it! The worst BonChon branch I ever been. Never recommend to anyone.

author: Sirichai Jungsatit
review_text: The service was terrible, the workers acted like we were kids and we couldn’t read!  Should really get fired. Not even a smile was spotted on their faces.

author: Hanuman Np
review_text: I visited Bonchon at CentralWorld and was really disappointed with the service. The restaurant was busy, but many staff members were just standing around, pretending to look busy without actually doing anything. Several came to our table multiple times to ask for our order, even though we had already placed it. It was clear that there was a serious lack of coordination and competence among the team. Unfortunately, the overall experience did not meet the standard I expect from Bonchon.

author: Vitchanart Sirising
review_text: Had dinner with my gf today around 7 pm. We ordered 4 pieces of chicken breast and 10 piece of wings. The chicken breast came out very fast while it took almost 30 min for chicken wings. The chicken breast tastes like it was cook for like a while already.  Both plate smell and taste like old cooking oil. Both of us end up got upset stomach after.

author: a a
review_text: Delicious, and the waiters understand the orders, and the kitchen can deliver.

author: Supreme
review_text: NOT RECOMMENDED. Picture 1 is what i asked, picture 2 is what i received. They insist it's the same plate!

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Justin Tan
review_text:
December 2025: I am a Level 8 contributor (>450 reviews) on Google and regularly review eateries and experiences both in Asia and Melbourne. I saw this eatery on Instagram and decided to check it out.

I ordered the signature noodle dish for 120 Baht. The outstanding items are the crispy pork, roast duck, Chinese sausage and the mushrooms.  The char siew is very bland, unlike the Hong Kong/Singapore version.  The pork and prawn wontans are acceptable,  but I would have liked to bite into pieces of prawns. It is accessible by walking along the bridge, past exit 3, then descending to street level.

Overall, it is acceptable and you can consider visiting if you are in that area.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Sam Root
review_text:
If you're in Thong Lor and need a quick bite, check out this egg noodle shop.

You can get your noodles dry or as a soup and add whatever you like—prawn, crispy pork, and duck are all on the menu.

They also have a ton of condiments on the table so you can spice it up yourself.

The shop is tiny but clean, and the service is super fast. I loved that the menu had photos and English, so it was easy to order. Plus, it’s really affordable; I paid less than 100 baht for my whole meal.

Since they're open from early morning until midnight, it’s a great reliable staple in the area.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Rbw dinata
review_text:
Pick any noodle stall in Bangkok, they were never failed. This is one of them.
Busy staffs, full customers inside and many online order drivers queueing outside.
Ordered their egg noodle with prawn and pork wontons and crispy pork belly. I amazed that chewy thin egg noodle could be so delicious seasoned by savory fragrant oil.
Their generous big chunks of crunchy pork belly, chubby wontons and some green vegies, satisfying.
Affordable price and good service too, fast, clean  and orderly.
Recommended.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Jana Chris
review_text:
We passed by this noodle shop several times during our stay in Bangkok, and no matter whether it was morning or late at night, there was always a queue outside. The display of crispy pork belly alone was enough to tempt us, so we decided to make it our final food stop before leaving the city — and it did not disappoint.

You can build your own bowl and choose exactly what you want. We went for the dry noodles with pork belly, duck, and crab meat, and everything was incredibly flavorful, tender, and perfectly cooked. But the true highlight? The egg noodles. They are unbelievably fresh, springy, and full of flavor — honestly the kind of noodles you could happily eat any time of day. If you go, do yourself a favor and order extra egg noodles!

With amazing meats, great variety, and truly outstanding noodles, this place is absolutely worth the queue. We’d go back in a heartbeat.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Thep Tan
review_text:
Easy peasy. Good selection, friendly staff. The broth was ok, a little bland but you can season it to your taste. Overall the food was good enough that I will come back for a quick meal.

We had 3 noodle dishes with wontons and fried pork, crab fried rice and 1 watermelon drink. The total was 360THB

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: joe conners
review_text: The atmosphere felt really homey and warm like eating home cooked meals but ready in 5 mins. Very simple food with lots of condiments to choose from so you can customize the noodles to your liking. The base itself is already flavourful so the condiments are only there to enhance it. The egg noodles are extra springy but if you put even one tablespoon of soup, it’ be less springy. So if you want to retain the bounce don’t add soup to loosen it. Very affordable too!

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Y.K
review_text: After my massage at Po Thai Massage, I was walking back to the hotel and randomly found this noodle shop right next door. Honestly, it was sooo good! Such a happy little find. I came for massages three times, and every single time I ended up eating noodles here too. Three massages, three bowls of noodles – sooooo great!!😌

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Jeng Shi Lee
review_text: The taste is blend and ordinary but when you add chilli powder to the noodle it changes the whole taste perspective. Chilli powder is spicy for people who couldn't eat spicy food advice not to take at all. The soya sauce on the table is good as well

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Luis See
review_text:
It's a must try in Bangkok Thong Lor. Just down the station very convenient location. Got a seat immediately at lv1, there's more seat at lv2.

Food is very authentic love the noodle with abit of everything, but sad thing is you can't do add-ons.
The fried rice is also superb with hints of wokhei.
Also ordered mixed trio of crispy pork, char siew and  duck; huge portion and value for money.

Overall good food and reasonable price. Definitely I'll be back.

HERE: 24 SEP 25

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Jennifyr Y
review_text: Well we enjoyed this thoroughly. Small bowls with handmade noodles. Pork was crispy and duck was tender. Food is 5 stars. Great tasting and excellent value. Hit the spot! Soup was subtle and flavourful. V clean toilet. No air con but plenty of fans downstairs. Aircon in upstairs part. So good we came again in the evening!

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Sim Kum
review_text:
Finally 1 of the best local restaurants which is not recommended by the internet or influencer!

Very delicious! This is what I am looking for!

Go for their signature dish!

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: kenneth tong
review_text: Wantons were perfect. Roast pork kinda hard and not crispy. Char siew didn’t taste like much. Soup is a little blend. Everything else is nice.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Ian Li
review_text: The shop front is relatively small, which makes the place look like it only does takeaways, but there is actually seating space inside and upstairs. The food is cheap and good, offering a variety of egg noodles and fried rice options, which come with various combinations of wanton, roast pork, roast duck, char siu, crab meat, and prawn. The noodles, if you choose the dry option, are coated in pork oil, which adds alot of flavour. Portions also aren't too big, so light eaters do not have to worry. During busy periods, expect to share tables. Only cash is accepted. Overall, it's a fuss-free place if you're looking for a quick meal.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: WM
review_text:
I was seated immediately during lunch time, and ordered a THB120 dry noodle (all ingredients combo). Every item was well seasoned - from the braised mushrooms, to the fragrant Chinese sausage, to the flavourful chicken, and tasty wantons. Noodles were springy.

Servings are small so men might want to add noodles for THB30.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Rachel Ng
review_text: This place is incredible! It's affordable, fuss-free, and the fried rice with sausage & crab meat was so comforting. I had the crispy pork & roasted duck, wiped it all up despite being a single diner. Thank you for the hearty meal!

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Francis Tan
review_text: Noodles was nice and chewy BUT the pork and wanton was just bland. Had much better wanton than this. Nor sure about the hype is all about since you can get better ones outside of Bangkok for half the price.  Expensive for 90B and not so great atmosphere.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Sakura Fujio
review_text: I ordered crispy pork! It was great, I wanted to order more cucumber and the staff give me two more pieces 😂 that was the funny part! I couldn't eat pork without many cucumbers! Anyways they didn't charge me for two extra cucumbers, thanks❤️

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Charles Chen
review_text: Tasty, cheap and popular with the locals. Springy egg noodles are the way to go. The crispy pork belly was super crisp. Clean ‘street food’ you can rely on in Bangkok.

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Whisky Dev
review_text:
Excellent wantan noodles (Bamee) place that has been open for ages (since the 50s). A solid 8/10 for me.

Paid a return visit to try their crab fried rice.  The standard plate cost just THB100 so don’t expect too much crab meat.  There is a THB250 option that has lots more chunks of crab meat.

My thoughts… good “wok hei” and delicious to the taste.  Perhaps they can charge a little more and increase the amount of crab meat a little.

Satisfying plate of fried rice.  I’d say a 7.5/10

restaurant: Bamee Kon Sae Lee Thong Lo
author: Jinghorjiak
review_text:
28/07/2025
First time try this wonton mee. The fried pork belly is good. Noodles are springy. Char Siew and Wonton is fresh and tasty. We ordered a place of crab fried rice to try. Not bad as well. Got wok hei. Can try. 😀👍

author: Klara Chua
review_text:
We stayed nearby, so it only made sense for us to drop by Paragon for Here Hai. We arrived around dinner hours (6pm+) and we managed to find a seat in the foodcourt.

Ordered and it was a 30 minutes wait till our buzzer rang. It was so worth the wait and look at the amount of crab meat. Great wok hey, fresh crab meat.

If your friends don’t fancy this, go check out other food stalls in the foodcourt - just like we did.

author: yc
review_text:
Located in Siam Paragon.
They operate using a buzzer system so you do not need to physically queue. Just pay and wait for the buzzer.
Both versions of the crab fried rice are v tasty and definitely lives up to all the social media hype.
Only regret was not able to have another meal here before we left Bangkok as we wanted to try other good food. There is really so many delicious food in Bangkok😋

author: Ben Chiou
review_text:
Good fried rice. Chunky crabs. The other dishes are very average but not bad either.

I went at 10AM on a weekday and got served right away. I wouldn't wait for more than 15 minutes for this though.

author: fengzy willa
review_text: Here Hai，a hidden Michelin gem in Paragon, serves incredible seafood that’s totally worth the 30-minute wait! The signature crab fried rice boasts large, juicy crab meat, and the pre-peeled mantis shrimp is tender enough to melt in your mouth—every bite feels luxurious. Don’t let the queue deter you; this spot delivers on flavor and quality that live up to its Michelin name!

author: Miguel
review_text: A famous Michelin guide spot. The crab fried rice did not impress me. It was ok but probably not worth that price. Their sauce tied it up all together beautifully.

author: Daniel Wong
review_text:
It's the stall with the longest queue. After ordering they will pass you a buzzer. Our dishes were ready after 15 minutes although we were told it's a 30 minutes wait.
Loved the fried rice, full of flavour with wok hei and generous amount of crab. The mantis shrimp was delicious too, lots of garlic, only complain is that the dish was not warm when it was served. Will definitely be back whenever we are in Bangkok.

author: D E
review_text: Easily the best Crab Fried Rice I've ever had. Cooked to perfection, you can taste a variety of flavours and the flames of the ultra hot wok. Every bite was special, this is certainly worth every baht spent!

author: Alan Tan
review_text: My wife discovered this place, and we decided to give it a try — and I'm so glad we did. Hands down, the best Thai fried rice I've ever had. It’s easy to see why this spot is so popular. They take their time to perfectly cook the rice, and the crab meat is absolutely incredible. This is definitely a must-visit and will be a regular stop for me in the future. Highly recommend!

author: Farouq AlMutawaah
review_text: Had the crab fried rice at Hai Paragon branch. The wait was about 15 minutes, which was fine, but the dish itself felt pretty average. Nothing special in terms of taste—not bad, just not memorable. Worth trying once if you’re curious, but I wouldn’t order it again.

author: Ray Pine
review_text:
It is a true delight to find a Michelin-rated spot like Here Hai within the Siam Paragon food court, making for a convenient and enticing stop while shopping.

While the crab fried rice was flavorful and notably generous with its toppings, the salt and pepper prawns were merely okay and would benefit from more culinary restraint. Given these are best-sellers, the staff should recommend a dish with acidity or freshness to better cut through and balance the heavy umami spread. Furthermore, the service, while friendly, was inefficient, taking 35 minutes to prepare a fried rice from a supposedly simple kitchen operation. It's still worth a try for the experience.

author: LS SPK
review_text: I'm kinda surprised to see Michelin in food court. The quality of fried rice with crab was quite good. The portion definitely not for Thais. The size S I ordered was really big that I could only finish half of it. The crab meat was fresh and juicy though. No regrets that I had tried it.

author: Jason Quek
review_text: No need to go to the main stall. The branch at Siam Paragon is equally good. And don’t have to queue long hours like Raan Jay Fai under the hot weather.  Save time and effort and fulfill your crab meat hunger. 😂

author: Merry M
review_text:
Food court atmosphere.
Chunky crab meat fried rice. Fried rice deliciously fragrant with char flavoured, serve best with their (green) Thai chilli sauce.
2 portions available - Small (395THB) or Large (495THB)
Couple of other menu items too - spicy crab meat fried rice, crab meat omelette etc.
Didn’t try the other items cos there’s multiple food options there. Just down the Gourmet market is the Street Food corridor, plenty of choices.

author: Fiona Tan
review_text:
Crab meat is tasteless and mantis prawn only taste garlic taste. Totally wasted for such delicious and precious Ingredients.
The only yummy part is the egg and the green chili 🥲
Cost THB 850 and worst than street food. Too bad!
Too disappointed and overrated. I wonder how they got the Michelin For many years.

author: Ibob Pramadi
review_text:
Food was good. High quality smoky fried rice and plenty of crab meat. The green sour chili sauce add more depth to the taste 👍🏽👍🏽

But the service is too long, 1+ hour until the food is ready to eat. Is it worth the wait? Simply no.

They should've add more stove, wok and cook to anticipate the demand.

Located in a foodcourt so cant expect much about the ambiance.

author: Jacob TAN
review_text:
Came here this morning to try the crab omelette rice. Place my order and waited for the buzzer to vibrate. A nice plate of omelette with crab on top of steam rice. The omelette and crab meat were excellent especially with the green chilli.
Next time will try the fried rice.
Service is very good.

author: WanderWithWit
review_text:
🍽️ Here Hai @ Siam Paragon – Michelin Name, Disappointing Reality

I walked into Here Hai at Siam Paragon with high expectations, trusting its Michelin-acclaimed reputation. But after this meal, I feel compelled to speak out — because what I experienced today was not deserving of a Michelin status, not even close.

🌟 To the Michelin Guide:
I urge you to re-evaluate how your name is being used across multiple branches. The original recipe might be there, but the cooking standards, execution, and value at this particular outlet are severely lacking. A Michelin title represents excellence, consistency, and culinary integrity — none of which I found here.

🍲 What we ordered:
1. Fried Cabbage with Fish Sauce & Pork Crackling (170 Baht)
This dish was shockingly salty, and the cabbage was undercooked — crunchy in the wrong way. For the price, I expected a refined version of a humble classic, but this felt like a careless kitchen effort. (See photo for reference.)
2. Stir-Fried Mantis Shrimp with Garlic & Pepper (455 Baht)
Another disappointment. While the mantis shrimp was a premium ingredient, it was again over-seasoned, making it hard to enjoy. Salt seemed to overpower every other flavor on the plate.

💸 Total bill, nearly 650 Baht — for two poorly executed dishes.

In such a prestigious location and with a Michelin label, diners deserve more than just branding. This experience felt like a cash grab hiding behind a name that no longer represents the quality it promises — at least not at this branch.

⸻

⚠️ Bottom Line: Michelin status should not be used lightly — and certainly not as a marketing tool when the food doesn’t uphold its name. Disappointed, overpriced, and not worth the hype.

Both dishes were below Michelin standard and we were very disappointed as we waited for 30mins.

author: Jerald Ici
review_text:
Tried the crab fried rice and stir fried mantis shrimps that met our expectations.

The Gourmet Eats food court is a gem in the city centre. Prices are expectedly higher here but you pay for convenience. Various payment modes avaliable, including credit card.

author: Tracy C
review_text: We tried the crab fried rice — although it was amazing and the main reason why we wanted to go to the original store, the wait for one dish was absurdly insane (1+ hour and also needed to get a food voucher which is another story). I do understand the hype causing these long queues, but I’d recommend for people to try the original location for a better experience with even better food (although again as mentioned above, it was already great to begin with)

author: Albert Khor
review_text: We ordered the crab omelette with white rice (395 Baht) and the crab meat fried rice (395 Baht) at Siam Paragon Mall. Given the location, the higher price is expected, but the dishes were delicious, especially when paired with the chili sauce. Aside from the steep price and the 45-minute waiting time, I have no complaints—it was a satisfying meal overall.

author: Liting
review_text: First time to this restaurant based on google’s recommendation. There are many food options and  i ordered the crab fried rice with egg and rice noodle in soya sauce with crispy pork. For the fried rice, the restaurant was generous as quite a substantiate amount of crab meat was given and the egg was well-cooked. As for the rice noodle, it taste was just nice with abit of the ‘char’ taste. And the crispy pork was soft and not fatty. The restaurant is located near Siam Square hence, not difficult to locate.  Highly recommended!

author: Julie F
review_text:
This place is very popular on social media, so I came with high expectations. I waited around 10 minutes in line, and once I finally tried the food, I have to say it was very good and definitely worth eating.

Unfortunately, the service significantly lowered the overall experience. Apart from the lady at the entrance who was managing the queue, most of the staff appeared cold and unwelcoming, with little to no smile — especially the cashier. The attitude felt tense and unfriendly, which was quite disappointing.

This felt very un-Thai. If you’ve dined at other restaurants in Thailand, the contrast in hospitality is noticeable. Considering the price, I believe customers should receive not only good food but also friendly and respectful service.

We traveled from overseas genuinely excited to enjoy local cuisine, but the cold reception made the experience less enjoyable. I hope the owner takes this feedback seriously, as the food has great potential, but the service needs improvement.

author: Dharmananda Lukito
review_text:
Great food, come at the right time so we dont need to wait.
Price reasonable, sticky manggo is good, the thai noodle is great.

Atmosphere : 4.5/5
Food : 5/5
Staff : 5/5
Worth to try : yes
Wort to come back : yes

One of best padthai we tried..

author: Miranda L
review_text: Came here due to recommendations from everyone.I had crab with rice. Be really honest, the food of course is nice. It is like normal good standard like everywhere else. Not exceptionally excellent as described as the hype. The environment is clean and food are fresh.

author: 金正一
review_text: I visited this restaurant after seeing a YouTuber’s recommendation. There are many food options to choose from. This time, I tried the crab fried rice. It had a generous amount of crab meat, and the eggs were cooked very smoothly and tenderly. The flavor was quite mild, perfect for those who prefer less strong tastes. I believe it would be even better if paired with some tomato sauce. The portion size was large, and I was already quite full after eating it alone, so I couldn’t try anything else. I feel a bit regretful for not trying the Pad Thai, which I’m sure would be even more satisfying. The restaurant is conveniently located near Siam Square, making it easy to go shopping or get a massage afterward. Highly recommended!

author: Anna Huynh
review_text: Great place for a snack so I tried the mango sticky rice, individual serving. I liked that there's an individual size because I know I will overeat it-silky, smooth and sweet.  I also tried the lotus root juice, light in taste and refreshing. I love lotus root and to see it in juice form was interesting.

author: Brian Tamase
review_text: We ordered the pad Thai and the crab egg roll. The pad Thai was good like most pad Thai places. Very classic approach. The crab egg roll was a welcome surprise because the rolls were big and was literally filled with crab meat.

author: Ekim Mike
review_text:
Authentic and Flavorful Pad Thai at Mae Thong Bai, Siam Square

Pad Thai Mae Thong Bai at Siam Square truly lives up to its Michelin Guide recognition. Their pad Thai is incredibly flavorful, with fresh, juicy prawns and perfectly stir-fried noodles that hit all the right notes — sweet, savory, and just a hint of smokiness. Pair it with their sour vegetable minced pork soup, and you’ve got a beautiful balance of rich and tangy flavors.

The eatery itself is small and cozy, with a casual setup that gives off an authentic Bangkok street-food vibe. During lunch hours, it’s buzzing with both locals and tourists, though you’ll likely spot more tourists eager to try this well-known spot.

While the food and ambiance are top-notch, be prepared to pay a premium. Prices here are nearly double what you’d usually pay for a similar meal elsewhere in Bangkok. Still, for the quality and taste, it’s a worthwhile splurge if you’re in the area and craving a solid pad Thai experience.

author: Mel JH Tan
review_text:
Man this is a great place. Firstly, the crab with fried egg; chunks of fresh crunchy garlic really added to the kick, with the Basil, fish sauce and chili padi really brining the dish together. Sunny side fired egg adds a creamy depth to the bite.
Second, the pad thai was sweet and chewy with good wok hey. Good amount of chunky peanuts. River prawn was seasoned with lesser salt than usual, which paired perfectly with the sweet and salty pad thai.

author: ʕ•̫͡•ʕ•̫͡•ʔ•̫͡•ʔ•̫͡•ʕ•̫͡•ʔひかり
review_text:
Got here early so we didnt need to queue. But after around lunch time theres small crowds start queuing up.

The Pad thai was ok, but abit sweet and the crispy pork abit hard to chew. Clear Tomyum soup is sour & spicy enough for me.
For the crab rice its too spicy.. so please let the staff know if you cant handle spicy 🌶️

author: 狐鸣
review_text:
I found this place on xiaohongshu. Short walk from Siam Square and there was no queue. The staff there were very friendly and helpful even though there was a slight language barrier.
You can find all things crab here, and the deep fried pork belly is a must-try. Do try the mango sticky rice. One of the best I've had during my trip. They also have this unique lotus root juice which was very refreshing.

author: Jan Jan
review_text:
Really delicious food and lovely place to sit down for a meal.
We had the crab fried rice (crab was really fresh), and pad thai as well as tom yum soup. Longan drink was great too. Also great to be able to watch the chefs in action at the front.

author: Kenny Choo
review_text: The roaster pork fried rice and crab meat rice are really nice. If you can take spicy, you may eat with the chili it brings up the flavour in your mouth.

author: P S.
review_text:
The price tends to be higher compared to the quality of the food. However, if you factor in the rental costs, the price becomes more understandable. As for crispy pork, it leans towards being sticky rather than excessively crispy.
However, this is just a personal experience. I recommend giving it a try.

author: Ong
review_text: Ordered the Crispy Pork stir fried with Basil and it's the bomb! Highly recommended! I was already full but I still ate the entire plate. My friend order the spicy crab rice and it was also saap and delicious. Will definitely be back again for more!

author: Catharine Ong
review_text:
Small restaurant with cold aircon

Stir fried spicy crab meat rice is fantastic 👍👍👍
Stir fried rice noodles with crispy pork belly abit disappointed as the crispy pork belly not crispy anymore after stir fried
Longan Juice is good 👍👍
Deep fried crab ball is delicious, eat tgt with the sauce will have another different taste 👍👍

Service maybe can improve abit, if first time here was thought to queue nobody approach to you, until we saw another group to ask some question then we just aware but actually you just get the number from the waitress and wait they calling your number. But luckily is quite fast so do not need to wait long time..

author: Kelias Quek
review_text:
I love Thai food and visiting Bangkok is a yearly affair for me and my partner. We have never tried this place before but decided to give it a go after seeing some review on RED.

Here’s my thought, crab meat rice was good, Tom yum too! But the other two dishes was a big no no. Firstly the ‘fresh’ river prawn tasted flakely and with no seasoning, which is a hi he disappointed. And the seafood vermicelli was just so-so.

This really gave the place a huge mark down in my pov. So if you do visit there, do try the crab meat with rice and egg or Tom yum. Other than that don’t waste your stomach space.

author: Mischa Ngan
review_text:
4.5
Casual setting, yet great food. Amazing crab ball wrap, fried egg, and very good padthai.

author: Kai Neo
review_text: Super popular place with tourists and locals serving up phad thai and phad see ew, as well as krapao dishes. Personally prefer the phad see ew as it is less sweet, with an amazing chewy texture and roasty burnt garlic flavour. The tomyum soup was great too, with fresh plump prawns. Highly reccommended if you are looking for a quick bite after shopping at Siam.

author: Olivier Guillard
review_text: Good pad thai at Mae Thong Bai. We went there for lunch and it was good, considering the price. The size of my plate wasn't very big but the price and taste somewhat made up for it.

author: Shawn Ng
review_text:
Roast continues to deliver a consistently good experience.
This visit was a light one — I had the French fries, a piccolo coffee, and a watermelon smoothie, and everything was good as usual. The fries were nicely done, the coffee was well-prepared, and the smoothie was refreshing and not overly sweet — simple items, but executed properly.
I’ve also visited other Roast outlets previously, including the CentralWorld branch, for brunch, and the consistency across outlets is commendable. You know what to expect, and the quality holds up, which is always a good sign.
A reliable spot whether you’re stopping by for brunch or just a casual coffee and snack. Comfortable environment, steady standards, and easy to return to anytime.

author: YC L
review_text:
Roast at EmQuartier offers a broad all-day menu with coffee, desserts, and breakfast plates in a mall setting near the garden-facing side.
During this visit, the tiramisu was the most notable item, with balanced layers and a clear coffee-cocoa profile that matched the classic presentation. Pancakes are available with selectable add-ons, allowing diners to choose fruit, syrup, or spreads to adjust sweetness and texture. Coffee service includes standard espresso-based drinks and milk options consistent with modern cafe expectations. Seating ranges from counter spots to tables suitable for small groups, with steady foot traffic typical of a shopping mall environment. Overall, this branch provides reliable dessert and brunch choices, with tiramisu as a dependable pick and customizable pancakes adding flexibility for different preferences.

author: Maitte
review_text: I enjoy coming here for a healthy and tasty bowl. Drinks are also good and the iced latte is balanced and a generous portion. The service is pleasant. It's a nice venue for breakfast, lunch and also dinner.  Alcoholic drinks are also served. Although it doesn't have a bar vibe, but if you want to enjoy a drink with your meal or simple a quieter place than a bar, this is a great option.

author: Christian Breitkreutz
review_text:
You can almost forget that you sit in a mall. Until you have to use the bathroom. But ok. As long as this cosy restaurant feeling carries you through your lunch / dinner it‘s ok.

When you eat at Roast you get Roast. No matter which place you choose. And that’s good. Because the food is delicious! A nice creative fusion approach to many Western cuisines. And they just revamped their menu.

I had the Peruvian chicken. Very nice. My girlfriend had the chicken pasta (actually gnocchi) - great!

author: Jean Tan
review_text: Came for breakfast and lunch separately on the same day. Only remembered to take photos for my lunch. Had the Peruvian chicken and rose penne with salmon. Both are great especially the chicken that was paired with a jalapeño sauce that packs power!

author: rony soerakoesoemah
review_text:
October 2025: under new management- new menues, higher prices- same good service

The go to place when you just want to eat without deciding what to order...food is consitently good and service even better...from burger 🍔🍟to pasta 🍝all tasty, the fried chicken 🍗could be a bit more cooked.. the complimentary french bread is oh so warm 🥖  go here when to lazy to cook or just wanna get outta of the house🏣

author: Sam Danesh
review_text: I tried the thong lor branch and I had very good experience but this brunch doesn't satisfied me at all, its ok to try once but overall they have a long que and the food is not that great, just ok in my opinion, good to try once but I dont think I wanna try again

author: Phatt H.
review_text:
🍟 Fries: Absolutely delightful — crispy, golden, and clearly made from real potatoes. They’re the kind of fries you’ll crave again.
🦆 Duck Confit: Honestly, this dish didn’t quite wow me. It’s decent, but I’m looking forward to trying other menu highlights.
🍰 Mille-Feuille: Loved it! Each layer was perfectly crisp, and the cream was just the right amount of sweet — not too overpowering. A truly elegant dessert.
📖 Menu Variety: The restaurant offers a wide selection of dishes, and I can’t wait to come back and explore more.
✨ Ambience: Beautiful setting — cozy yet sophisticated. Perfect for a casual lunch or a special dinner.

author: Christopher Scott
review_text: I’ve been in Bangkok for 17 days and Roast has slide into my top 3 places to dine… It’s so good I came back twice. I partake in the happy hour ( buy 2 and get 1 free) , the mouth watering fried chicken ( which is indeed a shareable dish ) and the outstanding berry pie…. The staff is so sweet and hospitable….. I sat outside over looking the beautiful greenery and waterfall….. To the team at Roast, thank you so much and you’ll definitely see me again!!! ❤️ 😘

author: Connush B
review_text: The restaurant is nice, however the tables are too close to each other and it is loud so it is difficult to talk in private.  Food is average but affordable.  Service is friendly and attentive.

author: Anthony Huszar
review_text: Friendly, nice vibe, and good food. The Peruvian chicken was delicious.

author: Des P
review_text:
Beautiful food here - and nice seating - even an outdoor section where you can hear the waterfalls.

I will come back here - the food is exceptional

author: D C
review_text:
This is my second visit, so you know the food has me hooked!

Even though it’s tucked inside a fancy mall with all the luxury glitz, this spot still steals the spotlight. The food? It’s like a big warm hug from home—but with a cool twist that makes it unforgettable.

Let’s talk about their dipping sauce—one taste and you’ll know they mean business. And that chicken? Crispy on the outside, juicy and tender on the inside—basically a party in your mouth with every bite!

It’s also the perfect hangout for drinks with friends. Trust me, the corned beef and a cold one are a match made in heaven.

To top it all off, the staff are so friendly, they make you feel right at home. Still wondering what to do this weekend? Problem solved—this is the place to be!

author: Share Share
review_text:
The Roast Café at EmQuartier is a trendy spot popular for its specialty coffee, all-day brunch menu, and laid-back vibe. Here's an honest review:

Positives:
1. High-Quality Coffee**: Roast is well-known for its expertly brewed coffee, with a wide selection ranging from espresso classics to creative signature drinks.
2. Trendy Atmosphere**: The café’s sleek design, featuring industrial-chic decor and cozy seating, makes it a favorite for Instagrammers and casual meet-ups.
3. Varied Menu**: The menu caters to diverse tastes, with a focus on comfort food, brunch staples, and creative dishes like truffle pasta and fluffy pancakes.
4. Great Location**: Situated in EmQuartier, it’s a convenient spot for a meal or coffee break in between shopping sprees.

Negatives:
1. Overpriced but you get the quality food**: While the food and drinks are good, the prices are on the higher end, which might leave you wondering if it’s worth it compared to other nearby cafés.

Take Note:
The Seafood Stew that was on promotion cost 890b. Big serving enough for 2-3pax. However the taste is diluted due to too much soup. The Seafood Stew that i had in 2017 was much more delicious then.
Fried chicken serving is for 4-5pax. The chicken is huge. Platter is good but too the chicken is too big. Cost 580b, come with 2 sides.

2. Crowded**: It’s a go-to spot for many, so getting a seat during peak hours can be a challenge, especially on weekends.

3. Service**: The staffs are friendly. Good service.

4. Portion Sizes**: Some dishes, while tasty, may feel underwhelming in portion size compared to the price.

Roast Café is a solid choice if you’re looking for good coffee and brunch in a stylish setting. However, it might not be the best value for money, and the crowds can make the experience feel less relaxing. Perfect for a treat and meet up place.

author: Eda A.
review_text: Quality, cleanliness, speed and aesthetics all in one place, a place you can come every meal of the day.👏✨️✌️✅️

author: Ji Young Yoon
review_text: Really nice brunch and drinks with great service. Had an iced latte with coffee cubes which was so nice and the hojicha latte was delicious. Crispy calamaris were good, smoked salmon egg’s Benedict comes with gouda cheese which was fantastic. Their oven baked eggs was creamy tangy and little spicy, so nicely balanced.

author: J
review_text: I was the very first customer on the morning of August 21st, and I ordered a flat white. I was utterly disheartened by what I received, it was the saddest looking espresso I have ever seen. The lack of effort put into it was glaringly obvious, leaving me disappointed. Wanted to start my day with a nice brunch but this is sad..

author: F@ye yuen
review_text: Overall the food are delicious and really pretty . The photos came out really pretty so if you’re looking for a place to take pictures of the food I recommend here. The pancakes are kinda blend but maybe because its a strawberry jam instead of fresh ones.

author: Gary Paul
review_text: I’ve been to Roast over a dozen times over the last 2 years.  The EmQuartier branch is my favorite, but all 3 locations are great. Comfort, quality and consistency are the best descriptors for Roast that I can think of. Always satisfying and delicious, with good mix of old favorites and new dishes to try.  I will be back again and again!

author: xiaoyu guo
review_text: Too many people and It’s a little noisy. I ordered three dishes and all test normal. The ham has a fishy smell. The quality is not deserved their price.

author: T greensake
review_text:
01/November/2025
Takeaway only. Bought the pandan & custard version, was extremely delicious. My regular snacks when I visit Bangkok. This kiosk is located next to the Novotel Siam Square front entrance.

author: Lim Lim
review_text: The pandan snack tasted good, but the other item with coconut filling was too sweet. I visited on Saturday morning around 11am, and unfortunately, the young lady serving showed a poor attitude, seemed unhappy to answer questions, and even got my order wrong.

author: Billy Lim
review_text:
Tried the dessert at Siam Pandan store nearby Siam Square. It's affordable and delicious 😋

One box is about 50 baht and my personal favourite is their signature Pandan and Taro pancake.

The taste is just simply amazing 😍
Not too sweet, but just nice 🙂

If you are near by the area, should try 😉

author: Kaman Kwok
review_text: A variety of pandan, coconut and rice cake. 8 pieces for 50 baht. They are all very sweet and not particularly special. The rave reviews seem to be overrated. If you are in the neighborhood it’s worth a try. However really not worth a special visit.

author: Janelle
review_text: Tried this yummy pandan snack at Siam Square 💚 Chewy, tasty, and honestly so addictive—could keep eating it and never get bored 😝

author: Travis Lim
review_text: One of the best there is. Not too small either. Although not the cheapest compared to other places but it is worth every cent. Highly recommend if you are shopping in the vicinity.

author: Madeleine Tan
review_text: We tried the mixed selection of pastries and it was a good taste of local flavors. The pandan cake didn’t have a strong pandan flavor but it made up for it with its soft, chewy texture, great for a light snack on the go. The coconut pastries were better as it’s sweeter with distinct layers of flavor. You could really taste the corn and purple rice well.

author: Terence Wong
review_text: Came to try this after watching a lot of tiktok videos that recommended this stall. But was totally disappointed. Only taste I got is very sweet. The other stall Kanom Siam we tried at one of the mall is so much better than this.

author: Iuliia Litsevych
review_text: Delicious pandan desserts, was my first time trying, and I can say it’s better to eat them hot or warm for sure 👍🏼 it’s a place with a lot of different sweet snack near Siam square!

author: Steph Tan
review_text: The pancake flavour quite special and nice. I like the green colour one - pandan flavour. ✌️❤️

author: Miki T.
review_text: It’s classic Thai Pendant pancake I ate it since I was young. Always go to take a few if I go to Siam, same taste and same price.

author: Jayon See
review_text: The Pandan dessert is not up to standard, no Pandan Smell, cold, and tough to bites. Really disappointed with the quality.

author: Nemo Atlantis
review_text: Batter Pandan pancakes, opened for decades,  great when eating hot.

author: Wilson Foo
review_text:
I had this before in my younger days but it’s hard to find them in Singapore these days.

This stall does theirs on the spot and they are soft and chewy with strong pandan flavour. Not too sweet though. 50 baht for nine in a box.

author: Elna Tan
review_text: Snack shop next to Siam Novotel, very popular and tasty with a hint of salt

author: James Lim
review_text:
Person taking the order was a bit perturbed that we asked what a certain roll was after being ignored for a while,  she was talking to a co-worker.  From there her attitude didn't turn positive, although she did take our order for a box of 8 rolls.

The rolls were ok, as per prior comments by others its best to eat while still hot.

author: Peiyi (Potato)
review_text: green pandan pancakes are the best!!!! Butter pancakes are nice too

author: 許睿森
review_text: It's delicious, but it tastes different from what I remember.

author: David Kho
review_text: Quick to serve. Good to give it a try but it did not fit my family's taste buds.

author: fei
review_text:
Siam Pandan is a popular dessert shop in Bangkok's Siam Square district. Their specialty is the traditional Thai snack "Khanom Krok," a bite-sized dessert made with coconut milk, rice flour, and flour, similar to takoyaki. Siam Pandan uses pandan leaves to create a vibrant green color and a uniquely fragrant aroma. The soft, tender, and slightly sweet texture makes it a favorite among people of all ages.

This shop has been operating in Siam for over 30 years, and despite relocations and name changes, it remains a classic dessert landmark in the area. Their creations are made to order and are best enjoyed while hot. Each box contains approximately 9 pieces, and prices are affordable (approximately 40-50 baht). The shop is located near the Siam BTS station and the Novotel, making it easily accessible to tourists. Besides their signature Khanom Krok, they also offer a variety of other Thai desserts and snacks, making them a favorite among locals and tourists alike.

author: Jake Poteat
review_text: Beautiful restaurant and terrific food. We had the grouper special, the fried herbal pork, the panang beef curry, the crispy pork papaya salad, the cabbage and chicken, and the and the egg stew with tofu and pork. We also tried a couple desserts. Everything was phenomenal. The staff and owner are so friendly and attentive. We will be back ASAP!

author: Shirling Ang
review_text: Beautiful ambience, great food and lovely cocktails!  The crab with mince balls and the fried sea-bass were my favorite. Another worthy mention was the southern sour fish soup which my camera did not get to in time.

author: Dave
review_text:
We selected this lovely looking restaurant from Google maps: it was just a short walk from our hotel (The Hilton Grande Asoke) and had very good reviews.

Oranuch is run by Aunty Ying (she greeted us as we arrived at the restaurant) and their website states "… at Oranuch, we don't serve Thai cuisine, we serve her cuisine."

It's a lovely looking restaurant and beautifully decorated inside. We loved the menu and it took us a while to choose our dishes. We started with a couple of cocktails, one of which arrived wonderfully fuming with dry ice:

- Siam Passion: Grand Cabaret Hendrick's Gin, Passionfruit Puree, Honey, Basil Leave, Elderflower

We then shared a plate of:
- Hokkaido Scallop Sashimi with Spicy Sauce

Followed by:
- Ribeye Beef with Basil
- Stir-fried Eggplant with Minced Pork & Salted Fish
- Pad Thai with Shrimp

The cocktails were beautifully presented and tasted so good. The sashimi was wonderfully fresh and delicious.

The beef, aubergine and pad Thai were also well presented and full of flavour. What a delicious meal!

We'll definitely be back!

(Also posted to my food blog on Instagram @AbbeyKing16)

author: Daniel Gehriger
review_text:
A Culinary Oasis at the Highest Level!
A fantastic Thai restaurant with a true high-end touch. The cocktails are outstanding – creative, well-balanced, and beautifully presented. The Pad Thai, whole chicken, and beef salad were all incredibly fresh and perfectly seasoned.
The restaurant itself is a peaceful oasis with a stylish atmosphere and top-notch cuisine.
Absolutely recommended – we will definitely be back!

author: Tazio Lai
review_text:
Some of the best Thai cuisine in Bangkok, all in a wonderfully warm welcoming set up!

Have never had any bad dishes over the past 8+ or so visits, and their standard remains equally high and memorable each time!

Service is prompt/fast and attentive, food is of course delicious and served quickly and the flower/plant green house vibe make for a beautiful environment to dine in!

On top of all that, the prices are very fair, especially for the area and quality!

10/10 would recommend!

author: Orn Lucky
review_text: The restaurant is decorated cutely and warmly. The staff provides excellent service. The taste of the food is not very spicy. It might be adjusted to accommodate foreign customers.

author: 오리새
review_text:
A gem in the heart of Asok! 🌟 Just a short walk from the BTS station, with its own parking lot—a rare find in Bangkok. The vibe is warm and family-friendly, with baby chairs available.

We had Tom Yum Goong, fried rice, lamb chops, and mango sticky rice—honestly, some of the best Thai dishes I’ve ever had. Perfect seasoning, spot-on cooking, and served at just the right temperature. If I lived here, this is where I’d bring special guests.

Prices lean slightly on the higher side, but worth every baht. And that beautiful mango basket at the front? Absolutely unforgettable—those were the sweetest mangos I’ve ever tasted. 🥭✨

* Reservation seems to be required

author: Zai.busaya
review_text: Very good service,Top quality of material and so so delicious. I will come back for sure. I’m Thai and I’m satisfy with the food here

author: Trinity Dickinson
review_text: Delicious Thai dishes, and a Cantonese special. Tamjai is a very attentive, friendly and polite hostess, and John the owner is an incredibly gracious guy who gave me an umbrella and told me about Bangkok. Everyone should try this place!

author: Thinh Nguyen Thi
review_text:
Our fav place for thai food in bangkok , even their vegetarian options were wonderful.
We had crab meat omlette, stired fried morning glory, vegetarian curry and more

author: Morla Angelia
review_text:
It was such a lovely experience from start to finish! The food was delicious, and the portions were generous and beautifully presented—definitely Instagram-worthy. Everything we ordered tasted great, though a few dishes were on the spicier side. The staff noticed right away and kindly offered us water. Super attentive!

We also tried one of their signature cocktails, which was tasty and served with flair.

The ambience sets this place apart. It’s so colourful, whimsical, and full of floral charm. It feels homey yet fun, like stepping into a joyful garden. The owner is beautiful and warm, and the service overall was fantastic.

There’s plenty of parking, and the menu has many great options for seafood lovers and vegetarians. We’ll 100% be coming back—with family next time!

author: Wittaya Wongvatanyu
review_text:
Location: the place is only 10 minutes walk from MRT Asoke and BTS Sukhumvit. While driving there is possible, the parking area is quite small so walking or taxi are better options. Also, prior reservation is strongly encouraged. We visited the place on Tuesday's night and the place was almost full. Don't go there on Friday night or weekend without calling them first. Front door had a step or two but wheelchairs should be able to get in with some help.
Atmosphere: the place was cozy and decorated discreetly. It may be noisy though.
Service: waiter was very polite and can handle orders in English. He has his supervisor to help explaining how-tos when the food was served too. They even offered to pack the leftover when they saw we left chicken mostly unbeaten. There were some mixed up when they brought us the wrong boxes a few times though.
Food: it was tuned for inner city people. Not too spicy, not too salty. Me and my friend ordered chicken masman, somtam (papaya salad), stir-fried morning glory with eggs, and grilled chicken with herbs. We had hot green tea and a cocktail as beverage. All of them were very good, except papaya salad which was not sour enough.
Hygiene: the place was clean. There was not undesired odour nor anything that looked dirty. We didn't visit the restrooms so no comments on that
Price: we spent a little under 2000 THB for two. They accepted credit cards without extra charge.

author: NATHALIE KRIEF
review_text: I just had such a great dinner in this restaurant. It's all I was looking for. Some nice green restaurant with good food. I had the fried sea bass with Thai sauce in the side and it was delicious. I will go there again for sure!

author: zaki zuriel
review_text: I ate alone. My wife couldn't come, so I ate twice. Everything was amazing, delicious, great atmosphere, aesthetic place, every dish I had was excellent. And the owner of the house, beautiful and amazing.

author: Munchanaks On Tiktok
review_text:
These were goood! The pricing is a bit on the higher end especially in BKK but I’d say if you want to have a good ambiance dinner with a mix of good conversations with your colleagues - this is a place you can go to!

Must get

🌟 Tom Yum

🌟 Crab Omellete

author: Sasi T
review_text: The crab curry at Oranuch Thai Dining is absolutely delicious—rich, flavorful, and well-prepared.  The scallop dish is also fresh and delicious. However, the restaurant is quite pricey, and the service leaves much to be desired. Most of the staff were not attentive, and only the owner seemed to provide good service. If you’re going for the food, especially the crab curry, it’s worth a visit, but don’t expect great service.

author: David Flacks
review_text:
If I could give this restaurant twelve stars, I would—Oranuch Thai Dining is hands down my favorite restaurant in all of Thailand. From the very first visit, it completely won me over, and I’ll keep coming back again and again, even if it’s just for their unforgettable Penang curry.

The moment you walk in, you’re greeted with warmth and grace, often by the owner herself, which sets the tone for an experience that feels both personal and elevated. The atmosphere is inviting and intimate—elegant without being pretentious, and filled with the kind of charm that makes you feel at home while still knowing you’re in for something truly special.

Every dish is prepared with exceptional care and attention to detail. The flavors are deep, refined, and masterfully balanced. Nothing is rushed or ordinary—everything is made to perfection, and it shows. The Penang curry is a standout, rich and aromatic, with the kind of complexity that makes you pause between bites just to savor it. The cocktails are just as impressive—crafted with precision and creativity, each one feels like a piece of art in both taste and presentation.

Service is another highlight. The staff are attentive, gracious, and genuinely passionate about the food and the experience they deliver. It’s rare to find such consistency in both hospitality and cuisine.

Yes, it’s on the higher end, and you’ll spend a bit more—but every baht is well spent. You’re not just paying for a meal; you’re paying for a dining experience that lingers in your memory. Oranuch Thai Dining is a true gem, and I’ll never get tired of returning to it.

author: Freddy Kua
review_text:
Thoroughly charmed by this restaurant, about 10 minutes walk from Terminal 21. The restaurant serves authentic Thai cuisine with upgraded ingredients. The enchanted restaurant is nestled amongst lush greenery, and the interior is beautifully decorated with flowers and plants, adding splashes of colour in every direction. I'm surprised that they have so many real flowers on the table too. Ladies will love it.

Had a pleasant surprise from the humble shrimp cake, filled with chunks of succulent shrimps. This is a must-have starter.

Their crab curry is another dish to enjoy, with plump and juicy crab claw meat swirled in creamy curry.

To complete a Thai dinner, a pot of Tom Yam gung soup does the job. Was again surprised by the upgraded ingredients, with two pairs of big river prawns simmering in a rich golden broth.

Heard their mango sticky rice is another must-have, but didn't have room for dessert this time.

Had a fun time during dinner as well. The lady manager was very helpful to diners. She would offer to hold the portable table lamp as lighting for diners to take food photos and to take photos for diners as well.

Highly recommended to drop by if you go shopping at Terminal 21.

author: Chen E.
review_text:
I brought my foreign friend here and we were impressed by both the food and the incredible atmosphere! While the prices are on the higher side, definitely more than you’d spend on everyday Thai food. I can say it’s worth it for a special occasion. The flavors are authentically Thai, so there’s no need to worry about taste.

The decoration, filled with various flowers, made you feel good. The place itself feels like stepping into a fancy yet cozy home.

If you’re driving, parking is hassle-free with plenty of spaces available.

Highly recommended!

author: alie sm
review_text: Amazing, we tried the tom yum crispy sea bass soup, it was our favorite. The original happens moo soup it is good in normal spicy.

author: Ms Lau
review_text:
Popular restaurant though we’ve booked, still wait 30mins to be seated, with a little souvenir as compensation, so sweet.

Great to bring Thai street/local dishes into this restaurant.  With not big portion and reasonable pricing, we could try more different dishes and drink.

Recommend deep fried crispy pork belly, garlic fried pork with omelette.  The coconut chicken soup is also delicious with lots of ingredients and fragrant herbs.

Appreciated much with the waiter’s great patience as long queue and super busy to get customers seated.  He always carries a good smile and be polite.

author: AiShan Eats
review_text:
Conveniently located near our hotel, this was our first dinner after checking in. I was never really a fan of Thai food, but after eating here, this local diner gave me a new appreciation of what Thai cuisine has to offer.

We had the Tamarind Prawn Set, Basil Beef with Rice, and Crispy Pork Belly—which turned out to be one of the highlights. The pork belly was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside. A great meal to set the tone for our quick trip.

author: Quoc Dung Phan
review_text:
🇹🇭🥘
Cozy local spot serving delicious Thai dishes.

The food is really tasty and worth the price. The place attracts many young Thai people, which makes the atmosphere lively, youthful, and friendly. I really like the concept, and the staff are very welcoming and attentive.

Definitely coming back!

author: D C
review_text:
This place is a gem for authentic Thai food! The portions are generous, and the interior design is charming, creating a cozy yet vibrant atmosphere. It’s an ideal spot to visit with a group of friends so you can try out more dishes together.

I especially loved the crispy pork—it was so good that we ended up ordering it again. Definitely a must-try!

Highly recommend this place if you’re looking for delicious Thai cuisine with a welcoming vibe.

author: Ine Christel Skogly
review_text:
Great food!

Some dishes are marked with «can be made gluten free on request». Just triple check with your server that the order is right as it’s quite busy.

author: Charles King
review_text:
Lon Lon has a warm and welcoming vibe, excellent food, tasty cocktails and a super friendly staff. Can’t recommend this place highly enough.

Every dish we ordered was delicious. Of particular note the chicken satay with pickled onion and cucumber is an interesting twist on a southeast Asian standard. The tamarind chicken is sweet and tangy, which balances nicely against other dishes. The sesame mushrooms are addictive - sweet and salty. And the banana flower salad is spicy but refreshing.

author: Kris
review_text: Really good Thai food and a great atmosphere. It’s always busy so expect to wait for a seat, but it’s worth it. Would definitely recommend.

author: Hannah Poole
review_text:
This was our second visit, and once again it was a near-perfect experience.

We arrived around 7pm on a Friday, it looked busy with lots of people waiting, but we only waited about 25 minutes. There’s seating outside where you can enjoy a drink while you wait, which made it pleasant.

The standouts were the pomelo salad and the chilli cashew stir fry, both absolutely delicious. The only miss was the roti, which was a bit hard and tasted like it had been pre-cooked and reheated, but everything else was excellent.

There are plenty of vegetarian options, and the staff speak English well, which made it easy to explain dietary needs. Drinks were also great, the passionfruit mojito and Thai tea were especially good. We finished with ice cream for dessert, which was fantastic.

The whole meal came to around 1,200 baht for two people, which felt very reasonable for the quality.

Highly recommend! We’ll definitely be back again.

author: Jules D
review_text: Excellent in so many ways. I’m sure a bib gourmand is coming soon. Servings are freshly made, flavorful and generous. Well priced, too. A definite addition to the Silom neighborhood.

author: Lets hoparound (hoparound.co)
review_text: If you're a fan of classic diner food done right, Lon Lon Local Diner is your spot! Every dish I've tried here has been fantastic – fresh ingredients and perfectly cooked. Their [mention a specific dish, e.g., breakfast burritos, meatloaf, pies] are incredibly flavorful and clearly made with care. The quality really stands out, and it's clear why this place is a local favorite. Great food, great value!

author: Brightastic
review_text:
📍 Lon Lon Local Diner, Trinity Silom Hotel, Soi Silom 3, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500, Thailand

🍽️ Modern Thai-Chinese Khao Tom Diner

🛖 Atmosphere & Vibes: Cozy and trendy with a lively. Wooden furniture, and vintage decor creates a warm, welcoming vibe. Perfect for casual dining or drinks with friends, though it can get loud and tables are small.

🚗 Parking: Free 2-hour parking inside Trinity Silom with stamp

Variety of set menu of porridge and side dishes, abundant portions, and great taste.

🍕 Food

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Set: Kale, Crispy Pork, Boiled Egg Soup
⭐⭐⭐⭐Set: White Garlic Chive, Pickled Cabbage

author: Duke Poolpangnga
review_text:
A lovely little spot we keep coming back to! Lon Lon Local Diner has a cozy, welcoming vibe that makes it perfect for a casual meal. The Thai food here leans toward the milder side in terms of spice—perfect for those like me who prefer gentler flavors—yet it’s still packed with authentic taste. We especially enjoyed the green curry and the affordable set meals, which are great value for money.

The staff are always friendly and attentive, making the dining experience even better. Plus, they have a happy hour for beer before 7 PM—definitely a nice bonus! Conveniently located near our place, it’s become one of our regular go-to spots. Highly recommended for a relaxed meal with good vibes.

author: Sarah Khalbuss
review_text: We came back to this restaurant four times in our one week trip. I am obsessed and it has never disappointed. The price point, the service, the aesthetics and the gourmet food brought us back. We loved the tamarind tofu, tamarind shrimp, chili jam chicken cashew, chili jam tofu cashew, massman curry, pickled cabbage, calamari, spring rolls, and mango sticky rice. The menu is vast. The sets are a great deal with an appetizer. My friend was able to eat vegetarian every time. They even let us switch spicy appetizers for sets which was very kind for us foreigners who can’t handle Thai spicy! I recommend this place a million times over.

author: Dounia Nifa
review_text:
10/10 - the food was delicious from starter to dessert (salted coconut ice cream is incredible). The drinks are original and also a must order.

One of the best eat we had in Bangkok, if not the best.

author: Curt P
review_text:
Updates - Aug 19, 2025.  Still 5* food & service, nice cozy space.  Glad to see they are still delicious worth a visit!

Update - finally tried their Thai sour soup (keng som) & it’s very good, not watered down at all.  Def a must try if you like tom yum soup, this is more intense & spicy (it’s predominantly spicy, then sweet & sour). I think you can have it either with fish or shrimp. I would not suggest this soup as a main entree for anyone who doesn’t enjoy at least an 8 level of spicy on scale of 1-10.

Update - Aug 21, 2023:  still solid 5 stars, staff, space & GREAT tasting Thai food! Come for lunch or dinner, menu is the same:)
Keep up the good work!  Reservation recommended for dinner because they are often busy after 5:30 PM!

Initial review - 5 stars for staff, atmosphere & definitely food! Word has gotten out and this place was filled even on Monday dinner service! Be sure to call ahead for reservations, especially if you’re coming with 4 or more :)
Menu has many dishes we wanted to try and will be back! You can get “set menu” (main dish, soup & rice), or order a la carte and share family style. The soft shell crab in garlic, salt & pepper/chili was so good and never had anything like it (spicy! Don’t eat too much of it at once, try a little first). The shrimp in tamarind sauce was good too. Prices are reasonable, dishes range from about 150-300bht. Definitely a must try - it made me think of what Anna Cafe on Sala Daeng (some +15 years ago) used to be for ambience, service and food! I’m coming back tomorrow night actually & will add more pics! Don’t miss it!

author: gary ong
review_text:
Luckily I came here early and nice staff was able to give me a table.
Food here is pretty good, some dishes had some unique flavours.
Environment was okay, abit too noisy, but overall was a nice experience here.

author: Otherwise Winson
review_text: I am surprised how good the food was! The atmosphere has a very good vipe good chill music on the background what more can you ask for! Perfect

author: R M
review_text: What a fun hip trendy young jazzy place with great local food at perfect human portion sizes at very reasonable prices.  When you enter the atmosphere grabs you like a student cafeteria as its lively and chatty but the setup is rather unique and smart.  From ordering to receiving food is ultra fast yet the dishes are fresh and crisp.  This is a great place to share plates and try a criss cross of local dishes.  We tried their Pomelo salad. The pork belly. Morning Glory. Masaman Curry yo name a few and walked happy content.  Well done

author: Ninajda
review_text: The taste of food is amazing. Variety of food to eat. Hanging out with friends and family vibe. Would recommend to have for dinner because of the atmosphere. Pretty chill place. Food came early.

author: TorquxMusic
review_text: Great food. Cosy and vibrant atmosphere. The staff are very friendly. Was right next to our hotel. Good prices. Would 100% recommend.

author: Joyce Lin
review_text:
Yummy beef bowl in town! 🥩
Yummy beef bowls at decent prices! The menu is limited but focused - and when you come here, you know exactly what you’re getting: a really good beef bowl. The egg yolk and Thai sauce on the side are perfect additions that take it to the next level.
Cozy ambience, though it’s mainly tourists visiting. Definitely worth checking out if you’re craving a quality beef bowl! ✨

author: Joyce
review_text: Not sure if there's 2 outlets or they shifted so there are 2 different address on grab which you may need to take note when booking your ride here. A low key shop tucked in an alley near Thonglor. This place is a gem! Probably one is the best beef bowl I have eaten. Atmosphere and service is good just that the family beside my table was rather noisy. Definitely will come back again.

author: Tazio Lai
review_text:
Finally made it before last order for Friday lunch & well worth the previous attempts to come!

Ordered the Wagyu beef fried rice bowl + the beef skewers and they were as delicious as advertised!

Decoration/ambience is a bit on the eclectic side BUT was there during the day so imagine that in the evenings it comes more to life.

Restaurant is spotless, service was with a smile and very prompt, and food came out piping hot in short time.

Will definitely be back again to satisfy beef bowl cravings!

author: CC
review_text: Always such a great experience at CHUNN! The food is incredible — from perfectly grilled skewers to flavorful rice bowls topped with that rich egg yolk. Atmosphere is welcoming, and the service is consistently excellent. Definitely a spot I’ll keep coming back to

author: Keith Chan
review_text:
Tucked away on the second level of a small building, we even walked past it. You go in a small hallway then up 2 flights.

The beef bowl was a soft spot but bit dry, the yolk was interesting but i preferred the yolk to ooze out. The corn was okay. You could order something else.

The wagyu rice bowl is the star here. Tender and flavorful! Would recommend!

Chill vibes at night with the dj!

author: Jody Chang
review_text: This is my second time visiting, and the food and atmosphere are excellent. Strongly recommended for Thai-style beef dishes.

author: mud mee
review_text:
Atmosphere is sooooo gooooood
Staff is also friendly and welcomed
FOOD!! perfect

Recommended!
- Grilled beef tongue

you definitely get good vibe and positive energy here 👍🏼

author: Chaithawat Dongcharoaen
review_text: I recently visited CHUNN Restaurant in Ekkamai and had a really enjoyable experience. The atmosphere is modern and lively, yet it remains cozy enough for a relaxed dinner. The menu offers creative twists on classic dishes, and every plate I tried was full of fresh flavors and beautifully presented. Whether you’re planning a casual hangout with friends or a special night out, CHUNN in Ekkamai is definitely worth checking out. Highly recommended for beef lovers 🙃

author: Ivy Fukun
review_text: Tidy and Cosy place for beef rice bowl. Try the recommendations, you won’t be disappointed.

author: FoodLover Benson
review_text:
Beef steak rice was not bad
Adding the fried onion gives a marvellous crunchiness for the whole dish, but a little bit lack of sauce.

Beef tongue is something you could die for! Love the charcoal smell and every pieces are perfectly cooked. Gonna order two for myself for the next time!

author: Ng Ng
review_text: Nice vibe with excellence service. Ordered their signature beef rice bowl. The rice itself is abit dry so I wished the yolk was more runny. Would probably mixed really well with the fried garlic. But the beef was nicely done medium rare.

author: Ammz Drrt
review_text: Nice food especially tongue and beef fried rice is so great to try. Don’t forget to order sweet potatoes fries, it’s so so so delicious I love it. Someday they will have party to join, it’s so fun and many people there. Cocktail at Chunn are also interesting. 🫶🏼

author: Kaewjai Nacaskul
review_text: Menu looks appetizing.  Only a few metres walk from my gym.  I'm here for lunch but looks like a lot of actions at night.

author: P R
review_text: Reasonable price for beef dishes. Ordered beef rice bowl and beef truffles fried dumplings. They are delicious. The atmosphere is good and photogenic. Staffs are having well mannered.

author: NomNom
review_text: Really wanted to like this place— went the first time and it was closed due to new years, okay no problem. Came back on our last day in BKK and was so disappointed. The place is small and atmosphere was gloomy. Found it odd that there was no music at all and could hear every conversation. ok, nevermind. The food was the most disappointing. It looks aesthetic and the beef was… mediocre. The yolk looked good but the whole dish lacked flavour and sauce. it’s literally a steak with a rather dry (overly cured?) yolk and a ton of crispy shallots. Anyone could easily make this at home without their expensive prices. I would not recommend.

author: Jiayi (Summer) He
review_text: The food was amazing, the beef is so tender and in my opinion the sauce really brings everything together in the rice bowl. The raw egg yolk is also really good

author: riley
review_text: Very good food. Fun vibe. When we arrived the sign said closed but I’m glad i walked in. She mentioned it sometimes turns from the wind, i would correct this as how many people think it’s closed and just go away.

author: Ann W
review_text: Beef stew aroi mak mak. Truffle mash potatoes was very flavourful and the beef was very tender. Would definitely come back another time!

author: Austin
review_text:
Cool place for lunch or dinner.

[+]

-Very tasty and fancy foods
-Services were nice

[-]
-Portion was not much compared to price

author: Misu
review_text: Truffle Mashed Potatoes really really good！！but beef just ok also the egg not that good enough，i need to admit that it is a really good place for friends to go and chat

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: chefquak
review_text:
excellent dinner

@ เอกฉันท์ - Ekachan Ethnic Thai Cuisine

superb meal for the price.

tomyam (traditional without coconut milk) with river prawns was superb. river prawns very fresh and nicely done not overcooked. the tomyam flavour was excellent.

Ceylon chicken with Royal Thai curry was very good and goes very well with complimentary ruby black rice.

the deepfried fish with tumeric sauce also superb. really sweet and very fresh fish 👍👍👍

excellent meal for 1338b=S$55nett inc drinks

2.1.2026

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Jacob Yap
review_text:
Authentic Thai Flavors & Great Vibes

We had lunch here on New Year’s Day 2026, and it was the perfect start to the year! Ekachan definitely did not disappoint.

• The Food: The cuisine is incredibly authentic. We highly recommend the Tom Yum Goong, Fried Fish, and the Pomelo Salad. Don't miss out on the Mixed Rice — it was too a highlight of our meal!

• The Venue: The space is beautiful and spacious, but it gets very crowded because it’s so popular among tourist.

• Pro Tip:  Strongly suggest making a reservation in advance to avoid a long wait.

Overall, a fantastic spot for ethnic Thai cuisine in Chiang Mai. Highly recommended!

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Michael Nguyen
review_text: My wife and I found this jewel of a place in our trip to Chiang Mai.  The service was great.  They were packed and had a number of tables that have big groups so it was a little bit busy and service was a little slower but not so bad.  I use to work in the food industry so I know how it can be when you have a packed house.  I had their grill steak with mushroom and a small side of beetroot salad with mustered and the steak melted in your mouth with the garlic basil chimichurri sauce. We also had their chicken curry also that did not disappoint.  The chicken was soft and tender and moist. The cabbage stir-fry with garlic tasted great not too oily or salty the cabbage was still crunchy. Then we also had a salad tomato with fruit and dried shrimp with shells on.  It tasted so refreshing.  You will need a reservation for this restaurant.  We ate there at 7:06 on a Friday night.  I forgot to get our servers name but he was excellent  always stopping in to check if we needed anything,  he was also very professional when there was a rude customer service at one of the tables next to use.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: NinaBelle Travels
review_text:
Dining at Ekachan: The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine feels less like a meal and more like a carefully composed travel essay, one written in spice, smoke, and story.

With a focus on unique authentic ingredients, sourced with reverence and prepared with quiet confidence, each dish unfolds as a chapter, guiding us on a journey through the four corners of Thailand through the cuisine. And journey we did, from the herbal depth of the north to the fiery brightness of the south, all balanced with thoughtful restraint.

We selected a luxurious Yunnan beef dish in honour of my maternal heritage; and a bold charcoal grilled catfish, along with a spicy squid egg number in honour of my paternal heritage.

There is an elegance to Ekachan that doesn’t announce itself loudly. Instead, it lingers, much like the flavours; inviting reflection, conversation, and an appreciation for the cultural wisdom embedded in every plate.

We loved it so much, we decided to return for a birthday dinner, a rare compliment in a city rich with extraordinary dining. The second visit felt even more special: familiar yet revelatory, celebratory yet grounded in tradition.

Thank you to the wonderful Ekachan crew who looked after us! 🇹🇭🥢🍚

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Vytautas Majauskas
review_text:
It is easily one of the best places I’ve eaten at in Chiang Mai. Once I discovered it, I ended up coming back every single day during my trip.

Their beef and chicken dishes were my absolute favorites: rich flavor, great texture, and consistently delicious. I also tried their recommended daily special, the catfish, but personally, I wouldn’t suggest picking that one. Everything else, though, was outstanding.

They also have an amazing selection of soups, each packed with depth and authentic Thai flavors.

The staff here is always attentive and friendly, and there are plenty of them, so the service is quick and smooth every time.

If you’re in Chiang Mai and want genuinely great Thai cuisine, this place should be at the top of your list.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Chloe H
review_text:
Very nice food. Average service.

We walk-in at around 17:15 on a weekday and was able to get a seat quickly.

The appetizer (Sausage) tastes much better than I expect!

Deep fried chicken wings - super juicy! But a little too raw, some still have red blood inside.

Today's special catfish dish is indeed special. Tender fish and sweet flavor mix in a great way.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Farah Amine
review_text:
Came here twice for a reason. The first bite I took here I cried and sang. Absolutely worth the wait, staff are so kind and it brings all flavors from different regions.
We live for their pamelo salad with the leaves. Their dessert was ok, but loved their tea and it was served hot. Overall, food was so fresh, hot and flavorful.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Skye Cai
review_text:
Environmental and atmosphere is great.
The fried chicken wing is nice. Very juicy.
Squid salad is quite refreshing, which is the baby squid.
Prawns yellow curry is not to bad, with very fresh prawns.
Coconut pudding not too sweet. With some old coconut floss on top.
Not worth the price but in general it’s okay.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Yvonne L
review_text: Ordered 3 things for dinner, clear hot and sour sea fish soup, deep fried chicken wings and Singha beer.  The fish soup is terrible.  It is obviously not made to order, scooped up from a big pot of ready made soup.  The fish was very firm and broth nothing special.  The chicken wings are too sweet, nothing else.  Beer is cold and good, however.  Server also seems to have a little attitude.  There are many better places to go for a good and enjoyable meal in Chiang Mai.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Manop Pithukpakorn (mprandy)
review_text: This local restaurant takes traditional Thai dishes to the new level. I went to this restaurant knowing nothing about this place. Upon arrival, I was amazed on how attentive the staffs were. Service is outstanding. Every dish was delicious and flawless. This meal also ended in high note with Honey Yuzu sorbet, perfect combination of smooth sorbet, fragrance, right degree of sweetness and citrus. No wonder it’s very popular esp. among tourists. This is the place with Michelin-star quality. 👍

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Dhara H
review_text: Ordered 5 dishes and all 5 taste fantastic! Didn't take a photo of the prawn spring roll, but it's absolutely scrumptious that we'll come back just for this! The white rice and Riceberry combo is highly recommended, brings a different layer of joy to accompany the curry or the beef menu we ordered. Special mention to the young coconut drink that comes pre-peeled off its husks, not just novelty but great way to enjoy your beverage and the coconut flesh (I'm a self proclaimed coconut connoisseur!). Cannot wait to return to this restaurant and try other items in their menu. PS. Must book in advance or you won't get a seat.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Sean T
review_text: I was quite disappointed with my experience here. The food was standard and didn't stand out, especially considering the prices are quite high for Chiang Mai standards. The only highlight was the complimentary steamed rice. While ผัด 3 เหม็น was okay, ฉู่ฉี่ was poor…a few prawns weren't fresh. By the way, the drink they served before meal (to open the palette) was way toooo sweet.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: C.N. Cheng
review_text: I’ve got nothing to complain about, went there for a dinner, pretty authentic Thai food. We ordered crispy port with morning glory (this one was a bit too hot for us), fish and basil beef. I am saying this is one of the best restaurants we’ve been to in Chiang Mai. Based on my Asian standard 👍

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Jarad Yeow
review_text: Food wise one of the best restaurants out there in Chiang Mai so far. The food was flavorful and you would appreciate the flavours especially the tomyam in every bite you take.
