However, the only concern was that each time we had to wait for some time to get refills for our rice which took about 15 minutes each round. Ordered some fish, tomyam, morning glory and beef. The food I’ll give it a 9/10 for sure. Amazing. Atmosphere was great as well. Would definitely recommend here but just make sure you made reservations earlier as we were unable to get a seat the first time we went there.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Anne Lin
review_text:
My fiancé and I came here around 6:30 pm and parked easily in the big lot right in front. We had our hotel call earlier to book a table, which I’d definitely recommend since the place gets quite full during dinner.

There are three dining areas — an outdoor riverside balcony, an upper indoor deck, and a basement section (where we sat, not much view). The place is clean and nicely lit, but if you care about the view, let them know when you book.

Food and service were both excellent. The staff spoke decent English and were super friendly, patiently explaining the menu and giving great recommendations. We loved the stir-fried prawn with shrimp paste, deep-fried chicken wings, and crab egg curry. The only miss was the steak with chimichurri sauce — the steak is not very tender despite having a “Michelin recommendation” sauce aside (so we were told by the staff).

Overall, amazing food. Would totally come back to try more dishes!

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Nuttaporn Boonyateera
review_text: Everything is superb. I brought my BF to try the food here. He said it is the best thai restaurant I have never tried. He likes spicy. We love Squid dish. Service and staffs are well trained. We also enjoy the little market here in the community.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: steven suman
review_text: One of the best Thai food we have had.The pork belly was very good and the omelette was as well. We also have free rice. In conclusion everything was superb and I highly recommend.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: ms __
review_text: Easily one of my favourite restaurants in Chiang Mai! The flavours of every dish were incredible, and the warm, friendly team made the experience even more special. I was pleasantly surprised with a birthday dessert at the end of the meal — such a thoughtful touch that made the evening unforgettable. Highly recommend making a reservation before visiting, as it’s a popular spot among the locals.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Dia Worakittikul
review_text:
Basic, standard taste for local, perhaps good for foreigner not for local. Price is a bit expensive comparing to portion 5 main dishes, 1,8xx THB. taste is rich, spicy but not flavourful, especially Kang-kua-hoi-kom, spicy, coconut milk but not well balanced.
Service is on par, when asking what is mixed in this curry, they can’t tell, need to go back and ask in the kitchen.
nothing convince me to comeback again.

restaurant: Ekachan The Wisdom of Ethnic Thai Cuisine
author: Christopher Wong
review_text:
The food was exceptional and the atmosphere is incredible whether seated inside or outside. The spacing between tables promotes a casual relaxed vibe. On taste alone I can understand why this restaurant was recognized with the Michelin bib Gourmand award.

FOOD
(1) Rawaeng (Beef Turmeric Curry)
My favorite dish that pairs perfectly with Thai Jasmine rice.

(2) Deep Fried Chicken Wings w/ Lemongrass & Sweet Fish Sauce
My second favorite dish. The bed of fried lemongrass under the chicken wings isn't just for presentation. It goes well with each bite of the wing and sweet sauce. I liked this more than Korean fried chicken. Don't hate me.

(3) Grilled Pork Neck & Dipping Sauce
Has a flavor profile similar to Vietnamese grilled pork even though the dish looks more similar to Chinese BBQ pork. The garlic and herb garnishes pairs perfectly with the pork.

(4) Spicy Shrimp Salad
Taste was agreeable. But not what I was expecting for a salad in terms of texture and cohesion of vegetables and meat like if you were to order larb. It would have been more appropriately classified as a stir-fry with a sweet chili sauce. In retrospect, there were no vegetables or fruit like the squid or beef salad. Maybe they forgot or messed up my order?

SERVICE
While the waitresses were friendly, I was pretty disappointed with service. For customers waiting in the lobby, they offered other customers right before us a small cup of cold tea in the lobby. But not my party. My table was never shown the specials of the day blackboard menu unlike other tables around me. I ordered mixed rice but was only served white rice. I ordered bottled water with ice but only got a bottle of room temperature water. The water didn't even arrive though two dishes showed up on our table. It probably wouldn't have arrived if I didn't ask about it. I know the difference between Michelin Bib and Star establishments, but these waitresses are just standing around until you stare or wave them down for every little thing rather than being proactive and attentive. This left a bad impression on the overall experience. They need to train and figure out their service workflow because it was pretty bad. I just wanted to get the check and leave as soon as possible. Well, I got the check and saw a mandatory service charge for 10%. Hopefully my service experience at another Chiang Mai Bib Gourmand will be better tomorrow.

author: Erin F.
review_text: Fantastic food! I love a good savory brekkie and this delivered. Extremely busy little shop. Staff and food were wonderful. Cute atmosphere but due to how busy it was, I would not come here to have a long catch up over coffee with a friend. I got the Jacson... perfect waffle, egg, bacon, and fresh veg.

author: Ewa Marcol
review_text: Best sandwiches I had in my life. Definitely recommend visiting!  The french toast was indeed a bit dry, but the fruits very fresh and sweet. It takes a while to get your order, but once you have it it's so good, you forget about the wait time

author: C
review_text: Fabulous breakfast. Outstanding service and very generous servings! I've eaten here several times and it never disappoints. The French toast, and waffle with scrambled eggs are superb. Great coffee and teas and darling atmosphere. This is a MUST!

author: Yuka R
review_text:
I ordered a highly rated French toast that looked absolutely stunning, so my expectations were high. However, I was a bit disappointed with the actual taste. The egg mixture hadn’t soaked through the bread — it was only lightly coated on the surface.

Of course, this comes down to personal preference, but I love French toast that’s thoroughly soaked in the egg mixture and turns out soft and custardy inside.

If you prefer a lighter texture where the inside still feels like regular bread, or if you’re mainly after an Instagram-worthy presentation, you might enjoy it. But if you love that rich, pudding-like softness, this one may not be for you.

author: Alicia Linder
review_text: Delicious brunch spot with a super cute and pretty atmosphere! We got the strawberry fizzy soda, the Harmonie, and the Scamby. Everything was absolutely delicious. Their menu is varied with plenty of great options. Highly recommend!

author: Dan Brown
review_text: I have been out for breakfast literally thousands of times in my life, and this is by far the best place I've ever eaten!  The portions are huge, service is prompt and they are very welcoming.  I will never forget this place!

author: Kisse
review_text: Lovely cafe and nice food.Nice but bit slow service. French toast with fruit was huge portion ( big enough for 2 people)

author: Charlotte Thomas
review_text: We ate here and the food was so good! The portions are very big so it’s good value for money! Staff were friendly and service was quick! Perfect place for brunch/lunch!

author: Gabriella Enrico
review_text: Our favourite breakfast spot in Chiang Mai! So good we went twice fresh fruit was amazing loved the mango

author: Ferran Arlandis
review_text: The coffee was very good and the food was made with love! Definitely would recommend

author: Gia Ade
review_text:
Would not recommend unless you’re only going for the aesthetic and photo ops, not the actual food or drinks. I ordered the Thai Tea with popping dish (their take on chicken and waffles). The chicken was good, and the waffle was decent but a bit soggy. The Thai tea, however, was terrible—basically milk with the faintest hint of Thai flavor.

I asked both waitresses if I could swap the Thai tea for their special Choco drink since the tea was so bad. They both agreed, but when it was time to pay, they said they couldn’t remove the Thai tea because it had already been made. Had they mentioned that upfront, I never would’ve ordered another drink and would’ve just stuck with water. And speaking of water—it’s not automatically served; you have to ask for it, and I’m assuming you also have to pay for it. I noticed several guests brought their own water bottles, which makes sense.

To make matters worse, the special chocolate drink was bitter, so I ended up wasting money twice. I didn’t even drink a quarter of it. Overall, a complete waste of 894 baht.

author: Phimyada P
review_text:
Car parking: side road
In door seat: 5 tables each table for 3-4 people
Out door seat: 2 tables, all about 8-10 seats
The menu is big compared to the shop’s size. The price is reasonable.
Food presentation was photogenic. The taste was fine. Doesn’t that wow for me
Seems like the staffs were busy or else. I cannot feel that they were welcome the customer. However, they sure worked fast. I dunno a bit smile wouldn’t hurt, right?

author: J Y K
review_text:
Perfect spot for Breakfast & brunch. Quality & portions are great for the price. Staff could be a bit more welcoming but overall dining experience was beyond expectations.

Recommended to come early to avoid the rush hour.

author: Neko Chan
review_text:
Very colorful and tasty breakfast. Good presentation of food.

There are both air conditioning indoor seats and outdoor garden seats. Crowded with tourists.

I recommend the Ryan French toast. A must try  item.

author: Wenter S.
review_text: Super tiny so limited seating!  I came here by myself and waited about 5 minutes for a seat outside.  Such good breakfast and coconuts milk latte, yum. Can’t wait to come back

author: jacqueline azar
review_text: Cute little Café with awesome choice of breakfast, very very delicious and generous servings - but slightly overpriced. Staff is polite but seems to prefer thai costumers or is just generally busy. 4 costumers who arrived after I had ordered were all fully served including hot meals before I even got my drink. Sadly they have 3 wifi networks by name yet none is available for guests. Wanted to plan my day during breakfast as usual, that was quite disappointing - with company I wouldn't have minded it. If seated outside mind the smell, if you have a sensitive nose you might prefer to sit inside. However, the plants and decor outside are nicer. Outdoor seats are in the shadow during mornings. Cafe is usually busy especially after 10 am, many people waited or moved on as it is a small cafe with limited space.

author: tongwariss
review_text: 🍳🍉🍇This famous brunch spot truly impresses with its beautiful, homey decoration. The place isn’t very large, with around five tables inside and another three outside. The food is delicious, especially the fresh fruits served with the meals. However, there’s room for improvement in the service department. The staff seemed a bit indifferent, which detracted slightly from the overall experience.

author: Lina
review_text:
Fruits were so fresh, wide variety too! However I definitely feel that the taste of the dishes are just average and it’s the visual appeal and photo-worthy plating of the meals that makes them stand out.
The portion of the french toast served is very generous — probably would recommend sharing it with someone else. The slices we got didn’t seem fully soaked with egg which was slightly disappointing as only the outside of the bread bore the taste of a classic french toast. So overall, not overly impressed with the toast but the fruits absolutely made up for it!
As for the Happy Bowl, the yogurt was vanilla-flavoured and too sweet for my liking, though I guess that could depend on personal preference. Would be interested in seeing variations with soy/greek yogurt offered. Would recommend getting this if you’re just interested in a light meal as it won’t fill you up
Lastly, we had the ABF! Bacon didn’t look that appetising but taste overall was good, nothing to write home about but a good typical breakfast~

The cafe isn’t very large which does contribute to the cozy homey vibe, but can definitely feel a bit cramped for some and the few tables present can lead to a wait time. Thankfully we didn’t have to wait long — felt like just 5 minutes! Staff also don’t rush you to clear your table like some restaurants do. Even stayed a little after we were finished to have a coffee :) Coming from Bangkok the prices are just incredible - any brunch spot in Bangkok would probably (over)charge you double for the french toast.

author: Nael Din
review_text:
Food was so good it's almost illegal.
The change was placed in a duck basket which was a cute little touch. Overall experience puts you in a great mood the whole day.

author: Riri
review_text: A lovely little café with a charming outdoor garden filled with greenery, which instantly lifts your mood. I had the delicious Ryan’s French Toast, served with a variety of fresh fruits, and enjoyed a relaxed afternoon chatting with friends.

author: Simone Pantaleoni
review_text:
Their signature dish, grilled pork, is fantastic and definitely different taste than classic and traditional thai food - very suggested of you want to take a break from the usual Bangkok flavors.
Staff is kind and service is quick - prices are very fair

author: Melissa LovesIceCream
review_text: Well ventilated place, clean toilets and delicious local Thai food especially prawns with glass noodles and scallops with a tinge of minced pork - Awesome and worth returning!

author: Yuta Sai
review_text: The owner of this place is a really nice and friendly person. We ordered the sukiyaki and scallops and there were absolutely delicious. They are on the spicy end so be prepared but it was really good and really cheap as well compared to more expensive places like Hong Kong . The classic spicy sauce of sweet spicy and sour really complement the dish . I look forward to coming here again to try some more things . Get the fried rice !

author: James.KahHuat Seet
review_text:
The scallops are superb and the beef in the beef sukiyaki is so tender. The grilled squid goes very well with the sauce.
Price is pretty reasonable especially with the great tasty food standard.
Definitely will return again on my next trip to BKK.

author: Praym
review_text: *** Update after 11 months: Original location in Pom Prap has since closed. A shame as it gave a classic and authentic old Bangkok atmosphere. I have ordered food from the new location, still delicious! Apparently they are in a bigger space now.

author: Fury Mah Thailand
review_text: It is a sukiyaki that is quite expensive.But I have to admit that it tastes good and has a dipping sauce that makes it taste deliciously spicy.

author: Bry H
review_text:
Sukiyaki sauce is definitely memorable and delicious. Seafood vermicelli, various shelled seafood were good as well. Recommend!

Cash only or some QR transfer... No visa/mastercard

author: Martina Mattar
review_text: Surely a highlight of my 3-week trip to Asia. I really wish I could eat the steamed fish every week... The scallops were also bomb. God bless Elvis Suki and Seafood + all their staff.

author: Andrij Barytskyi
review_text: Michelin noodles with beef were good, the spicy sauce made it different. But the scallops were outstanding, the first time i tried such a combination with minced pork, onion, garlic and butter + chilli sauce on the side. Recommended!

author: KK IT
review_text:
If you're on the hunt for a sukiyaki experience that's as authentic as it gets, Elvis Suki in Soi Yotse should be your next culinary destination. Nestled in a bustling alley of Yotse, this eatery offers a nostalgic trip back to traditional Thai suki, with a twist of modern flair.

**Ambiance:** The first thing you notice when stepping into Elvis Suki is the casual and welcoming vibe. The décor is simple, reminiscent of a classic Thai diner, but with an undeniable charm. The bustling kitchen and the sound of sizzling meats create an energetic atmosphere that's both lively and comforting.

**Menu Highlights:** The star of the show here is undoubtedly the sukiyaki. The broth is rich and flavorful, simmering to perfection with a harmonious blend of herbs and spices. Whether you prefer it with pork, chicken, or seafood, each option is cooked to tender perfection. The accompanying vegetables are always fresh, adding a delightful crunch to each bite.

One must-try dish is their famous grilled pork, marinated in a savory sauce that strikes the perfect balance between sweet and savory. It's grilled to a delightful char, adding a smoky flavor that's simply irresistible.

**Service:** Despite its modest setting, the service at Elvis Suki is top-notch. The staff are friendly and attentive, always ready to make recommendations or refill your broth. They go out of their way to make you feel at home, which only enhances the overall dining experience.

**Price Point:** One of the best aspects of Elvis Suki is its affordability. The generous portions and reasonable prices make it a fantastic option for both lunch and dinner. You get excellent value for your money without compromising on quality.

**Overall Experience:** Dining at Elvis Suki is like taking a journey through time, with flavors that evoke memories of home-cooked meals and family gatherings. It's a place where tradition meets taste, providing an unforgettable sukiyaki experience. Whether you're a local or a tourist, Elvis Suki in Soi Yotse is a must-visit spot that will leave you coming back for more.

author: Tan Thomas
review_text:
Worth the trip for the sukiyaki as it was well done for me but not for my wife. ( as some say , either u like or don’t). Don’t fray, the Seafood will make up for it.
Top - must order is the Scallop ( BBQ Style with bacon 🥓 chips and minced meat with a salty buttery taste 👅).
The grilled squid 🦑 is really good too with the chilli sauce. Almost perfection juicy and tenderly nice with tiny areas charred. Vegetable was good and Thai styled. Oh…. Do not miss Green Mussels as it was good but a little for me. And lastly some shell fish grilled .

Overall , filling and satisfying!

author: Yuchen L
review_text:
Overall, great food. I'd recommend the grilled prawns, scallops, and fried noodles.

The sukiyaki is well made but too sweet for my taste buds.

The only issue was that one of the prawns was undercooked. Instead of giving us a new prawn, they re-grilles the prawn we already de-shelled.

author: S G
review_text: Delicious food but sometimes strange combinations. They put pork into the scallops and pork fat into the seafood soup. The price a little bit higher for such places.

author: Nick Hensman
review_text: Top quality Suki as expected at a Michelin rated establishment. The scallops are a must here, cooked to perfection with a nub of sausage and lots of butter.

author: Dan
review_text: Food was average. There is a lot more delicious food in Bangkok. Prawn though was a huge disappointment. Under-seasoned and a bit over-cooked with no umami.

author: Piyamas S.
review_text: I have been eating here since high school, almost half of my life. I so much in love with stir-fried sukiyaki, it's my number one dish.

author: Beau Brasseaux
review_text: Almost miss it being it's like a food truck, there's another location on same road with the same name. Be sure to check for the michelin recognize spot. The food was amazing and quick!

author: BulbousBrain
review_text: Simply world-class. The scallops are purrr-fect! And the glass noodles are just as good! Worth the hype!

author: Pattarapon Buathong
review_text: Dried beef suki. Beef is delicious (but not many pieces given). Other is so-so. Vegetables are crispy. Fermented tofu takes the lead in taste. Quite expensive. Store entrance is wet and quite dirty.

author: yang soong
review_text: Food is moderately expensive. They have a separate menu for foreigners. I attached a receipt as a reference guide of the price of 5 pax. It is quite close to the chinatown MRT(m line) station way mangkon. It's walkable, about 500m away from the mrt station. Suggest to have dinner here and walk to Chinatown afterwards. You may enjoy the night street light of chinatown.

author: Roy Ong
review_text: A must try if you are ever in Pratunam Bangkok. I had both the dry and wanton soup noodle. Noodles are of a small portion but with generous amount of prawn wanton. I preferred the dry one over the soup.. Only 90 baht per bowl. I also tried the thai milk tea and green tea. Not bad but i tasted better… around 50 baht per cup. There is this Stir Pork with Basil. I ordered less spicy but damn the flavor is a bomb! I ate the entire basil on my own… and im not a big fan of basil. Worth to pay ard 280 baht for it.. the flavor is intense… a must try!! It located at the end of the alley. Small shop at the corner.. one of the staff there speaks English if you have trouble communicating in Thai.

author: Candy Neo
review_text: We stumbled upon this spot while exploring the area near Platinum Mall, and it was packed! The food is delicious, and we loved the value. The wonton noodles ($4.90) came with generous portions - three big prawn dumplings! The tom yum seafood noodles were also a highlight, with a rich and flavorful broth. Overall, a great find!"

author: Marie
review_text: Definitely recommend this, a good and cheap local spot. I got the pink tomyum noodles for 70 THB. The soup was like tomyum soup, the topping consisted of fishballs & some seafood. The service was fast too.

author: Thanh Phat Nguyen
review_text:
First noodle shop i visited in Thailand and they don't let me down.
There are a lot of different dishes so you can visit here day after day. I choose Tomyum and padthai, my friends have curry and basil rice, egg with crab etc...
Everything is perfect except egg with crab lol. It's not so specical, but the price is really expensive so i don't really recommend that one.
Everything else is perfectly fine.

author: Ars 3276
review_text:
Used to be good the last time we had it 2 years back.
Guess team has change as food is not good.
Wanton was bad. Pork leg too fat and oily. We asked for less fats but i guess msg didnt went thrgh.
Overall no good, period.

author: Alice Yeo
review_text: Located inside Pratunam market near glow hotel.. Not too far and difficult to find. Offered a varieties but we went for Wanton mee. The portion is bigger and the wanton has a big prawn inside which cost us 80bhat. A good local place to try with value for money and good food compare to the famous wanton mee stall. No q n fast serving. Will drop by again.

author: Tian hin Tai
review_text:
This place is visitor friendly, their waiter do speak good enough english for your daily ordering.
Food taste wise are general, but cleaniness good and feel safe at this alley while dining

Good for a good quick grab while you are hungry.

Enjoy your trip!!!

author: Adrian B
review_text: The best tasty food.. Wanton mee / noodles compared to the others ...reasonable amount of vegetable on the noddle bowl. Been here are few times,  no regret coming here. Thanks Yok-Zod the Noodle

author: Ceres Ng
review_text: Saw this somewhere on YouTube or 小红书 and decided to come and try it. Taste ok, I like the soup. Ordered dried wanton mee and dry noodle. For dry noodle, they will ask you to choose noodle type. I would say for singaporean the taste is ok not those very unique type so safe for me as I don't like too unique. By the way the fried wanton is like fried wanton skin, not like singapore inside has meat or prawn.

author: Jessen Tan
review_text: Second time here. Stir fried vermicelli is good. Good place to eat after long shopping walk to catch up. Price is reasonable.

author: Philip Wong
review_text: Not bad. Good taste. Add your own Chilli for the spiciness you want. The wonton is great and tasty

author: Dennis Cheow
review_text:
Will Recommend this Noodle shop then the famous 'unfriendly'.

Food is good, same, 2 mouths finish it, but you can always add noodle for 20B. I str add 2 serving.
With the dry chilli powder, everything taste the same. Cheerz

Staffs is friendly.

Kopi ice is good.

The noodle really more worth then the "famous" 1.

author: TLC Cleaning Pty Ltd
review_text:
When I come back to Bangkok, I always visit Yok Zod

Great little noodle shop, quick, clean, and always value for money and also right in the heart of the markets

author: Arina Ong
review_text: It's located in the Pratunam Market. Delicious and a variety of choices.

author: Army Army
review_text:
Love their soup noodles the most!
Food: 5/5
Drink: Recommend the EstCola, only in Thai, good to try!
Price: Ok

author: TAN JAY
review_text: Prices are shocking for a shop like this charges tourist prices and I don't understand the hype about it mostly patronised by tourists only taste is so average,there r so many stalls around it selling cheaper and better noodles and rice.

author: Q. Nhu Tran
review_text: please dont let the good review make you lose you money for bad food and bad service, we ordered and after 30mins they bring food, the food were too bad, hard and lots of spice... we lost 370baht for nothing, just bad foods. please dont come here

author: Yong Hwa Goo
review_text: Try if u like wanton noodles with Thai style. Braised pork is tasty and braised extremely well as it melts in your mouth.

author: Pang Jing Xuan
review_text: Food was nice . Ordered tomyam wonton and pork leg rice. Portion was slightly small

author: Christian Natan
review_text: Crab omelette for 590 bath like 1 egg only without crab meat, zonk!

author: Tan SR
review_text:
The stall is located closely beside other stalls. There is only a small alley for patrons to queue and a table and 4xcounter seats.

Ordered one with rice and without for additional pork. The fats does dissolve in your mouth, would recommend for those who like it.

author: Peiyi (Potato)
review_text:
Dk is it dabao back left it for too long cold then the meat not tender alr so it tasted quite meh to me. Gravy wasn’t exceptional as well. A bit disappointed. But chilli is nice and made it nicer. Will be back to try it again on the spot next time.

At first I actually tried the wrong stall, the one outside and it was so good (it turned out to be my fav of all) so I assumed this would be better since I saw it being highly raved on TT, so maybe that did raise my expectations a little more.

author: iamafoodtaster
review_text:
A Humble Stall Along e Alley...
Long Queue w Limited Table Seats So Most Of e Customers Request For Take Aways.

Worth To Queue For First Try.
Not A Bad Idea To Take Away~
很家乡味。。。
I Personally Loves It As Compared w Sabx2!!

Will Be Back Again 🤭🤭🤭

author: MJ
review_text: The best pork rice I had in BKK! The skin will melt in your mouth. Highly recommend to there around 7:30am before they sell out

author: Steven Wang
review_text:
A street food which offer Chinese dish consists mainly of fragrant pork leg rice with choice of pork, pig skin, egg and some vegetable

The pork leg taste is good. Chili sauce is just nice, not too spicy.

Usually busy, both for dine in and take aways. The dining area in small alley, is for you to eat only, not that comfy if want to have a chat.

Focus to enjoy the food. Highly recommended!

author: Lee Boon Kit
review_text:
A humble eatery run by a lovely old couple, this place is a must-visit if you're in Thailand.

The stewed pork leg rice is phenomenal! the meat is super tender, and their chili sauce is a must-try as it really hits the spot for me.

However, the seats are very limited and I would recommend to be there early if you want to dine in.

Its located in the heart of Pratunam Market. For a 70 bath meal, I say it's worth the try with it's quality and quantity being quite decent.

Don't miss this place out if you plan to dropby in Bangkok!

author: Jane S
review_text: Visited this place twice during my trip, and it did not disappoint. The prices are reasonable, and the pork leg rice was absolutely delicious. The meat was tender, juicy, and packed with flavor. Also, the owner was generous with the portions, making it even more satisfying. Would recommend coming earlier as it can get quite packed later in the morning

author: MJ Kim Hee
review_text:
I don't typically eat pork belly, but I accompanied my family to this restaurant since they wanted to try it and my dad loves pork leg very much. Luckily, they had a variety of dishes beyond pork belly! I opted for the wonton soup and noodles, and was pleasantly surprised by how delicious they were. The noodles had a great chewy texture and rich flavor without being oily. Highly recommended!

Although I didn't try the pork belly, I did sample the lean meat and it was incredibly tender. The pork gravy was flavorful and paired perfectly with rice. The wait in line was worth it! Note: Be aware that outside food and drinks aren't allowed, so be sure to leave them at the designated rack outside the restaurant.

author: Wai Ling
review_text: This place near Pratunam/ Bangkok City has the most authentic taste of Thai style Pork Leg Rice. It is located along an alley, though not easy to find, and the place is very small, but it makes you feel like a local. The pork itself is very soft, and tastes great! The price is affordable and reasonable too (only 70 baht) Be sure to get there early as it sold out fast!

author: Sakthi Ganesh
review_text:
This place is in a small alley. Don't trust Google maps directions. Anyway. The place can seat only 10-12 and it's pretty hot there. So you can either get a takeaway or wait for people to finish eating and dine in there.

Whatever you choose don't miss out on the food. It's run by an old grandma and grandpa. So don't complain if things are slow either.

Coming to the food, we ordered brazed pork knuckle with rice. It comes with some veggies, some pork fat, meat, rice and a boiled egg. You get condiments like chilli sauce, ground chillies with it. The meat was so juicy and tender and the fat was so gooy and gelatinous. A simple dish with a rich taste and a 5/5 for me. Each play costs 70 baht. There are also other options such as meat without rice and can cost up to 120 baht per plate depending on what you order.

author: Esther
review_text: This modest eatery exclusively caters to the breakfast crowd. The flavor here surpasses that of the usual tourist hotspots by a long shot. Rather than flocking to pricier, less authentic options, visitors should make a point to sample the genuine Thai pork leg rice here. It's truly exceptional! Oh and I love the chili!!

author: melson teo
review_text:
awesome pork knuckle that melts in your mouth. we didn't get to eat it the day before because it was already sold out when we reached there. the staff keeper is so cute and kind, my wife got the change but dropped the 5 baht coin, she gave us another.

the pork knuckle is so tender and flavorful. the rice is well cooked, each grain on its own. the chili is sweet and sour, goes very well with the pork knuckle.

it was so crowded we had to pack it back to our hotel.

author: Chin Yan
review_text: A humble eatery owned by an old couple selling stewed pork leg rice. Located inside of the Pratunam morning market, very crowded and do expect some waiting as there’s not much sitting area. You may opt to takeaway. 70THB is a fair price but this place costs higher than other stewed pork leg place around the area, mostly found around 60THB. Be there early, they may sold out earlier than expected.

author: Victor
review_text:
The food in this area is unbelievably delicious and costs around 60 baht. We tried many different stores and were never disappointed.

Pork knuckles, crispy pork (you got to try this, mouthgasm), basil pork rice, omelette rice, the list goes on. We had breakfast here everyday, eating from all the stores.

author: 美人鱼のDiana yii
review_text: Famous because of their fair selling price and of course their braise pork is delicious. Sticky and doink doink. Haha. Outside all sell above 100 Thai bath per meal. Here only selling 70 Thai bath per meal.. Worth it. Come here for two consecutive days and always have customer queueing.

author: Charjen
review_text: Pork leg stew rice stall you can find in a rather tight alley of morning market in Pratunam. This is a gem find given its lower-than-competitive price and quality of food provided. The total downside is the number of seats available for dine in - less than 10 seats.

author: Z Y
review_text:
Quite famous pork knuckle rice. Decent amount of tender meat to fats ratio, and does not have a strong porky smell, very bearable.

Should dress light here; located in a tight street corner and share space with many other stalls.

author: Yun Yi Thiam
review_text:
Pork knuckle was tender, delicious and flavourful. The fats to meat ratio were just right, really just melts in your mouth! No strong pork smell and very value for money! Enjoy it with their chilli for a much tasty bite!

70 baht for a bowl of goodness! Shop owners were really nice too. Will definitely come back again! :)

Do note the place is very small so get it to go if you don’t want to wait.

author: SM S
review_text: So good!!! We found this place purely by chance.. the initial wanton noodle place we wanted to go to was closed so further search landed us here and food did not disappoint! Meat was juicy and tender, and the fats melt in your mouth! Love it! It's in a very small tight alleyway, so you have to walk further in to find it. Shop's run by a lady and an elderly man. So please be patient. Tables are also very limited but the turnover is very fast!

author: Chin Boon
review_text: My No.1 street food in Thailand !! Her pork knuckles rice is the best authentic taste I ever tried, the sauce was pretty yum and the meat will totally melt inside your mouth !! I don’t mind to sit here every once a week to enjoy this meal !!

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Jason Chin
review_text:
🍜✨ Hidden Thai Gem Alert! ✨🌿
Discovered a secret food haven tucked behind a quiet shop lot! Everything here is a winner—crispy Pork Crackling, juicy Grilled Pork Balls, silky-smooth Kanom Tuay, and the incredibly flavorful Boat Noodles. Each bite feels authentically Thai and undeniably delicious.

Trust me, your taste buds will thank you! 🤤👌
📍 Choo Jaroen Boat Noodles

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: CRNX S.
review_text: Guaranteed by locals! This place is a hidden gem. I’m not usually a fan of boat noodles, but this shop made me really enjoy them. The portion is just right for one person, the crispy pork skin is super fresh, and the atmosphere is perfect for enjoying good local food. The noodles are already perfectly seasoned no need to add anything!

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Anne Marie Kim
review_text:
We got to taste the authentic boat noodle at this place. There is a parking further down. And it has a beautiful garden that is so well-maintained.

The boat noodle has a flavourful thick soup, the best we’ve tried. My friends tried their basil rice and stew pork rice - both are good.  We also tried the dessert, which is the Thai equivalent of “kuih talam”.

This is definitely a place to return to!

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: κεηηγsκ
review_text: A-ròi mâak mâak! 👍🤤👍 I’ve marked this place as my go-to spot for boat noodles the next time I’m in Hat Yai. Seriously next level delicious and hearty bowl of noodles and broth.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Ah Zhi & Jie Wen
review_text:
Went there for consecutive 2 days, great services, waitress can speak Chinese and English. The chef gave us the sweetest smile that made us feel like home.
Noodle taste great (personal opinion) very aromatic 👍

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Jay Chong
review_text: I was really impressed by his boat noodles. They suited my taste perfectly. The flavor was incredibly rich and delicious! Recommend.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Glen Yu
review_text:
Mind-blowingly good! Every spoonful was packed with authentic taste.

These boat noodles truly capture the essence of Bangkok street food. Authentic and incredibly tasty! Seriously, best boat noodles in town.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Celestie Liew
review_text: I love their boat noodles very much. Despite the noodles texture a bit soggy (not so chewy), I love the soup base. It will be even better if can have fresher beansprouts. The space is spacious and you cna choose to sit outdoor which is under the trees or indoor.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Emeline Koh
review_text:
A very nice environment but a bit difficult to find for the place because it’s located at the inside of the road.  You need to walk all the way to the inside from the main road before you will see the stall.

The lady will help to take your order and she can speak English as well.  So don’t need to worry about language if you do not know how to speak Thai.

For the noodle , personally I find that the soup seems too thick for boat noodle but the taste is still not too bad for my liking.  But it’s not really that superb as per what I have watch from social media.

Worth to try if you have nothing much to eat around the corner

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Yan Peng Lim
review_text: This local boat noodle joint was a real gem! The broth was the star of the show - thick, flavorful, and just the right amount of savory.  The meat was incredibly tender, melting in my mouth.  The ice milk tea was a perfect complement, creamy and refreshingly unsweet. Every bite and sip felt like a celebration of local flavors, and I'd definitely go back for more!

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Keikei Foo
review_text: Hidden gem !! One of the best boat noodles I've had !! Taste is better than those already famous , very flavorful. Must try !! Definitely will back when I back to hatyai . Keep it out !!!

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Zhihan Yeo
review_text:
One of the best boat noodles I've had anywhere in Thailand. They only have the pork version, I had the mix of everything with pork balls, intestines, liver and stewed pork. Ingredients were higher quality than usual without being expensive.

Grab some fresh pork crackling and khanom thuay too! Thick, creamy, coconut and pandan fragrance without being overly sweet.

This place is a little hidden but its walkable from the main tourist centre and definitely worth seeking out in Hat Yai.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Allen Teo
review_text: Must try with its egg noodles served with pork balls, and liver if you want. It’s located in a hidden street located back of the flat. Environment is quite nice, with their high hospitality.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Kierra Long
review_text: Super yummy boat noodles! So flavorful and the spice was just right. Ask for without liver if you don’t want that. And I should have ordered extra noodles because the amount of egg noodles I got was a little low.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: buck low
review_text: Simply Heaven! The soup is thick and full of umami. Bigger in portion and price is even more reasonable than those already famous.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: May Ling
review_text: I like the soup and the special dessert, Khanom Thuay(similar to our Malaysia Kuih Talam).Nice place different from the Busy market area.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Nikki L.
review_text:
A hidden gem tucked away inside an alley (look out for the banner and sign at the alley entrance). Having tried the most famous boat noodle in town, I think the pork boat noodles here are much tastier with more generous portions! They have an English menu and the staff can speak Bahasa too. Be sure to try their khanom thuai dessert, commonly eaten with boat noodles.

There's a parking lot beside the restaurant, I believe it's paid parking.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: 吃喝玩乐
review_text: Hidden in a back alley, they told me only have pork. Very delicious and tasty but the soup is more on the sweet side.  At 70 baht per bowl, slightly more expensive than other stall but the meat portion also more, big chunk of meat and very tender.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Wen Chien Cheang
review_text: Boat noodles were perfect. Surprisingly, the rice and pork combo tastes well. Plenty of parking spaces available.

restaurant: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือชูเจริญChoo Ja Roean Boat Noodles
author: Killer Tank
review_text: One of the best Noodles in Hatyai, I try 3 types of noodles and it's worth 🤤 recommend to all food lover out there 🤙 the atmosphere is amazing to

author: PY L
review_text:
Everything is great here.
Arrive at 11.30am and get a seat straight. There are many tables here suitability for 4-6 people. Waiting time is short.

They serve food fast too, in 15 mins.

2 of us manage to try 4 dishes. Pra Ka Bao got a lot of wok hei.
Tom yum is thick and slightly sweet not to my favour. Garlic fried pork is crispy, vege with meat taste good too

author: T Sp
review_text:
Must came earlier to this restaurant, or else u had to wait in queue!
Always loved their cuisine, the taste was delicious & authentic.
Southern style braised pork was so flavorful. The gravy was incredible nice.
Every dishes were thumb up! Superb

author: Joyce Lau
review_text:
Crispy, flavourful Thai-style dishes! The fried fish was perfectly crunchy with lots of garlic, and the salads were fresh and well-balanced. Great comfort food 👍

Definitely coming back for their food!!

author: Hai Cheen Choong
review_text: We checked on Google for good food in Hatyai and found this place with thousands of reviews and a high rating – and it definitely lived up to the hype! There were people helping to take care of our car during parking, which was very convenient. The food was served very quickly, and everything we ordered was absolutely delicious at a reasonable price. The floor and tables were clean, and the staff were all very friendly. Highly recommended!

author: Alphonse Eelric
review_text:
Dishes are good, fast, price are very reasonable. But its always crowded with Malaysians hence some time waiting time would be long. But overall is a good place to catch a nice meal.
Try not to drive here as there is no parking! take a grab or ride a small motorcycle is better.
Note: not Halal! not Halal! not Halal!

author: Shirlene Tay
review_text:
This is a very popular place with lots of locals and tourists. Be prepared to wait for at least 15 minutes but the queue is quite fast and the serving time is fast as well. Many workers and all are efficient and fast workers so no worry about that. They can speak pretty good English which is good.
The price is reasonable. Around 100 baht or so per dish

author: Ch'ng Ewe Theng (Thomas Ch'ng)
review_text:
A special thank-you to the Boss and his wife for the amazing meal they served us for free on the night we escaped from the city centre. They turned their restaurant into a soup kitchen, offering free food to everyone — customers and locals alike.

We thought we could go home the next morning, but the second wave came and destroyed their restaurant overnight.

We truly believe the Boss will receive good karma, and his business will come back even stronger when he reopens. 🙏❤️ From the B2 Premier Hotel 7th floor 11 Gang with Love ❤️❤️❤️

author: Khay Yin Tang
review_text: The food here is tasty and delicious! It's also very affordable, which is a big plus. Additionally, the service is impressively quick—dishes arrive in no time! I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a great meal without breaking the bank.

author: Zen Yong
review_text:
Krua Pa-Yad is one of those restaurants in Hatyai that many people talk about, so we decided to give it a try — and it did not disappoint. The restaurant opens at 4 PM, and we arrived early, becoming part of the second batch of customers for the evening. This turned out to be a great decision because the place can get very busy later on, with long waiting queues forming rather quickly. If you plan to visit, I would highly recommend going early to avoid the crowd and enjoy a more relaxed dining experience.

The staff here were friendly and attentive. They greeted us warmly and took our order promptly. Despite the restaurant starting to fill up, service remained smooth and efficient, which made the whole experience enjoyable.

The environment is clean, spacious, and well-maintained, providing a comfortable setting for a casual dinner. The open layout and neat arrangement of tables create a nice atmosphere where you can enjoy your meal without feeling cramped.

Price-wise, the menu felt reasonable and fair for the quality and portion size of the food. The dishes we ordered were served in portions that matched the price, which made it easy to order a variety of items without worrying about wasting food.

Taste-wise, everything we tried was delicious. The flavors were well-balanced, and you could tell the ingredients were fresh. It’s the kind of food that feels homey yet flavorful, perfect for sharing with family or friends.

Overall, Krua Pa-Yad is definitely worth a visit if you are in Hatyai. Between the friendly service, clean and comfortable environment, reasonable pricing, and tasty dishes, it makes for a satisfying dining experience. Just remember to plan ahead and arrive early — it’s popular for a reason, and the waiting queue later in the evening can get quite long!

author: Tammy Tan
review_text:
Cafeteria style dining. Bright, clean spacious. Drinks & dessert is places in a fridge where customer can grab what they want. Some food in small portion some big. 2 of us ordered 4 dishes plus a botel of mineral water & 1 dessert cost 400+ thai baht. Food taste good 👍 Most of the staff speaks Chinese. Go there before peak hours then you don't need to queue.
Went there again, this time ordered Fried Squid & Braised Pork. Both ok but I prefer Braised pork more

author: Stephen Kagawa
review_text:
Food is amazing and delicious! The tomyam and crab meat with yellow curry is must try!
Strongly recommended when you in hat yai.
Price is affordable. We spent around 500baht for 3 person.
We were there around 5.30pm and it was almost full house.

author: S C
review_text: A restaurant with many workers, so even though it's often crowded,  food service is pretty fast. We ordered a number of dishes which are all very satisfying.  Price is very affordable as well.

author: Tony Tan
review_text: Delicious food in a nice, spacious area. They prefer cash payments, so please be ready with cash.

author: Wei Kang
review_text: The food is delicious and reasonably priced! Since I walked here from the hotel, I didn’t have to worry about parking. Also, I arrived before the busy hours, so there was no need to queue. Shortly after I sat down, I noticed more and more people arriving. So I suggest everyone who doesn’t want to wait too long should come a bit earlier!

author: Andrew C
review_text: The order arrived very fast within 5-10 minutes. Vege, squid done not overcooked but the fish is a disappointment. Fish too oily and seems to be pre-prepared earlier, refried few times. Price reasonable. Fish dish at Jia-lek is much better but need to wait if the place is crowded. Still like Jae-lek better even bit more expensive.

author: Frida Tan
review_text: Came here around 1pm and not so crowded. The owner (i assumed, the person who took order and payment) can speak English well, no worry for ordering. All good served in reasonable speed and overall really delicious. You can customise the spicy level for tomyam too.

author: Billy Kok
review_text:
When you see locals crowd a restaurant it signalled good food.

We were recommended to visit and on arrival to Hat Yai we took a tuk-tuk here.

Easy pictorial menu, point and point. Portions are for 2, so order more if you have a group. The 8 of us had 2 veggies, 2 whole fishes, 4 som-tam (as we liked it), 2 tomyam, 2 deep fried sotong and 2 pork.

author: pear arnont
review_text: Good food, good taste. Reasonable price. Worth it. Recommend

author: Lye Guang Yang
review_text: The dishes are packed with flavour, nice! The staffs are friendly and welcoming, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. Recommended for a satisfying local Thai meal. Just that the parking would be a bit of problem as we needed to park at the roadside. The uncle directing the customers was very friendly though.

author: SE Teoh
review_text: A must visit in Hatyai! Very affordable, our meal was only 300 baht. The stir-fried kailan with roasted pork is a must-try, and the crispy garlic sotong is delicious. Fast service and a very clean environment. Highly recommended!

author: Yeen Yeen
review_text: Went to Ban Khun Bhu for lunch, it was raining heavily during lunch hour, but luckily there was no crowd and no need to queue. The restaurant owner was very friendly and even recommended some must-try dishes. We ordered tomyum soup with pork, grilled chicken, grilled pork neck, sweet and sour glass noodle with seafood, fried rice, and more. We absolutely loved the tomyum soup with pork! We chose spicy level 7 & just nice! Definitely worth a visit. 🌶️🍲

author: joyce lee
review_text:
The food here is scrumptious. We ordered the shrimp tomyam, seafood fried rice (be prepared as a serving for 1 is incredibly small but is full of punch), a Northern and Eastern sausage, omelette, sticky rice, catfish salad and drinks for 3. Total was THB650.

The tomyam was really good and full of prawns. Same with the fried rice.

Definitely a place to return to next trip.

author: HS TEH
review_text: Good food, served quickly. Arrive on 11.30am already full house but can go in less than 15mins. Sausage have 2 flavour which can order in mix. The vege is a bit sour and very appetizing.

author: Sidney Kan
review_text:
Lunch was within a walking distance from out hotel and yet so hidden within the town centre. Food at Ban Khun Bhu was just amazing, light and delicious. Shrimp omelette was just unbelievable delicious, fragrant, warm and addictive. Their bbq boneless chicken got us hooked, love the fine firm texture of the chicken and tasty marinated. White tom yam was just amazingly good, owner himself told us that the fresh herb used comes from his home garden without any peticide. Ours came with plenty of sizeable prawns. We also add on their specialty Northern and middle Thai homemade sausage, it was so good. We also tried the coconut drink too, nice. Love this eatery, no frills so delicious ♥️♥️♥️

Baan Khun Bhu
1 Prachathipat Road,
Hat Yai District,
Songkhla 90110

author: Onlyjulieee
review_text:
The food is great!
My top pick is the grilled chicken — it’s packed with smoky BBQ aroma and comes with a tangy sauce that’s incredibly appetising.
For the tom yum soup, you can choose your spice level from 0 to 10. We went with 7, but it could definitely be spicier. The friendly boss even encouraged us to try a higher level next time.
It was also my first time trying coconut nectar water!
Will revisit when i come to Hatyai next time.

author: Sharon Goh
review_text: Just tasted the best authentic food during our holiday stay here. The tom yam is superb & traditional. It is a small eatery shop, nothing fancy but really rustic. But one needs to catch the opening hours. We tried 3 times & finally, the 4th time, we managed to savour these good dishes. If you missed it by 5min, you will not be able to enter. The boss is a friendly, humble man & he could speak English. Thank you for keeping up the good local food with standard! 🥰😁😆😉😋 We will return! 🤣😂😊😉

author: Elaine SYL
review_text: Absolutely love this place! 😍 Affordable and super tasty Thai food with generous portions. The boss is incredibly friendly and always checks in to make sure the spice level suits you. Great spot for a casual meal without breaking the bank. Highly recommended! 🌶️🇹🇭

author: Chee Kng Lim
review_text:
I found Baan during my first foray to Hat Yai as a working adult. We went twice but only ate once. This was because I did not do my research properly; on our first try, they were not open for business. Second time, we should have gone earlier. They open at around 10.30 to 11am and before opening, there would have been a queue forming. Not a long one.

If you go during the peak hours, be prepared to wait a while.

The menu has been consistent, at least since my last visit.

The boss is very friendly and fluent in English. He can give you recommendations if you are in two minds.

Our favourites are
1. Tom Yum Seafood Clear
2. Stir Fried Liver
3. Pork and Onion Omelette
4. Sour Glass Noodles Salad with Prawns
5. Thai Sausages (mixed flavours)
6. Grilled Pork

They have more items which we have not tried so we look forward to more Hat Yai trips.

All these food is topped off with a coconut flower nectar drink which is quite hard to find. I have only ever seen it in their shop and another eatery in Hat Yai.

author: BKK
review_text:
Bad experience.

1. When I first entered the restaurant, I saw many birds flying around inside and even bird droppings on the floor — very unhygienic.

2. The menu had no prices. When I asked the owner, he said the menu for foreigners is different and told me to just ask him for prices. This felt very dishonest and made me uncomfortable.

3. The food was not tasty at all.

Definitely not recommended.
My first visit — and my last.

author: N.I.I
review_text: Everything we ordered is superb! Come and try on your own! Just the place is very hot and drinks kinda limited. Will definitely visit again!

author: Allen Teo
review_text: Served authentic Thai cuisine but the taste might adapt to Malaysian. Anyway the experience is still good to try. Ordered thai sausage, tomyam soup and Thai basil pork.

author: Jack Choo
review_text: Unassuming look from the outside and very local like. Many tourists visit this place as well as the food is fantastic at a decent price as well. Authentic Thai fair with them asking before hand foreigners the spice level….so beware! Come early of you want a spot.

author: BOON LEONG TAN
review_text: On 13th July 2025, me and family members come to visit this famous restaurant in Hatyai. Since the crowds are big and the waiting time to be around 20 to 30 mins. The ordering was easy as the restaurant owner well speak English. All the dishes we ordered are recommended.  We ordered the roasted chicken, clear tomyam, sausage and fried rice. Although with a many customers the timing to serving was great and didn't take much time. Well done.

author: DAK
review_text: Authentic thai food in Hatyai. The fried rice was awesome so are all the dishes. Tom yam seafood a must try. The owner speaks good english and you can choose the level of spiciness 1-10. We chose 8 and still feeling it

author: Shang Yih Leong
review_text: Best local Thai restaurant I had experienced so far in Hatyai. The food is delicious and free of MSG. The friendly boss can also speak fluent English. Must come early to get into a shorter queue (very unlikely that you won't get into a queue because of its popularity, so you can only wish for a shorter one).

author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)
review_text: Nice boss, easy to converse in English. Menu is rather limited with a lot of focus on yam and somtum, grilled meat, sai krok isan and sai oua, and tomyum. We ordered the sai krok isan and sai oua platter, a yam woon sen (glass noodles) kai, seafood tomyum, and a minced chicken omelet. I like their sai krok because its not as sour as most sai krok, we ordered a level 5 tomyum and find it not spicy enough. The yam woon sen portion is generous, and taste is there. Omelet is standard. Overall, we spent 720b for 4 pax with 2 bottles of coconut nectar and 2 bottles of water. The food taste and freshness and pricing are fair.

author: Tang Zhao Zhen
review_text:
Restaurant serving local Thai Dishes. Food taste suite my taste

Order both or their Thai Sausage.

1)Darker one is more chewy. Taste like otak otak, but less sweet, more spicy

2)Red one mixed with sticky rice. It is softer and taste more on sour(fermentationside with a little sweet.

author: Justin Wong
review_text: Their Nam Tok is out of the world, how they make the meat so crunchy, chewy and tender at the sametime is out of my mind. Best savour every cjew to bring out the favor, take your time, don't cone when you rushing. The Sai Oua & Sai krok Isan also pretty good.

author: Willy Soon
review_text:
Good service, good food
Tomyum, grilled chicken, somtum, sausage must try

author: Poh Zhi Nan
review_text:
This was my first meal in Hatyai and I am glad I started my solo trip on a good start! The fried rice with BBQ pork was so fragrant (there was wok hei!) and every bite was packed with flavour. There was a side of cucumber as well which I believed was to cleanse the palate. I ordered a coconut nectar drink as well but it felt too healthy for me and I was not really used to the taste haha.

The owners here are very friendly and they are bilingual (can speak English and Chinese aside from Thai). There is seldom some fruit flies flying around but it doesn’t affect the meal experience. I thought it would be warm but there is ample ventilation. Overall, it’s a really authentic experience and I highly recommend this place!

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Notorious
review_text:
My first review in Thailand, more specifically Hatyai. This is a famous spot for pork and rice (Go Chew). The staff are all very friendly and welcoming. Ordering is no problem if you speak Mandarin.

The roast pork is crispy and tasty, while the braised pork with eggs and vegetables is tender and flavorful—best enjoyed with rice since it’s on the salty side. The chicken is pretty decent as well, comes with special condiments. Prices are quite reasonable for the quality. Definitely worth a try!

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: κεηηγsκ
review_text:
One senses from the name alone a promise of heritage: “The Original, Traditional Recipe. The star of the show is, of course, the stewed pork leg, beautifully tender and perfectly balanced in flavor. You can choose to have it served whole or chopped, though most diners seem to prefer the latter.

However, the real surprise is the roasted pork belly, the unexpected hero, delightfully crispy, flavorful, and generously portioned. Despite the holiday crowd, our dishes arrived quickly, and the staff were friendly and spoke Mandarin, which was super helpful. Oh, and the black iced coffee? Absolutely loved it!

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Goh Jun Wen
review_text: Decent food but I've tasted much better ones. Portion is big and generous, total 1270 baht for 6 people including drinks. Service is okay, food is served fairly quickly. Alot of tourists.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: david chong
review_text:
The signage at the stall front says Ko Chew so do make sure you’re at the right place.
The pork leg comes in 3 sizes. So does the crispy pork and chicken depending on the party size. Decent pork leg that comes with hard boiled eggs on the side. The crispy pork is also good. Popular place for tourists, mainly Malaysians.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Joex JF
review_text: 3 dishes small size for 460 baht, flavourful and too much for 2 person, very friendly staff, they speak chinese and english

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: yunzen96
review_text: Super delicious! On holidays, there’s a small queue of about 30 minutes. The dishes come out pretty quickly. Seven people spent 1,440 THB. Compared to the braised pork leg, I love the crispy pork belly even more. This is the best roast pork I’ve ever had!!!

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Samuel Main
review_text: This is probably quite a nice stew pork leg place, but unfortunately I tasted better one so I’m gonna give it a 4 star as it is still considered quite good. The staff is very helpful as well.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Emeline Koh
review_text:
Just the normal kind of atmosphere at any of the coffee shop in Thailand. Nothing really special about the ambience there.

The food is just normal. Nothing really very fantastic about the pork leg. But the roasted pork is not a bad choice because it’s really quite crispy.  Worth the calories to eat the roasted pork.  For the pork leg, I think the braised is not good enough for the taste which I think I have eaten better ones in Bangkok.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Crayon Lum
review_text:
Highly recommend the crispy pork here, juicy and crispy, big portions, and it best matches with their homemade chili sauce which is super appetising. Every dish is reasonable and decent.
The staff is friendly and they speak mandarin well. Beware of peak hour (after 10am) and the seat are limited.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: jejakjejak
review_text: One of my favorites place for breakfast or brunch. Generous serving. Braised Pork Throttle is superb. Tasty and tender. Roasted Pork is crunchy and juicy. There are many places in Hatyai selling similar food but this place has my thumbs up.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Vling Chong
review_text:
真心好吃😋
This pork leg rice is delicious and so lucky no long wait for me even lunch time 😊
Their service is good and serve fast , very efficient service .
Their crispy pork is so delicious and crunchy.
Definitely will visit again next time go Hatyai again☺️

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: KH (Alson)
review_text: The pork knuckles rice are flavourful. Juicy and tender. Must order the rice for it. Soup can be exempted from it as it tastes below average.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: C. G
review_text: The pork leg rice here is super authentic, the meat’s really soft and tender. It can get a bit hot and crowded, but the wait isn’t too bad. Kinda sad I missed the roast pork though, so come early if you want that! Staff were polite and looked happy, chatting and smiling as they worked.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Raymond Beh
review_text: The pig trotter and pig leg is must have. The dishes here are not as salty as compare to the stalls out there. Price are reasonable too. Staff service are amazing. Do order their chinese tea, good to cleanse away the oily after taste.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Grace Ong
review_text: Aroiiiiii, very nice food and the roasted pork is super crispy, the rice smell and taste good, I will definitely miss it!

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: celine hng
review_text: Food is just okay, nothing special. Tourist prices—small braised pork leg + roasted pork + 2 drinks = 350 baht. A bit pricey for what you get.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Elaine L
review_text: Really flavorful braised pork rice which is not too salty. The clear fishball soup with seaweed is also good and pairs really well with the pork rice. Portion is also good. This must be a local favorite as there are both locals and tourists dining here. Lots of people here even during breakfast time.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Victor Khoo
review_text: A bit overrated and expensive now due to its popularity with tourists. I came here many years ago when there are more locals eating here than tourists. That’s a shame as you don’t get that authentic feel anymore.

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: Jenny Loo
review_text: Real delicious braised Pork leg, Roast Pork  Fish Ball sea weed soup especially Thai tea 😋😋

restaurant: ข้าวขาหมูอินเตอร์ (โกชิว) เจ้าเก่า สูตรโบราณดั้งเดิม
author: JE N
review_text:
No prices on the menu.
A 3 person portion cost us about 180baht. It’s affordable but I would feel more comfortable in ordering if everything is more transparent.
However, drinks do come w a price tag at 20baht, so why not for food?

author: Alphonse Eelric
review_text: personally recommend kao-pad-poo (crab meat fried rice) &  glass noodle hot pot at this shop. price are reasonable, plenty of parking, just beware of traffic rules at this area. also beware they have afternoon closing hours from 2pm to 4pm.

author: Apple Ong
review_text:
Chance upon this restaurant when we were searching for dinner near our hotel. We got lucky and had air condition seats for family of 5. By 6:30pm on a Sunday, the shop was filled with local customers. Food was very yummy, with lotsa wok hey for stir fried option and less oily as shared by other patrons too.

The shop staffs were very local, so we communicated through Google translate for customised dish and they charged us an affordable price overall including customised dish. As one of my sisters is a vegan, they attempted to customised the dish accordingly, but may not have plant based seasoning. So do proceed with caution if you have very strict vegan diet.

No outside food and drinks were allowed, we ordered their drinks and the blue pea lemon drink is unique and refreshing. Will recommend to others who are around the area to try this restaurant.

When we left about 7pm the customers were still coming in as showed in the video.

author: Elaine L
review_text: Everything is superb here. I was traveling here in Hat Yai and this is the best meal I’ve had throughout my trip. It’s just a simple stall at the corner but everything is so good and flavorful. The crab fried rice is so generous with the crab. It’s such a simple dish but it’s so flavorful. Plus point is that it’s not oily at oil. The Tom yum is also amazing. Full with flavor, not too salty or too sour. Everything is perfectly balanced. I ordered 2 omelette. 1 with pork and 1 with crab. I definitely love the pork better as it has a better texture than the crab one. The glass noodles is the least of my fave but it’s still a great dish. What a hidden gem and will definitely return for a meal here. Price is also so reasonable with such generous ingredients. The place has a very simple layout. Hence, it does not have the best atmosphere but you can tell everyone is enjoying their meal very very much. ☺️

author: Reo. C
review_text: Wait outside to be served, Recommend fried rice, fried noodles and omelette here. Personally I think their Tomyam can be improved. Price is okay.

author: King Tohoku
review_text: Famous for its crab fried rice, which is surprisingly not too salty. Prices are very reasonable, and they even support cross-border QR payment, super convenient!

author: jasper oh
review_text: A simple corner store offering reasonable prices with generous ingredients and flavorful taste- love the seafood fried noodles and fried rice with plenty of crab meat. Plus points for being not too oily and well balance for the taste. It's great value for money and definitely on my go-to list whenever I'm back in Hatyai!

author: Duangsamorn Songmuang
review_text: Delicious fried rice with crab.good and quick service.great value.clean restaurant.

author: MudCrab Sea
review_text: Hidden gems in Hatyai. Superb local food. Always eat here and the price is reasonable cheap as well. More well known to local and less tourist.

author: Taweesilpa Achanond
review_text: As the name suggests, this restaurant is famous for its delicious crab fried rice and tasty dry sukiyaki, along with many other à la carte dishes. There's seating both indoors (air-conditioned) and outdoors in the cool breeze. The food is reasonably priced, tastes great, the owner is friendly, and the staff are well-mannered. It's a popular spot for diners, and the chefs maintain a consistent standard of taste every time. If you're in the area, I recommend this restaurant – delicious and reasonably priced.

author: Supat Limsakul
review_text: The crab fried rice was delicious, with large pieces of crab. The sukiyaki was also delicious; the broth was tasty. The fried pork was very tender.

author: Nattarika nana
review_text: If anyone comes, I recommend ordering the dry pork sukiyaki. It's very delicious. The crab fried rice is also delicious. The stir-fried chicken is also delicious. If anyone comes to Hat Yai, I highly recommend coming to this restaurant. Every time I go back to Hat Yai, I stop by to eat here. The price is not expensive. I recommend coming to eat during lunch time so you won't have to wait in line for long.

author: Wiroon Polwattana
review_text: A roadside restaurant with easy parking, delicious food, reasonable prices. Come and give it a try.

author: Fion Tan
review_text:
Crab fried rice 👍🏻
Tomyam is nice!
Thai omelette is the best!
Vermicelli noodles are also delicious.

author: 로리
review_text:
Enjoy Southern Thai-style suki in a cool and comfortable indoor setting! The stir-fried suki features meat infused with smoky flavor, bringing out the crisp texture of the vegetables. The seafood suki was initially thought to be a sweet broth, but the chili sauce and chili powder were added, and it was addictive.

Above all, you absolutely must order the authentic Thai omelet here. It's crispy, moist, and perfectly smoky, with a savory egg flavor.

They prepare your order fresh to order in their open kitchen, and everything is delicious and refreshing. If you're in Hat Yai, be sure to stop by!

author: Mukskie
review_text: The fried chicken noodles are very delicious. The dry seafood sukiyaki is good. They give a lot and have a spicy taste. The food comes out quickly and is hot. You can park on the side of the road.

author: Natchapon Nomnunthasab
review_text: This might seem like a strange comment, but I really like the macaroni at the Suki crab fried rice restaurant. It's like my mom's homemade macaroni with lots of ketchup. If anyone recommends the macaroni and suki menu to me, it's delicious. I don't really like the crab fried rice, but I'm more indifferent.

author: Apivigorn Longrak
review_text:
Food: Delicious. The tom yum is rich and flavorful, while the sukiyaki is a bit bland. You can request extra dipping sauce.

Parking: The restaurant is on the roadside, but there's no parking. There's plenty of parking across the street, just a short walk away.

Service: Very staffed. Upon arrival, the staff will bring you ice and are always on hand to assist you.

Opening Hours: The restaurant is open in two shifts: 10:00 AM–2:00 PM
4:00 PM–9:00 PM

author: Maysaya Bass
review_text:
This restaurant is another popular choice when it comes to sukiyaki. They don't have a huge menu, focusing on simple, yet delicious a la carte dishes.

I recommend:
- Mixed Dry Suki: The sukiyaki sauce is excellent, stir-fried with a fragrant wok aroma. The toppings are packed with pork, squid, and shrimp, making it a great value.
- Chicken Stir-fried Noodles: Soft, wide noodles stir-fried with a fragrant wok-fried sauce, served with a generous serving of crispy squid.

This restaurant offers a delicious, balanced meal, with portions appropriate for the price.

author: ice bear
review_text:
A fried rice shop specializing in fried rice. I walked past and smelled the aroma. I saw a few customers, so I decided to give it a try.

The crab fried rice was perfectly cooked, with the rice grains separated and fragrant. The shrimp sukiyaki was fresh and crispy, and the squid was bouncy. It was tasty, but a bit too sweet. Overall, it was a good experience.

It's cute, and there's a sink for customers to wash their hands.

The food is reasonably priced, and the service is relatively quick.

author: Venus Saksongmuang
review_text:
This restaurant's crab fried rice is absolutely delicious... The fried rice is dry and not oily, and they have a lot of crab claws. The portion is very good value for the price. The only downside is that the flavor of the fried rice isn't very rich and is a bit bland.
P.S. You have to add your own chili fish sauce and a squeeze of lime for a perfectly balanced flavor.

author: Cher Ong
review_text:
Latest visit : Visited again after half a year. Ordered 3 different dishes to try. This time around, their taste is not as good as i expect. Their signature black pomfret 🐟 is very normal but very expensive.
1st visit : Quite an interesting Thai restaurant. They don't accommodate too many customers so better make reservation before visiting. Service is not very friendly. Ordered some basic dishes but tasted delicious. The keng som is super duper spicy. For the weak heart, better don't test your limit. The price is a bit on the higher side.

author: mystic delusional
review_text: Beautiful settings, good service and good food. Drinks are not crazy sweet. Almost didn't make it there, glad we did. Should try.

author: Ong SV
review_text: Love this tiny little restaurant that serve dishes with nice plating. Food tastes amazing too. Their petai bit spicy for me. Love the crunchy crab meat spring roll too.

author: Shermin
review_text:
We’ve found the most delicious gems on this trip.
Every dish we tried here was bursting with taste. Limited seating but lucky to have a spot at this delicious spot😋

author: Juliana Ong
review_text: WhatsApp them to make a reservation way before my trip as we went on Christmas Day. They were fully booked, for walk in only avail 7pm and after. Very small restaurant so seating is limited but the restaurant is cosy and clean. Ambience is there, food is delicious and staff fine albeit attitude a bit cold. Take note they only accept cash.

author: Berry Yeap
review_text:
Authentic Thai cuisine in a charming setting! Loved the decor—you enter through a narrow path before reaching the restaurant. 😍✨

🛎️ Without a reservation, you might miss out! We walked in around 5:30 PM and were lucky to get a table. One note: the high chairs for kids here don’t have safety straps. 😅 Thankfully, my little one managed fine.

With just two of us, we couldn't order too much. We tried the recommended appetizers: crab meat spring rolls (180/270 THB), braised pork leg with radish (today's special), stir-fried mani leaves (150 THB), and the spicy seafood soup (300 THB). Plus one rice and two drinks, the total came to 1,095 THB. Overall, a great experience! 😌👌

author: oh wei
review_text:
Foods are savoury and salty . Ordered 4 dishes. The clear soup tomyum is too salty, fried pork is ok. The money vegetable with egg is the most delicious. The foods are not as delicious as the other comments mentioned. Wouldn’t recommend for others to come.The food quality  is not worth for the price we paid. You can find better authentic and local Thai food in other places in Hatyai. This is the worst I had so far.

The staff is unfriendly and rude. Can’t wait for long and roll eyes while taking order. lol what a joke. Bad service overall.

Good atmosphere and ambience though , full of decorations.

author: Lim Chin Chuan
review_text:
A big No No for me to come again...

Food is below average for the price paid...No comment on the taste as this is subjective to individual. But they cant even serve the tomyam hot...i mean temperature hot..

The worst was the bad service...Imagine a boss warn you for a 2 years old kids holding their decorative flower, saying that we need to pay if broken.

After order 5 dishes for a table of four, and 5 dishes for another table of five, I told the staff enough for now and too add later if need more..The boss stand at the back ask me to order now in rude tone otherwise will be slow serving later due to many guest.

No more next time...Thank you for the bad experience...

author: Azhar Rashid
review_text: came in earlier for dinner but not allowed to go in though many empty tables (reservation 630pm) two persons ordered appetizer and main course. waiter nor the cashier bother to ask if we were ready for main course once we finished with appetizer. cashier fridgiting for us to leave by 8pm and even told us after that to leave in 10 minutes. cashier didn’t even know what we had ordered and asked waiter to tell him what we had before issuing the bills. time spent 1 hour 30 minutes including waiting time for both appetizer and main course. cashier could have been friendly rather than faking it to be friendly. told us to leave in 10 minutes with reason to accommodate the next guest was so uncalled for as the restaurant published closing time was 8pm. took me a long time to write this review ‘cause i should have understand people in the service industry better. but not for this restaurant. food was good but not great and service has to improve.

author: Daniel L
review_text: Went there at 5.30 pm, and strangely, pretty much everything we wanted to try was sold out despite opening at 5 pm. on a Friday night. Nonetheless, spring rolls with crab meat and pork were good. Claypot pork trotter has a similar taste to Cantonese style Cheong Zheng. Couldn't taste the other signature dishes and might have had a higher rating given the limited food choices they had at that time. It was disappointing despite being conferred a Thai Select award.

author: say.w
review_text:
The decor was beautifully adorned in the timeless Nyonya style, with its intricate details and vibrant touches.
I savored the delicate flavors of white tom yum, a perfect balance of spice, and the stir-fried bitter gourd with shrimp, which offered a delightful contrast of textures. Simply exquisite and unforgettable!👍👍👍

author: SingWei Wong
review_text: Quits an upmarket experience at a Thai restaurant, food are made freshly n delicious. The serving size is quite substantial, so do not over order in the first round.

author: annt
review_text: We at the restaurant about 6.45pm, didn't make any reservation, waited 20mins in a very hot small tiny "courtyard". Decoration & presention of food looks good, Taste of food are really normal. Staffs not friendly.

author: Siwat Phansuwannakee
review_text: Delicious food, great vibes, and fair pricing. A must-visit!  👍👍

author: Lydia Chin
review_text: Amazingly delicious authentic Thai cuisine. Need to make reservations in advanced as they only have 7 tables. We walked-in and were lucky to get a table.
