Recommend to do have seperate small size portion too then we can try more dishes.

author: Dean Sonetirot
review_text: Best southern Thai food I've had in a long time. The 'Gaeng Som Pla' was the best I've ever had in all of Thailand. Amazing food at a very cheap price 👍

author: Ninven Koh
review_text: Crab 🦀blackpepper not recommend & kemsom soup a little bit salted🐟,vegetable pakliang kai 🥬is taste so yummy

author: Richard Choy
review_text: Family like restaurant. Seafood is fresh and delicious. Service is good. The restaurant boss/cook comes out to check with customers any feedback or comments on the the food serve.

author: loo jay
review_text: Food is Good taste,price also acceptable,but the white face waitress is very very bad service ( boss didn’t give salary or what?)

author: ZX Chin
review_text: Really authentic and yummy southern Thai food located at the edge of Hatyai town which makes it easy to find street parking. Food can be quite spicy but I'm sure you can ask them to reduce that. English menu is available, staff have limited English communication but they were happy to serve with a smile. Will be back to visit again soon with my friends.

author: Tan Chiew Ming
review_text: Food is definitely awesome and for local, not those designated for tourists. Should try for food lover!

author: Min Wen Mo
review_text: Skillful fried vegetable, very delicious 👍🏻👍🏻 but the taste of gaeong som might not suit me, more to sour side and very spicy. Fried Shrimp cake is worth for a try.

author: Millie Voon
review_text: The ambience and decorations are lovely. However, the food are just average and way too salty.

author: Ben Werakit
review_text: From the crowded customers since early morning speaks volume about the popularity of this restaurant. Once they give you table ticket, you can go ahead to pick by yourself the variety of homemade dim sum and other dishes so they will steam or cook for you. The taste is sumptuous and the price is reasonable. Just give it a try and see if you like it.

author: Zen Yong
review_text:
Visited Cook Chai Dim Sum during my trip to Hatyai and it was truly one of the highlights when it comes to local breakfast experiences. This spot is very popular, not only among tourists but also locals, which already tells you a lot about its reputation. If you are visiting Hatyai, this place is often mentioned as a must-try breakfast stop, and after dining here, I can see why.

The staff are friendly and attentive, despite the busyness of the restaurant. Even when the place was quite packed, the service still felt smooth and efficient, which is impressive considering the constant flow of customers.

The environment is lively and bustling, and while it can feel a little crowded at times, it is still comfortable enough for dining. In fact, the busy atmosphere adds to the charm of the place, giving you a sense of the local dining culture in Hatyai.

When it comes to food, there are a lot of varieties to choose from. The selection of dim sum is wide, ranging from steamed buns, dumplings, siu mai, har gao, and many other small plates that are fun to try and share. The food taste is decent—nothing overly fancy, but tasty and satisfying, especially for a casual breakfast. The food portion matches the price, so you get good value for what you pay. The pricing is reasonable, which makes it easy to try a little bit of everything without worrying too much about the bill.

What makes this place even more special is that other than dim sum, you can also order bak kut teh. Having a hot clay pot of herbal soup alongside a spread of dim sum gives you a hearty and unique breakfast combination that you don’t often find elsewhere. It’s definitely worth trying if you want to experience something beyond the usual dim sum.

Overall, I would say Cook Chai Dim Sum is an essential stop if you’re in Hatyai. It combines good food, fair prices, and an authentic local experience. The mix of locals and tourists dining together makes the atmosphere unique, and it gives you the feeling that you’re eating where everyone in town comes for breakfast. Definitely worth visiting at least once during your stay.

author: Rangsan Ruamyoo
review_text:
CookChai Dimsum is a lively and authentic dim sum restaurant that captures both the heart and flavor of Southern Thailand’s food culture. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere feels warm and bustling, with families, friends, and locals enjoying their meals together in a casual setting. The interior is simple yet full of character, decorated with traditional photos, bright signs, and the unmistakable aroma of freshly steamed dim sum.

The highlight here is, of course, the dim sum itself. Steaming bamboo baskets filled with classic selections such as siu mai and har gow arrive hot and flavorful, with generous fillings and a satisfying texture. Beyond dim sum, the restaurant offers impressive hot dishes. The herbal pork soup served in a clay pot is rich, aromatic, and deeply comforting, blending Chinese herbs with tender meat and mushrooms. Another standout is the sizzling hot plate dish packed with minced pork, mushrooms, and chilies, which delivers both spice and bold flavor. Pairing this with the crispy golden egg omelet creates a balance of textures that complements the meal perfectly.

Service is friendly and efficient, even with the busy crowd, and prices are very reasonable for the generous portions. Overall, CookChai Dimsum is not just a place to eat but an experience that celebrates traditional Chinese-Thai flavors. It’s highly recommended for anyone looking for a hearty breakfast or brunch in the area.

author: Jaris B
review_text: After landed at AOT HatYai, we were randomly looking for good local breakfast place. We found and we ordered dim sum, herb soup, fried buns, and Thai tea. The best part of this place is a signature dessert called "Ginkgo and Taro Sticky Rice Cake" (โอนีแปะก๊วย) SO GOOD and the rest was good, no complain.

author: rudy lee
review_text:
It’s breakfast time, we’re hungry, and let’s face it we need to eat. But that doesn’t mean we’ve lost all standards.

Now, we’re not being snobs here… just practical. Dim sum in Thailand? Really? That’s like flying to Italy and ordering sushi. Sure, it exists but should you? It’s not indigenous, it’s not iconic, and it’s definitely not what Thai kitchens wake up thinking about at dawn.

We’re in the land of tom yum and mango sticky rice. So, while dim sum might be available, it’s a no-brainer to stay away. Why settle for lukewarm siew mai pretending to be Cantonese when there’s a steaming bowl of boat noodles waiting to give you a hug?

Some might say we’re being picky. Nah — we’re just making smart choices with our stomachs. After all, breakfast is too important to waste on mediocrity.

author: Min Khant Zaw
review_text:
Not quite located near city centre but it is definitely worth a travel to this restaurant. Old school vibes with delicious hot steaming dimsum at great price!

To order: get a table and paper with that table number. Bring the paper to dimsum counter and choose whichever dimsum that looks good to you. Pass the chosen dimsums together with that paper with your table number. The freshly steamed dimsums will be delivered to you table a few minutes later.

Place is clean and staffs are attentive too.

author: long koek
review_text:
Came to eat many times....but no chance to review bcos once the dimsum served on table, everyone's chopsticks action faster than camera.

Today i managed to capture few photos.
This dim sum shop is very famous among the local Thai and even the Malaysian Chinese.

The lady boss is charming and her daughter is pretty. The guy boss will fried his golden pla tongko.

Recommended on the fish head fried koayteow. Variety of Dimsum to choose.

author: Alice Sok Peng
review_text: Chokdee closed then we try here. First time. Came around 12pm+ on Thursday. No queue. The bah kut teh and dim sum taste ok. Dim sum cost around 25/40 baht for each. Not sure which one is 25 baht or 40 baht. They will give one order list to order. The paper translated in English and it was easy for customer to order their type of bah kut teh and drinks. We ordered small bah kut teh meat only and ripened pu-er in pot. I would recommend to eat the prawn type steam dim sum. Char siew bao so so. Lor mai gai too strong five-spice powder, personally not prefer. Must eat their half boiled egg, the texture like onsen eggs and taste not like cheap eggs. All cost us around 580 baht if I not mistaken.

author: Simple Simon
review_text: So so compare to Chok Dee Dim Sum in Hatyai. No Air con room. Large size Buk Ku Tay is B380. Abit of high price.

author: Kok Hoong Lee
review_text:
6th January 2024 Visit Hatyai after 9 long months. Decided to have breakfast at Cook Chai Dim Sum together with my Thailand friend. The dim sum  isn't too bad but slightly salty for the chicken leg and pork rib. Surprisingly,  the Bak Kut Teh improved a lot compared to my previous visit.

8th March 2023 Once again, I went back to try other varieties and Bak Kut Teh. Overall, all the items that I ordered were acceptable, and the price is reasonable.

5th February 2023 My first visit to this Dim Sum restaurant in Hat Yai. All the items that I ordered were acceptable but not fantastic.  However,  I think the price is very reasonable for the amount of food that I ordered. (7 items, 1 coffee, and 1 pot of Chinese tea for 186 bahts).

author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)
review_text:
It is one of the top dimsum spots in Hatyai, but for us Malaysians, please do not compare Thai dimsum to Malaysian dimsum as well as their bak kut teh. Comparable to other dimsum spot in Hatyai, this one is pretty good, food is fresh, and choices are plenty. You can select what you want in the bak kut teh right on the spot too.

Service is good and fast and prices are competitive all over town.

author: Emeline Koh
review_text: Considering an interesting place for dim sum but a bit far from the town. The food here is not really fantastic as what social media have video.  Not as nice as Malaysia dim sum because the taste is quite bland.  The BKT is nothing fantasy and not strong. Might be good for those who like more bland food

author: Ng ys
review_text:
Food is good , very fast working when theres so much customer, thats why no need to queue for long . Xiu mai , har gao, lao sha bao is the best !!!

Bk kut teh taste diff from kl, must try

author: Pk C
review_text: A local tim sum restaurant serving bak kut teh too. Their speciality, fish head with fried flat noodle was nothing to shout about. The fish used was seabass but the flesh has some muddy taste in it.

author: adrian_97s
review_text: Recommended by the hotel owner, this dim sum joint is better than those touristy dim sum place. The bkt is good, not as good as those Klang ones but good enough. The dim sum were different than malaysian dim sum but nonetheless good.

author: Prasit Aphiphunya
review_text:
Excellent breakfast in Had Yai
Great selection of Chinese Dim Sum and others specialties dishes.

Restaurant are full of customers.  Great experiences!!!!!!

author: j s
review_text: Very good quality for the price . You walk over to the counter to select your dimsum n hand it over to be steamed. The noodle is also very good. Be sure to get the table outside if you can as the tables indoor are very cramped and the air inside a little stuffy

author: Denise
review_text: Nearby dim sum to our hotel, place is busy with locals and tourists. Good value and dishes were fresh. Thai coffee was also good. We like the ordering process, you pick the dim sum and they steam it on a tower with your table number.

author: Yelloboi Jaysen TJ
review_text: Assorted dim sum in hatyai. At least, no need long queue like cheok dee dim sum. Beautifully craft design mini dimsum. Taste average. Only steamed after ordering.

author: Shernny
review_text:
Local Favourite and It’s my favourite too.
Like their fried noodle and fish , the crunchiness of the noodle..yum.
I can just eat the Bak Kut Teh without rice as it is not to salty and just perfect.
Hatyai You Zha Kuih is a must eat. Plain without dipping sauce is my favourite.
Highly Recommend to visit.

author: Lauren Yoon
review_text:
The food comes out quickly. I think my health will get better after eating hot “bak kut teh”.  My mom said it was her first time eating bakute and it was so delicious.
It was a very good meal for the price
because many dim sum came out at a low price👍🏼👍🏼

author: Joon Wei Teow
review_text:
A popular dim sum spot offering a delightful fusion of Thai and Chinese flavors. The variety of dim sum options is impressive, catering to different tastes with flavorful and well-prepared dishes. The taste is satisfying, making it a great place to enjoy a hearty meal.

However, the dining area is quite packed with tables, making it a bit challenging to move around comfortably. The staff are busy and rushing to serve customers, which adds to the lively but slightly chaotic atmosphere. Despite this, getting a seat isn’t too difficult, and the pricing remains reasonable.

Overall, it’s a must-visit spot when in Hatyai, especially for dim sum lovers looking to experience a unique Thai-Chinese twist.

author: K M
review_text:
What's great?
Came here as Chokdee was closed. A different style of dim sum here. The music is most apt. Fried Gu Cai Kueh is the best.

What's to improve?
Found a dead housefly on one of the lettuce! Skip the salmon, it is overcooked.

Visit again?
Yes, but skip the lettuce.

author: Alice Woo
review_text: Our tour guide K. Mimi, suggested dim sum for breakfast and took us to Ama Dimsum. This restaurant is cozy, spacious and have different sections for indoor seating or with air conditioning. It’s like a ‘buffet style spread’ where you can choose and pick the dishes you like, thus no menu is needed. There is a huge variety of dimsum offered and you can eat to your heart’s content! Some dishes are pre-cooked, baked, fried and ready to be eaten. After you have selected your choices of uncooked dishes, you can hand the tray over to the staff and they will steam and warm up the food for you. We chose some traditional style dishes to try but our teenagers preferred those assorted flavoured fish balls. Overall, food was tasty and prices were reasonable with the portion size given. It’s not as authentic as the Hong Kong style dim sum but still good. This restaurant is a tourist spot for breakfast/ brunch, so expect a large crowd especially on weekends.

author: Seeker Star
review_text: The dim sum taste compared to Malaysia, I still prefer Malaysia. There is no juicy and normal taste. The space is big and will be available for you. The foods to steam but consider fast service.

author: Honzie Khong
review_text: Instead of the better know tourist dim sum place you should venture a little further out to A Ma's This has a 60 years history and the place is very nice and comfy.  Choose your dimsum and it'll be on your table in time for the tea to brew. What's good. The hargow, bitter gourd, phoenix claw Thai style, Chai kueh, are worth the try. But what's surprisingly good is their char siew wanton noodle . Can fight with KL. All in very enjoyable breakfast. Reasonable for 9 pax 1275 Baht.

author: cys edi
review_text: Food is so so and not the truly authentic Hong Kong style and standard. Probably the local interpretation of tim sum. The tim sum are pre prepared or frozen and steam on the spot. Nevertheless, it is a place to enjoy tim sum with the festivity mood as it is crowded and lots of people moving around enjoying the eats. Price is reasonable. Service is friendly and cordial. Overall quite enjoyable social eating.

author: Kenny Chong
review_text:
The variety considered a lot. Staff are quite friendly. Good not so bad. Bak kut Teh is kind of different. Overall can consider to come for breakfast.

This place is easy to find with the signature logo. The staff can converse in Mandarin.

author: CS Chai
review_text: This dim sum restaurant is among the more popular ones in Hatyai. Big sitting area including the non air-cond section at the side. Diners choose the dishes and the waitresses send them to be steamed in the kitchen. Kon loh mee, fish, pork and prawn porridge, bak kut teh and pork leg stew are also available. Free Wifi.  Accept cash only.

author: Bigman
review_text:
Came here to have my Dim sum with my friends - place is aircon and you get to pick your Dim sum and give it to the waiter with your table number
Taste to me is so so only compare the other more popular dim sum outlets
I still prefer the other Dim Sum taste

author: Rui Woon
review_text: This review got a 3 star purely base on food. Dim sum originated from the China and is consider part of Kantonese dish. If you are from China especially Hong Kong Malaysia, Singapore, I'll say give it a pass.

author: Kancy Eng
review_text:
Healthy dim sum. Fresh ingredients. Lack of varieties compared to chok Dee.
A bit bland taste.
Nice aircon environment.

author: sh ewe
review_text: AMA Dimsum has great deco homely atmosphere. Service is excellent with great selection of dim sum.

author: Peewara Chaichart
review_text: Nice place to enjoyed Breakfast. Not very crowded from Tourists tour like other Dimsum place in Hatyai but I can say the quality is great, clean and fast service. Various choices of food from Dimsum, Congee, Fried stuff and Ba-Kut-Teh(Pork stew).

author: Jiunnfa Khoo
review_text:
Congee is the best food available here for me.

Dimsums are just average. Place is cozy with air-conditioning. Worth a stop before going to songkla from hatyai

author: Nicholas Woo
review_text: Super nice dim sum with affordable price. More than 50 variants to choose from!

author: CoMeToPaPa
review_text: In Thailand if its dim sum.. Its not that big of a deal.. But for a try sure give it a shot... Malaysia dim sum is better

author: John lcf
review_text:
Very disappointed with both the food and service. The food portions were shockingly small, especially considering the high prices.

The owner seemed more interested in simply calculating the bill rather than providing an honest and pleasant dining experience.

Overall, I will not recommend "Ama dim sum" There are many other restaurants in hatyai that offer better food, fairer prices, and more honest service...
Sorry for given the poor fedback, but this is really my honest experience..

author: Tan Wei Sheng
review_text:
The foods are below par on the price paid. Limited selections and most of the items in store are pretty dull.

Service wise was a-okay.

Atmosphere is another down point as it's just too crowded. Bus loads of tourists tend to come in which seems to hype up the place but definitely not worth a 4* review.

author: Porntipa Sae-Kee
review_text:
Nice place for quick and yummy breakfast, the food is mainly DimSum: love adding the 'Cik Chow' (Chinese vinegar-black sauce on the table).

Apart from Dimsum, We also tried pork congee, it was a pork ball with egg in the congee, easy to eat and test better adding some pepper powder (personal preference) the portion is on the larger size in comparison with usual Dimsum shop that sell congee.

The wait time is reasonable and the staff could communicate in several languages. The price is reasonable, the shop is clean and good airflow. The parking is not too challenging to find (Note: we go on weekdays)

author: Alice Woo
review_text: This small restaurant serves some delicious Duck Noodles. You can have your noodles dry or with soup and with mixed meats. The noodles were very chewy and the broth tasted delicious and very flavourful. As for the duck meat.. it’s soft, tender and very tasty. They were very generous with the spring onions and crispy fried onions. You can add extra sauces if you like your noodle a bit spicier or more flavourful. We enjoyed eating the noodles very much… so yummy!

author: May L
review_text:
Decent local eats. Comfort food after all the spicy Thai food.
Bitter gourd stuffed with minced meat is so good. We had multiple servings of that dish.  All other dishes are acceptable.

Service a bit slow.

author: Terry Yee
review_text:
This is no 4 star restaurant but I would give 4 star for their duck noodle soup!

The broth is flavourful, the duck meat is just tender nice and adding on the fish sauce and chilli just make my first meal here after reaching so beautiful. ☺️

author: Chong Lip
review_text:
Great backyard Duck Noodle…amazingly nice…😋👏🏻👍🏻👍🏻
No doubt…must try if come Hatyai

author: Charles Chan
review_text: In the vicinity of Golden Crown Grand Hotel in Hadyai (this is a great option to Lee Garden which is often a choice for most Malaysian) are tons of little gem/stalls if you could not sleep and want to avoid crowded and touristy spots. I’m sharing a truly hidden gem called Hadyai Duck Noodles. Open for business only in the evening at 5pm and stay open till 4 or 5am. Local taste but the ingredients of duck parts , duck blood cubes and legs (not the drumsticks)😂😂😂😂😂. The soup is a bit peppery but lightly induced, might have some “msg” and loved the taste overall. Sharing so that other visitors can have another choice in terms of midnight snacks.

author: Bosco Khoo
review_text: There are 2 stalls here, no. 16 and no. 20. This one is right at the corner of the alleyway (No. 20). The lady boss knows Mandarin language. I chose a bowl of duck noodles soup, it tastes good. More locals are seen eating here than at the other stall. Support it.

author: Nicholas Lai
review_text: Try their duck soup noodle, is yummy. You would not get it in Malaysia.

author: WY Lau
review_text: This duck noodles didn’t meet my expectations. The soup is clear soup, a lot of pepper powder added into it. Portion is small but the duck still ok and it is soft. The place is hidden and not easy to find. The surrounding is dark and got mosquito.

author: Mel
review_text: The soup broth for our noodles was rather watered down, good if you’re looking for something light and flavours that are not overpowering. The pork balls are springy and has a good bite! Would go back again for the pork balls.

author: Harry Lee
review_text: Can order in Chinese. My dad say the current proprietress is second generation. Soup is used to be thicker. Still quite nice now.

author: dawn sun
review_text:
Simple yet so delicious! Such a comfort food.
It’s a must have, where locals would go instead of going to the Main Street.

author: Seth L
review_text:
Really great food, had trouble deciding which store to eat since there are two stores selling the same dishes. But after trying this place I definitely think this is much better.

Staff was also extremely friendly. 10/10 would recommend

author: PH Yeap
review_text: More locals came here compared to another shop selling the same thing besides. Lady boss was friendly , noodle best taken as dry version with soup separate

author: Anthony I
review_text: Good duck and chicken soup n noodles nice flavour with ginger and other spices,love the green noodles

author: Arisuありす
review_text:
Yummy duck noodles soup in the midnight..
Siew Mai a bit sweet, not my taste..

author: Yuwalak Uthairangsi
review_text: Chicken thighs is my fav and duck thighs for my mom. Been eating here since I was a kid

author: LEE TONY
review_text:
I had a very satisfying duck noodle soup at Duck Noodle Hatyai. The owner and wait staff were very welcoming and warmly welcomed everyone, making everyone feel right at home. While the restaurant isn't particularly upscale, with seating outdoors, the atmosphere is relaxed and comfortable.

The menu offers a variety of noodle options, all of which were very delicious. The duck broth was savory and the toppings were plentiful—very tasty. The prices were very reasonable for Malaysians, making it a great value.

If you enjoy noodles, especially duck noodle soup, this place is highly recommended. After learning about this place, I'll definitely recommend it to my friends and family who love noodles, and I'll definitely be back!

author: Fah Lunla And Luna
review_text:
Duck leg noodles are good. For those who like a mild ginger soup, the ginger smell is not too strong. This shop is good.
The duck meat is well-made, tender, not tough, no fishy smell. When cut, it falls off the bone. The innards are clean and well-made, no smell.

- Steamed dumplings are very delicious. Dip them with the shop's dipping sauce. There is sweet and sour sauce.
* But the shop doesn't steam them fresh in the microwave, so some parts are a bit hard, but only a little.

author: YAP FLY
review_text:
This is a three-generation duck leg noodle shop!
It's located next to the Grand Hyatt Hotel (a short walk down the street)! With decades of service and its reputation, it quickly fills up after 8:00 PM, mostly with tourists.
The clear duck leg noodle soup has a subtle ginger flavor (Malaysians might find it a bit bland, but compared to other clear broths, it's quite good). The duck leg is perfectly tender and delicious. 👍
The food was a little slow to arrive, though. We waited 20 minutes for our food, even though there were still two or three bowls ahead of us.

author: Eleanor Li
review_text: I couldn't sleep because I stayed up late, so I went out to find something to eat. It was so delicious! The two of us ate three bowls! I highly recommend the duck leg noodles!

author: Khay Yin Tang
review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I was pleasantly surprised to find that this restaurant is entirely staffed by women, including the chefs! The atmosphere was welcoming, and the food was absolutely delicious. Every dish I tried was full of flavor and beautifully presented. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a great dining experience!

author: Chow Stephen
review_text:
Open kitchen concept, surprisingly all female employees from front desk till kitchen.

We arrive is queue outside prepare chair for waiting, while waiting let you view menu and take order, mention to ours 20mins, after seating clean up the dishes are serve direct, manage well on timing.

Kem som taste normal spicy,
Egg omelette nice
Fried pork belly garlic nice
Broccoli with shrimp nice
Pepper ginger pork slices taste good
Petai Shrimp very nice.

NON-HALAL
Not plenty of parking lot
Environment clean and neat
Price cheap 6dishes with 7pax 705baht

Highly recommend

author: Notorious
review_text: First dinner here on my trip. The first thing you notice is the huge window into the kitchen, where it looks like an all-female team of chefs is at work. The food is tasty, well-seasoned, and flavorful. Communication is easy too—no problem with English here.

author: C J
review_text:
I loved their tomyam, spiciness at the very nice level. I ordered shrimp tomyam, it comes with 6 medicum sized shrimps and the portion is good for 2 people.

Waitresses are friendly and helpful by offering chairs while waiting to be seated inside.

Parking is not hard to find.

author: Supat Limsakul
review_text:
The food is delicious, flavorful, and the portions are generous. The ingredients are of high quality.
The service is fast and efficient.

author: Li Yuen
review_text: Tried this Thai restaurant and really enjoyed it! The fried seabass with chilli sauce was slightly spicy and tasty with a nice crunch, but the tom yum soup was definitely our favourite… so flavourful and comforting. Will be back again!

author: Elanggo Krishnan
review_text:
Shop is very clean.
Tomyam seafood taste great.
Sea fish not fresh but cooking flavor taste well.
Stir Fried Seafood with Curry Powder taste good too.
Basil Pork moderate taste.

author: yin jia goh
review_text: Nice food with reasonable price👌😋 but I think tomyum soup can be more spicy abit

author: Chong Lip
review_text:
Very nice Authentic Thai Food! Best in Hatyai!!!
Michelin standard! 😍😋👏🏻👏🏻👍🏻
In summary, best of the rest!😋👏🏻👏🏻👍🏻

author: Jeff Chua
review_text: Food is nice. Service is good. Got English menu available. Price reasonable

author: Stacey K
review_text: Another pleasant surprise. A restaurant we went after seeing long queue outside the restaurant for a few days. Good and cheap Thai dishes. Dishes portion more suitable for 1-2 pax

author: Aves Khiung
review_text: Good foods. Place is clean. Open kitchen with many staffs. Foods are served very quick after order, maybe due to at least 7 staffs in the kitchen.

author: Kuan Fung Chin
review_text: Friendly staffs, fast service, good food, reasonable price

author: EWE DE LUNN
review_text: Loved by the local, the food very nice, tomyum can choose the spiciness, fried vegetables good to taste, fried squid is a must!!

author: Lee Hoon Loh
review_text: One of the best local Thai Food restaurants ever tried compare to those other over high rated restaurants, this one very good 👍🏻

author: Wen Chien Cheang
review_text: We ordered these dishes for 4 adults. More than enough, love the big portion served. They had an open kitchen, the kitchen is clean, able to watch the chef cooking performance too. Noticed most of the chefs are women, the staff were friendly too. Most importantly, the dishes were cheap, value for money.

author: Sujie Won
review_text: Nice place to have some simple Thai Food😋. Tom yam is spicy 🌶️ the veggie is the best especially I love the Kailan 👍👍👍. Will visit again 😉

author: CS Lim
review_text: taste very nice with reasonable price. need to queue, but won't wait too long

author: Mauricio
review_text: Ordered a curry paste chicken ala carte, and frankly it was disappointing. The chicken were small fragments of bone with tiny slivers of meat. Taste-wise it was ok, nothing out of the ordinary. Poor value.

author: Peter Tan
review_text: Good place to eat. affordable price, clean and new. thai and Chinese style cook food

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: EXOL & NCTzen
review_text: Too many options of what to eat from their fresh seafood, fishballs section, meats, ready to eat food, their desserts and more. Overall food here is very good and delicious. The seafood is fresh. U can either cook yourself or ask them to cook for you. There are some you  can make to order just have to let them know your table. Their drinks also have many options. Service is also very good. Just that if u are not local, u may need to go by ehailing as it’s quite far from the main city. Recommend to try. We all came out full and happy.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Bordin Jindawattanawong
review_text: This is one of the best mid-to-high-range buffets in the city. I loved that many dishes were cooked-to-order rather than sitting under heat lamps, which kept everything tasting fresh and premium. We decided to go for the 498 Baht seafood package instead of the basic tier, and for the most part, it was excellent value. However, the reason I’m not giving it a full 5 stars is that I was really expecting to see fried mantis shrimp with garlic on the menu for this price point, but unfortunately, they didn't serve it.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Teng Sook Yin
review_text: Wide range of food and varieties. Given 2 charcoal stoves. One for Mookata and for BBQ. Can choose to cook ourselves or ask them to cook, especially the larger items like fish and crabs. The seafood is fresh. The salt grilled fish was delicious. Just the environment was very hot due to heat from the stoves. But that is expected I guess. Not all areas can be installed with fans. Still enjoyed the meal.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Ju Nguyen
review_text: The diversity of the food, the food freshness, the service, the outdoor atmosphere, everything is excellent if you have a big stomache.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: W T
review_text:
Visited what I’d call the best seafood mookata spot I’ve tried in Hat Yai, and it was an unforgettable experience. At around 500+ baht per person, the price is slightly higher than most local barbecue places, but I personally feel it’s worth every baht for the quality and variety offered. The seafood selection was outstanding — fresh river prawns, squid, clams, and fish, all prepared perfectly for grilling.

What makes this place unique is a special section where you can hand over your chosen raw ingredients for the staff to cook according to your preferred style, which adds a personal touch to the meal. I focused mainly on the seafood, which was flavorful and fresh, while my companion sampled the meat and felt it wasn’t quite on par with the seafood. Still, for anyone craving a satisfying seafood mookata experience in Hat Yai, this spot is definitely a must-try.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Eskimo 0308
review_text:
25feb25.Anybody wanna join me tonight? I am solo traveler.
Finally manage to taste the food. Value for money. Many dishes didn't try because I solo dining. Next trip will come with friends. The staff polite and friendly. So sad as 8pm they stop service prawn cooked vermicelli.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Jess Lim
review_text:
No time limit, you can eat from 4pm to 11pm

Extensive selection of seafood, dessert, vegetables and meat.

You get to choose the cooking style for the seafood you have chosen.

The waitress cleaned up the table and refilled the food on time.

Not air-conditioned but the place has good ventilation.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Yuri Tan
review_text: Worse experience ever do not eat here if Yr here, here's recap on my part, my family was trying to enjoy the buffet yes we ordered the normal package we payed around 300baht, but when we eating the next table besides us ordered the package that includes premium seafood, they offered my family a crab, and and then the workers came by and warned me us once tht we can't eat the seafood, Ok look BUT is the table next to us offering to us, and then the second time the worker comes and they did not say anything about they will charge my family table extra 298 baht just because OF ONE CRAB that the other table offered, they also stated they will charge if they seen us taken the item BUT the sign they pointed at IS NOT FOR THE PRICING that they gonna charge if anyone taken the seafood

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: yow suen tho
review_text:
Quite extensive seafood if early. If late, also still well stocked.
But place quite large -about 100 tables so getting to the raw food material to cook is quite a way to go if not seated towards center.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Daniel L
review_text: Huge assortment of seafood and meat options. Indoor seating is warm, outdoor seating is cooler but is not shaded. 498 baht per pax for access to all seafood and meat options. Grilled whole fish, horseshoe crab roe salad among the selections. Seafood were all fresh.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Valentino Tan
review_text:
what i like about this place is i can choose my own fish and let them cooked the style that is being offered.
Theres 20 options for a variety of seafood, fish, prawns, shells.

big fat prawn and fish
theres 2 charcoal pot, one for grilled one mookata style.
the salt fish with lemongrass inside is nice.
this place good as i can smoke. its in the open

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Leia
review_text:
We arrived at 4:30 PM and found several vans already there. This is an open-air restaurant without air conditioning.

The seafood buffet is priced at THB498 per adult and THB198 per kid.

The sheer variety of food is overwhelming. The seafood is fresh. You have three options: order and have it cooked for you, choose from their ready-to-eat dishes, or grill the food yourself.

There's no time limit for dining. Worth to try it.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Joey Ng
review_text: Best of both worlds, where local Thai style dishes and Thai mookata can be experienced in one location. Seafood choices was plentiful, styles of cooking was variable too. Choose to grill or Mookata your way through the extensive food choices of meat and seafood or pick your choice for them to cook up a pretty legit Thai style dish. Side dishes, local dessert, ice cream, fruits and drinks choices were awesome too. THB 498 per pax is such an awesome deal, with Eat All You Can No Time Limit. Only suggestion for improvement is the condition of their chairs which can be improved in terms of cleanliness. Plenty of parking.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Toto Ong
review_text: Fully recommended moo-ka-taa buffet with exquisite seafood selection like a seafood market. 498baht per person with unlimited time. Must come early to take your Q number. Plenty of car park provided.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Eric TJF
review_text:
One of the famous all-you-can-eat buffet in Hatyai with seafood package priced at only 498 thai baht per person.
Accept Malaysia national QR payment method as well; easy and convenient, no cash is required 👍
Be sure to be at here earlier during weekends as it's quite pack

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Katrina Felix
review_text:
Nice food, worth the price. It’s naturally ventilated so it can be warm. Seafood all fresh. There’s a combination of cooking it yourself and selecting the seafood and the restaurant cooking it for you. Either way , all delicious.

I forgot to take the fresh uncooked seafood but you can see from all the photos shared on google reviews- still the same now.

I recommend you give it a try when you’re in Hatyai!

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Ong Lieh Yan
review_text:
Seafood galore!!! Fresh seafood everywhere and many types to choose from too. Was impressed with some fresh big sized fishes there. Even the bigger sized squids are available. Meaty section is there too. Provided with one Thai hotpot and a charcoal grill. You can cook your own or ask them to cook for you. Desserts from shaved ice to ice cream. Definitely a must-go to place when you are in Hat Yai.
My personal recommendation: Go for the seafood AND most important ask them to cook!! 😀

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Yenestc Lim
review_text: This is super nice experience! Variety of choice, pork leg very nice, seafood very fresh, non stop to top up from staff! Need to book in advance for better reserve of table! Worth with money gave!

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Cher Ong
review_text: Very spacious area for seafood buffet & mookota. I'm here just for the cooked seafood as I'm too lazy to bbq it on my own. It's way more convenient & save the work and heat. There are a lot of seafood variations & other side items. Dessert, salad & drinks are also available. It's definitely worth the money even if you're not with a big appetite.

restaurant: Buffet Rimnam Mookata And Seafood Hatyai
author: Peekaboo
review_text:
Eat all you can!! Great choices of fresh seafood and meat!! For tourists you will be offered many local Thais cuisine, so eat all you can! Make sure you bring empty stomach so its worth your money 🤩🤩
They offer payment via both cash and QR (non Thai can use TnG etc)

Toilets can be improved 🙂🙂

author: Notorious
review_text: Trying Bingsu for the first time, and what better place than the country where it originated. The shaved ice is cooling and refreshing, and you can adjust the sweetness yourself with the syrup provided. The café itself is cozy and clean, though the outdoor tent seating isn’t particularly impressive. A highlight for me was the friendly cat lounging out front 🐱, which added a bit of charm to the visit.

author: Kenson Luk
review_text: Best shaved ice I have ever had. I got the Thai milk tea bingsu. It had 3 kinds of bubbles and croutons inside, whip cream and sliced almonds, the ice was very soft and light.

author: Yee Sheng Kwan
review_text: FANTASTIC!! The best Bingsu I had tried ever. Really impressive 🔥 Good photo and good desserts! Jackson Wang must try thiss!

author: Chin Yan
review_text: The details they put into the deco and the food is spectacular. Recommended to be there during brunch, crowd starts around 1-2pm. Got the salted egg coconut bingsoo, unsure of the original name. Hint of saltiness but sweet. Free parking available here.

author: aqilah yahya
review_text: This café is aesthetically beautiful—cute and sleek. It has a nice ambiance, making it a great spot to hang out and take photos. The food is delicious, the service is excellent, and we didn’t have to wait for a table. My friends and I had a great time here.

author: May Choo
review_text:
Same taste as the original branch in Chiangmai! I've ordered the Earl grey bingsoo that came with boba. As it's not that sweet, I pretty love its taste. The bingsoo is very mellow and smooth. Adding sweet boba is a great combo.
The staff can also communicate in multi languages. However, it's super crowded at lunch time.

author: W T
review_text: Portions are big, and the desserts taste alright—my companion enjoyed them. We had the Thai tea bingsu and panda coconut toast with a lemon tea. The total came to about 580 baht.

author: Leanna
review_text:
I love everything about this place. The food, service and the atmosphere, everything is great!
Nothing to complain and totally worth the hype!

We chose the typical thai’s specialty; sangkaya & mango.
The mango ice shave is so sooo good! Not too sweet. And the mango is not too ripe. So, it was a bit sour and it compliments the sweetness from the ice.

And their sangkaya toast also so yumm! Sangkaya with coconut ice is such a perfect combo.

author: Ziee Chiam
review_text: Love this place, just look at the picture. No queue as we were the first to arrived. If you come late, then yes long queue. Staffs were friendly. Desserts were awesome. So so so good. Love it!!! Will definitely revisit when I go Hat Yai again.

author: FARAH LIYANA
review_text:
We had much fun having a good ice-shaved (bingsu, garlic bread, caramel pudding, & drinks at here! 100% satisfied cuz all hot selling menu are so mouthwatering and delish! We will definitely come here again!

The ambience and deco are so cozy & warm. We were so lucky by the time we arrived, the cafe was not so crowded. We enjoyed the most!

author: Chian
review_text:
Still my favourite shaved ice spot in hatyai!!! Good food, good environment and great service. In love with their salted eye shaved ice!!

Tried their croffle for the first time and turned out a BOOMMM!!!! regret to try it too late!!! We ordered the kaya croffle , it’s so nicee mannnn!! Buttery and crunchy yummy! End ii we ordered the second one : salted egg croffle, it’s still good but i would recommend the kaya one more ❤️

author: Yaw Cheng Chong
review_text: Great place to chill and take pretty ins photo, salted egg bingsu and caramel bingsu are nice. Definitely would come back to try other flavour

author: Bobby Lornimitdee
review_text: It's comfortable for families, with average prices and great flavors. I especially love their Dirty Coffee.

author: Liaw Ben Hsia
review_text: Second visit here, but sadly the desserts were below expectations. The Thai milk tea especially was a big disappointment – definitely not worth the price. Overall, not a satisfying experience.

author: Anasuya Roshan
review_text:
This is a fantastic spot for satisfying your sweet cravings.

The bingsu servings are impressively large – easily shared among three adults, making it perfect for a group dessert outing. The finely shaved ice, paired with a variety of toppings, ensures a refreshing and delicious treat.

However, the highlight for me was the waffles. They were perfectly crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, with just the right amount of sweetness. Paired with their selection of toppings and syrups, the waffles were absolutely delightful.

The ambiance is cozy and inviting, making it a great place to hang out with friends or enjoy some quiet time with a good dessert. The staff are friendly and attentive, ensuring a pleasant experience.

author: Nurkhalida Rahman
review_text: Very beautiful place. Went there in the evening Saturday, less people. Washroom complete with bidet. The wild berry ice shave so good, not too sweet. Clear matcha drink also nice tops with caramel. Will repeat again.

author: Alvin Toh
review_text: My first visit here. Place was nicely done up, air conditioned, clean and comfortable. Do prepare for the long wait for seats during weekends and peak hours. They have a small open field right beside the cafe with some chairs provided, so maybe you can consider takeaway or relax there while waiting for your table. Deserts here were pretty decent and nicely done. Drinks were normal.

author: LimKoppi
review_text: Our driver suggest this place to us. Need to take number and queue ya. Need to queue at least half an hour to one hour but it is worth to queue 😆😁 we all loves this cafe very much. All food and dessert is nice! And wish to go again.

author: Sharon Chen
review_text: Love the desserts here! Everything is fresh and beautifully presented. The bingsu is super soft and melts in your mouth. Cozy environment and friendly staff!

author: Wong Kok Ming
review_text:
The place is pack with tourists from all over the world to try their food and bingsu.

The environment of the place is very comfy and comfortable to enjoy food and drinks with friend and family.

The staff here is very friendly and helpful.  Number is given for the customer to wait for their turn and there is a bar code where you can scan and see their menus before getting your table.

The food here is delicious and got variety of selection to choose from.

author: Zen Yong
review_text:
If you’re visiting Hatyai, Chokdee Dim Sum is definitely one of those breakfast spots that locals and tourists alike recommend, so I decided to give it a try. It was a good experience overall, and I can see why it’s so popular.

The staff here are friendly and attentive, even though the place was quite busy during breakfast hours. Service was quick, and they patiently guided me through the dim sum selection process, which is a nice touch if it’s your first time there.

There are two dining areas – the main store and a newer, more spacious dining area just opposite. I chose to sit in the main store, as it is closer to the dim sum counter and has a more authentic, bustling atmosphere. The main store feels a bit more “classic,” while the newer section seems to cater to larger groups and tourists.

The price is reasonable and in line with what you would expect for a well-known dim sum place. The portions are small, but they match the price, which makes it easy to order and try a variety of dishes without wasting food.

Taste-wise, the dim sum itself was decent – I would say it was just ordinary compared to other places I have tried, but still enjoyable. I also ordered their Bah Kut Teh, which was slightly salty for my liking, though taste can be very subjective and others might find it just right.

Overall, Chokdee Dim Sum is a nice breakfast experience if you are in Hatyai. The variety of dishes, reasonable pricing, and lively atmosphere make it worth a visit. Just be sure to go early, as the place can get really crowded during peak hours.

author: Alphonse Eelric
review_text:
This place offers variety of Chinese style dim sum & Bak Kut Teh (Chinese clay pot sup with pork). Pricing wise is reasonable, but some time it might crowded with tourists from other province & Malaysia. Parking are plenty, park free at roadside, but beware! do not park at red white line or against the traffic as your car will be locked by traffic police & unlocking fee is whooping 1000baht!!
They have another hall opposite their outlet, customer can take seat at either side & order food they want.

author: Jony
review_text:
Since 1996, this beloved spot has been serving up mountains of delicious, affordable dim sum. The experience is part of the fun: just pick your favourites from the counter, and the staff steams them on the spot, delivering each one piping hot to your table.
Don't let the crowds scare you away! Their efficient system means you'll be seated in no time, ready to dig into classic dim sum or their famous Bak Kut Teh. With three locations, it’s easier than ever to get a taste of this local legend.

author: K M
review_text:
What's great?
Loved the you tiao with Kaya dip the most. Got 2 sets of it. Yam bun is so nicely oozing out! Amazing place with nice decorations. Get a seat number slip from the main shop, then cross the road to choose your steam dim sum from another shop, then cross back. No need to go over, if you do not want steamed stuff. Very crowded, but moves very fast.

Visit again?
Yes!

What's to improve?
Bak kut teh and steam pork ribs are ok. Not fantastic.

author: Henry Tan
review_text: Very reasonably priced and delicious dim sum in Hat Yai, definitely a must-go location 🫖🥢

author: Winther Tan
review_text: Very nice dim sum in hatyai. Always full, so need to go early. They r famous for their bak gut teh, but to me it seems too salty. But the dimsum is nice compare to many other places in Thailand n price is very affordable.

author: Yuhng Yeap
review_text:
Amazing dimsum place, definitely not overhyped. There's still quite a queue even at 10am. You order by taking a table number and a tray from the stuff, and pick any dimsum you want from their wide range of selection. They will steam it and sent it to your table. They have multiple stores with seating area around the block, some seatings stores are opposite the road.

They also have a bakkutteh store which I highly recommend to give it a try. The soup is a bit different from what we usually have in Malaysia, but still very delicious. Best part is definitely their pork cuts inside, super tender and soft, literally melts in your mouth.

Highly recommend getting more of their Thai specialty dimsum instead of classic ones you usually see in Malaysia for a more unique experience. Some highlights includes the steam cob and meat dimsum, various types of siewmai, and glutinous rice chicken. Their har gao is a flop tho, dry and tasteless, can skip it.

Recommended.

author: Min Khant Zaw
review_text:
Bustling old school dimsum place right in the middle of the city. A must have for breakfast! Also, their thai tea is one of the best in the city. Who knew pairing thai tea with dimsum will be such a great combo!

Friendly staff. Room with aircon available across the road. Plenty parking spaces available on the side of the road.

Very affordable price.

author: Gina K
review_text:
I understand that everyone has their own taste when it comes to dim sum. I’ve tried dim sum in many places—both in Thailand and abroad—but honestly, this is the one place I just don’t understand the hype.

Most of the customers here were foreigners, with only a few Thai diners. As for the taste, I personally found the dim sum quite disappointing. It was edible, but definitely not something I’d come back for.

That said, I really appreciated the staff here. They were friendly and attentive, and the service was excellent. While the food wasn’t for me, the warm hospitality made the experience more pleasant, but overall, this place still didn’t meet my expectations.

author: Ju Nguyen
review_text: From the food quality, service to atmotspher, personally I would like to give 5 star.

author: Stephie C
review_text: They got 3 shops here, waiting time around 10 mins only. Bak kut teh tastes quite good. Overall dim sum not bad. Worth for a try.

author: I'm Done
review_text:
A wide variety of dim sum options at very affordable prices, a table full of food for four cost us only 700 THB. Service was great and the space itself was roomy and comfortable.

However, one downside I would say was the staff's overwhelming presence. We were the only customers at the time, and over 10 staff members gathered closely around our table, watching us intently. I understand they wanted to provide prompt service, but it felt a bit excessive, a little more personal space for us would be so much better 😂

author: Raymond Beh
review_text: The dim sum is very fresh, the taste is good as well, hence the high review online. Strongly recommand to try their bak kut teh, way above my expectation, as the dish is not a star within thailand. I would say that this is as good as some of the best bak kut teh in Malaysia. Must try dish here in Hatyai

author: VC Loh
review_text: Love the dim sum and bakuteh, very fresh ingredients and nice.

author: Songren Lim
review_text: Decided to check this place out due to the close proximity to my accommodation. It was a delightful experience. The Ladyboss was friendly and ushered me to the air conditioned dining area which was a nice surprise. Felt their Bak Kut teh was decent but would definitely return for their unique dim sum dishes and variety.

author: Simon C
review_text: Great restaurant. You go to the main places on one side and then get a number and seat. With this number you cross the street and choose the food you want to eat. Mainly you find a variety of great tasting dim sum. The prices are super fair. With about 12-14 plates, beer and water we ended up with about 550 BHT. Would definitely come again!

author: Rohee Lee
review_text: The dim sum are really tasty! Their portion is small and you can try variety of choices. Ordered Bak kut Teh and the meat is tender, soup is really good. Very satisfying with their food, will go and eat again for next trip

author: Jaime See
review_text:
a different style of dim sum - miniature size.  not of d same variety 1 wld find in a typical dim sum restaurant.  taste has more of a fish sauce base, but subtle enough to taste d meat.

tried d bak kut teh which was a bit flat, not of d herbal flavor of klang, malaysia.  haadyai's bkt more on d salty side, more like a meat soup.

however, d char kuew teow was not bad at all.  has 'wok hei' n tastes good.

the milk tea n coffee were not up to par at all, but they use a squarish cup for their chinese tea.  a pleasing visual indeed...

author: Dr. WH Tan
review_text: The food here was undeniably delicious, but if you want to try their signature dim sum, you will need to place your order from across the street. This unique setup might require a bit of extra effort, but it is well worth it for the opportunity to savor their specialty dumplings, buns, and other delicacies.

author: Nivic Aun
review_text:
Stepping into Dim Sum Delight is like entering a culinary paradise for dim sum lovers. This cozy eatery offers an authentic and unforgettable dining experience, perfect for both seasoned dim sum enthusiasts and newcomers alike.

The ambiance is warm and inviting, with traditional decor that exudes charm and a hint of nostalgia. The layout is designed to encourage a communal dining experience, making it a great place for gatherings with family and friends.

The service at Dim Sum Delight is top-notch. The staff are friendly, attentive, and efficient, ensuring that your dining experience is smooth and enjoyable. They are knowledgeable about the menu and happy to make recommendations, which is especially helpful given the wide variety of dishes available.

The star of the show, of course, is the dim sum. Each dish is a testament to culinary excellence, crafted with fresh ingredients and cooked to perfection. The menu offers a great balance of classic favorites and unique creations, ensuring there’s something to please every palate.

Overall, Chokdee Dim Sum is a must-visit for anyone looking to savor the best of dim sum. With its welcoming atmosphere, excellent service, and mouthwatering dishes, it promises a dining experience that you’ll want to repeat time and again.

author: Under Cover
review_text:
We came here for lunch and were really happy with our overall experience. The restaurant is located just a couple of streets away from the main beach road, making it easy to find but still quiet enough to relax. The atmosphere is casual, clean, and comfortable, and the staff was very friendly and attentive. All dishes were freshly prepared and arrived quite fast.

I started with a Caesar salad, which looked nice and fresh, although there was a bit too much dressing for my taste. I would have preferred it lighter, but overall it was still enjoyable. We also ordered chicken wings on skewers, which looked amazing and came with a delicious sauce — perfectly grilled and full of flavor.

Another highlight was the Laab, a Thai-style minced meat salad with mint, onion, and herbs. It was served cold and packed with flavor — perfectly seasoned and very authentic. We also had squid with sauce, which looked great and tasted just as good. Another dish we tried was chicken in coconut sauce, which was absolutely delicious — creamy, flavorful, and perfectly balanced.

For drinks, we had water and pink milk, which was very sweet but refreshing. The restaurant offers a wide variety of dishes — both Thai and Western options like pizza and sandwiches — plus a great selection of beers.

In total, we paid only 530 Baht for everything, which is incredibly affordable for such a touristy area. At the end, they even gave us a small mint candy with the bill — a nice touch. Overall, a great experience and definitely a place we’d recommend to anyone visiting the area.

author: Singh G
review_text: Overall it’s good expressive, i have been to oasis, coffee club and here and it tastes near to same. Good place. Got to visit this place after watching one of YouTube video to taste authentic Thai food and I’m not disappointed . Just a reminder, Pad Thai is noodles and not rice. Shrimp pineapple rice were best of all the menu. They also have bottle beers costing around 100 bhatt. Also the washrooms were super clean.

author: Neil Fairley
review_text: We have eaten here many times. The food, atmosphere and service are all tremendous it I superb value for money too. The satay sauce is to die for. Please if you read this get me email and send me the recipe so I can make it at home. 🙏photo says it all.

author: Raj G
review_text: Everything on the menu was served properly. Food is delicious. The pad Thai is on top of the world. Great drinks to complement Coconut water is definitely not something you should miss and stay away from the hot sauce obviously dip it in, add photos and videos but take too much of it and you get the heat

author: Ashley T (Shark and Eagle)
review_text: We are from Melbourne and solid fan of Doo Dee Melbourne, I was surprised Doo Dee was originally from Thailand I thought it was just some random name. The food is good and price is fair, I had curry crab for 350b, which would be cost 5 or more times for in Melbourne. Very happy and would def come back again.

author: Chong Wee
review_text: Very authentic Thai foods... Somtum is tasty,for the baked fish was awesome,the Thai curry fried crab really good

author: Dee D'Cruz
review_text:
Great little restaurant with very reasonable prices and huge variety of food, fresh seafood and even specialties like frogs legs which we tried!

We sat in the air conditioned restaurant and had probably the best Pad Thai of our trip! The fried rice and pork omelette were also delicious and we loved the Morning Glory (love adding some greens)!

Bonus points for the Iced Thai Tea being served ice cold and delicious!

author: Prianca bakshi
review_text:
Absolutely love the food here!!! I used to eat almost every day. So so reasonable too!
But, the staff, oooff. Most of them are rude and full of themselves. The one star goes because of those couple of waitstaff who were barely doing their job well!

Do try their red curry, cashew chicken, tom yum with fish, pad kra pao -some of my favourites.. but almost everything here was decent! Oh and also ask them to give you their seafood sauce. Yum yum!

author: Jakub Chrzanowski
review_text: Portions are a little small, also the taste was just so so. I had much better experience in Patong.

author: Darren Cantwell
review_text: The food is quite nice and it’s affordable. I did find a small hair amongst the chicken which is why I took off one star. The flavor was good.

author: Mika Salmela
review_text:
Very good quality food for a cheap price. Ice coffee was great (sweet) and the breakfast set tasted better than many hotels that have over twice the price. Kind service.

Pad thai was good.

I asked for Thai spicy tom yum soup and it truly was Thai spicy, be careful what you ask for. Must have been one of the spiciest so far. Still, the taste was amazing.

The neighboring table was praising even the chicken wings. I don't think I will go to any other restaurant for thai food this whole vacation.

author: Mia mia
review_text: the fried chicken wings and tom yum with fish are must order! Really enjoy the dinner with Thai foods here.

author: shin ri
review_text:
Food is great, price is cheap as well. Love their Tom yum soup with fish, it's exactly what I wanted.
They open from 9am onwards, so we had breakfast here everyday.

author: celinda.h
review_text: We found the portion size of the chicken basil to be quite small but the thai green curry (not pictured) was quite decent and delicious. Thai milk tea was not great and tasted a bit watered down. Great prices though! So cheap and would go back. Lots of staff who were very attentive.

author: Ruslan Panahov
review_text: Real authentic local food at crazy very good prices!!! Try not to fall for fake tourist traps guys compare any restaurant prices with this place and you can understand what must be near real price!

author: Seemantini Bose
review_text:
My go-to place in Phuket. Excellent food, absolutely reasonable. Heaven for seafood lovers like me. Their grills are to die for! Try out the grilled prawns, green pepper crabs, grilled white snapper.

Strategically located in Patong, you can either choose to walk from patong beach/ bangla road or take a tuktuk that will charge you 200 TBH. It’s adjacent to the hotel ‘Natural Resort’.

They have two seating areas, one open and the other one AC. Service is great and the waiting time for food is quite fast.

Don’t miss it if you enjoy seafood!

author: Natalia Reliszko
review_text: We visited this restaurant on our first day in Thailand, and it was outstanding. We traveled all over Thailand from Chiang Rai to Phi Phi and returned on our last day, curious if our impressions were a result of our first day of Thai cuisine, but no... the food was delicious, not overly contrived, not too sweet, not too heavy. Everything is fresh and served very quickly. AUTHENTIC UMAMI <3

author: Dru Lu
review_text: Ordered the grilled giant prawn and crabs which are the most expensive items here. But they grilled the crap out of it, till the point there’s no moisture left in the meat and it’s like tasting prawn jerky. The crab meat was so dry you can hardly get any meat from the claw. Do not order!

author: Weng Hau Hoon
review_text:
This is one of the restaurant with good food that the locals and tourist eat in Patong.
The BBQ Chicken Wing is delicious but the stir fry pork with mint can be skipped if you can't eat spicy food as it's actually quite spicy.
The Thai Iced tea and Rose Syrup with milk is tasty and cooling especially during hot weather.
Overall damage is about 500 baht and would definitely revisit again to try their Grilled fish and seafood.

author: Fan
review_text:
We came here because this place had such good reviews, but many other people thought that too. In the evening the queue is big and expect to wait a few minutes before you can enter.

The food is good, but not really great in my opinion.

What I loved was the original Thai bowl that they served the drinks in!

author: Tlangelani Mkhombo
review_text:
I went last week saturday around 20h00. It was quite busy but you could move around. It has a lot of markets selling Thai food from proper meals like pad thai and stir fried rice, to finger food like spring rolls and pork on a stick. They also sell fruits, some prepared and ready to eat (no fruit salads though). They also had some clothes and bags. The interesting ones were the guys with scorpions where you could take a picture for 10 baht if not buying. Vendors keep stopping you to buy from them, which is to be expected but can get annoying, but just refuse politely.
Prices for food was reasonable and written, so no negotiations needed. They were playing some music but you could talk. There was a bar for drinks where you could sit down and rest and eat your food from other stalls as long as you buy something from them, too. I went for food stalls and the vibe.

author: Frank P
review_text: 20251205 - night market near patong beach that is opened till late night. Sells variety of seafood, thai food, drinks and desserts. It is considered quite pricey compared to bangkok. Ordered iced thai tea, iced thai coffee and mango sticky rice. The drinks are ok but the mango sticky rice is disappointing, with dry rice that sticks together and mango that is not so sweet. I would consider going to nearby mall food court to eat instead. The roti banana nutella outside the market along the main road is nice though, with ripe and sweet banana.

author: Mauricio
review_text:
Love this night food market located right in the middle of Bangla Rd
Awesome local street food including a huge variety of seafood amongst other great dishes
It gets pretty busy which adds to the atmosphere and is a great place to eat before a night out on the town

author: Rajeev Rajan
review_text:
Great place to have some nice seafood & other non-vegetarian delicacies - like chicken & other meat! Be ready to bargain to get the best deal.

Too crowded on weekends & rightly so with all the party options around.

author: Krasimira Valkanova
review_text: Pretty good fresh sea food one can get in here but be careful because they're cheating with the scales and charge more than they should. We checked a few places before we decided where to eat. For example we told one guy to measure two of the big tiger prawns and they we half a kg on his scale. Went to another picked two smaller tiger prawns and it showed 600kg on his scale.... so yeah watch out. We've chosen yummy yummy and it was very yummy :)) fried rice with vegetables, one octopus skewer and two huge tiger prawns with garlic butter sauce, it was cooked to perfection and just enough for two people. And all together our dinner was half as cheap if went to a restaurant so didn't regret it and will go back again. 4 stars only because some of them are cheating. 5 stars for food

author: Glynis Brown
review_text:
Love the excitement of Bangla specially the street food.
Many thanks to Ceylon and staff. Done a wonderful job cooking our food

author: Toon Tran
review_text:
Bangla Night Market: Hits, Misses, and the Famous Roti!
The Bangla Night Market (บางลา ไนท์ มาร์เก็ต) offers a buzzing late-night culinary hub near Patong Beach, selling a variety of seafood, Thai food, drinks, and desserts until the early hours.
What to Expect:
* Offerings & Price: You can find almost any kind of street food, though it is considered quite pricey compared to Bangkok's markets.
* The Drinks: Your order of iced Thai tea and iced Thai coffee were noted as "OK," serving as standard refreshments.
The Disappointments:
* The market's famous Thai dessert, mango sticky rice, was unfortunately disappointing, described as having dry rice that sticks together and mango that is not so sweet.
The Recommended Alternative:
Based on this experience, a better dining alternative for overall quality is suggested: "I would consider going to nearby mall food court to eat instead."
The Must-Try Street Food:
Despite the disappointing mango sticky rice, don't miss the street vendors just outside the market: the roti banana nutella along the main road is nice, made with ripe and sweet banana—a perfect, sweet ending to your evening!
Bangla Night Market
(Near Patong Beach)

author: Aman Chawla
review_text:
Bangla Night Market, Phuket 🌃🍢🔥
A vibrant spot for Thai street food, fruit shakes, and quick shopping, located just off Bangla Road. After exploring the market, you’re steps away from top pubs and dance clubs like Illuzion, Tiger Nightclub, Sugar Club, and Barfunk — perfect for partying, live DJs, and late-night vibes. Busy, colourful, and great for food + nightlife in one place!

author: mohd idham
review_text: Fresh Seafood , choose and they will cook .Come here only for eating. Its cheap compare to other place . Portion and drink also big.. 😁

author: Nabeal Nasser
review_text: To find the truly good luxury spots, you have to gatekeep a little. They’re not obvious—you need to earn them by looking hard. Be patient, explore, and eventually you’ll discover those hidden gems worth everything.

author: Rinku
review_text: Best place for enjoyment. Its open in evening 6pm to 2am. Available dance club bar food restaurant. Also Available shopping market where you can get clothes or other things. Its street market and one of best place for enjoyment in phuket for those who liking drinking etc.

author: Danika Rose
review_text: From a cultural standpoint, great - the locals definitely thrive off the tourism however they must know the word “no” as the pushing gets old, they pester & follow you making you feel obligated to say yes, they also charge Australian prices, if you’re not bartering you’re definitely getting ripped off. The locals less polite here, making you feel very rude for saying no. The toilets are 10baht & you’re rushed, cultural shock for us aussies. They physically drag you away/grab your arm/ follow you for the adult shows, we felt especially bad for the men as the women just wouldn’t stop no matter how many times they said no or try to walk away.. it’s a whole new level of persistent, we saw men physically have to pull the ladies hands off them even if they had girlfriends. Thai ladies would guilt men saying “you no think I’m beautiful” and act sad guilting men. There are also male adult shows however the men aren’t nearly as persistent as the women. We did it once because we’re in Thailand but we will probably never come back to this market

author: Dharmendra Bhudia
review_text: Really tasty food and lots to choose from. Price are good also. A must id your in the area

author: Sandeep Anand
review_text:
This ain't for the the sensitive stomach kind.
You can have the normal seafood here of course.
What I tried are experiences ☺️

Grilled frog and a sea conch.. near the end almost of the market.

It really is true, they taste like chicken.
Disclaimer I don't have a well developed pallet 😂

author: abdul AM
review_text: One of the most important and beautiful activities in Thailand is visiting the night markets and experiencing the food and the wonderful atmosphere.

author: Willie B
review_text:
The night market is pretty awesome! It is a massive maze of food and shops. Pricing is great and its covered as well as can be. Consider it a large flea market if you're from the states.

It is hot so bring your fan and a towel if you're a sweater like me. If you're a germaphobe bring hand sanitizer.

You can haggle on prices here so give them your best offer before you settle on souvenir prices but don't cheat them. They are trying to make some money after all.

author: Morit Lahlali
review_text: The food was meh. Pretty sure we got scammed with a lobster. The one we got was way smaller than the one we bought and weighed. Oh well

author: Wayne Tota
review_text: Im not a nightout person but was buffled at what i saw😂.. noisy stuff, free adverts of everything ..they sell anything..check out all videos on my youtube @drwaynetota. I uploaded them all will upload some here. I only managed to eat Mcdonalds, afraid to be pulled into some bar😂

author: Aditya Raj
review_text: Crowded places, delicious and local dish, must try lobster here and fish here.

author: Ritika
review_text: Loud music and brings lights all over, good to visit when in Phuket. V similar to Pattaya walking street. Thai street food is good, coconut icecream is a must try.
